Students will explore changes in the functions of art museums and will develop practical skills for future museum employment.
catalog.prerequisites: ART-HIST 201 or ART-HIST 202 or ART-HIST 303 , or students pursuing the Museum Studies UGRD CT. Sophomore standing required.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: History of Exhibitions and Curatorial Practice
catalog.description: This course is a study of historically significant international art exhibitions in a global context from the 1850s through the 21st century. Students will examine the production and curation of seminal exhibitions as complex processes marked by particular social, political, economic and cultural forces. Students will gain practical skills by learning how to curate, install an exhibition and develop related programming.
catalog.prerequisites: ART-HIST 201 or ART-HIST 202 , or sophomore standing.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Site-Specific Art: Within and Beyond the Museum Walls
catalog.description: At a time of increased transnational mobility, contemporary artists are conceiving artworks that catalyze an enhanced awareness of the geographical and socio-political conditions of existence and art making. This seminar examines artworks that are produced outside the studio and are inspired by specific natural environments, museum settings and public spaces.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Pompeii and Herculaneum: The Archaeology of the Roman World
catalog.description: This class offers insights into the art, architecture, politics, economics, religions and social life of the Roman world through the study of Pompeii and Herculaneum.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Directed Studies in Art History
catalog.description: With permission of instructor, advanced students pursue independent research and production of a significant semester-long research project. Acceptable for graduate credit with approval.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Special Topics in Art History
catalog.description: In depth exploration of a special topic in Art History. Course may be repeated for up to 18 credit hours if topic is unique for each repeated effort. Acceptable for graduate credit with approval.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Special Studies in Art History: Internship
catalog.description: Advanced art history students gain invaluable practical experience in a professional setting in the field of art.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Scope and Methods of Art History
catalog.description: This course examines the history of the discipline of art history and advances the understanding of diverse methodological approaches and theories. Students will learn to propose a research question and formulate an argument well-supported by research evidence.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Made in the USA: Latinx Art and Experience
catalog.description: This graduate course focuses on art of and by members of the U.S. Latinx community. Students will develop advanced research on the politics of representation, gender, sexuality, race, class, and ethnicity in Latinx art, visual, and popular culture.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Whose America: Modern Art and Philosophy in the Americas
catalog.description: This graduate course focuses on art of the Americas, ca. 1800 to the present. Students will develop advanced research on the art and philosophy of the Americas, especially how art served to challenge colonial paradigms of racism and sexism, while asserting new national and continental identities.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Paris in the Age of Rococo
catalog.description: In the early 18th century, Paris overtook Rome as the artistic center of Europe. We explore all of the visual arts during the vibrant 'Rococo,' the age of Watteau, Chardin, and Boucher.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar in French Art: Renaissance and Baroque
catalog.description: A history of French art from the time of Louis XII through the Age of Louis XIV, with emphasis on painting and architecture.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar in Northern Baroque Art: The Age of Rubens, Rembrandt, and Wren
catalog.description: The arts of England and the Low Countries in the 17th and early 18th centuries. Emphasis on painting and the graphic arts in the Spanish and Dutch Netherlands, and on architecture in England.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar in Italian Baroque Art: The Age of Caravaggio, Bernini, and Borromini
catalog.description: Painting, sculpture, and architecture in Italy from the creation of the Baroque style in the late 16th century to the beginnings of the Barochetto era.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar in Span Art: El Greco to Goya
catalog.description: A study of Spanish art from the later 15th Century to the Napoleonic invasion.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Traditional and Contemporary Native American Art
catalog.description: This course aims to inspire students to appreciate the history and aesthetics of traditional and contemporary Native North American arts. We examine cultural and aesthetic continuities between Meso-American and Native North American Arts. Then we explore how Native American arts reflect the history of North America, including influences from Europeans, and conclude with contemporary Native American artists and their incorporation of various global influences.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: History of Modern Design
catalog.description: This course examines innovations in design, beginning with the Arts and Crafts movement in the 19th century, surveying all the major design trends of the twentieth century, and concluding with contemporary developments in the age of the computer.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Primitivism and Its Aftermath
catalog.description: This course explores one of the seminal movements of the modern era and its ramifications for the visual arts today. Class discussions will consider the complexities and contradictions of primitivism and its rejection through their appropriations from archaic, folk, and non-western art traditions, from 1800-on, while also situation these creative endeavors within the cultural and political contexts of the period.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Modern Art and the Grotesque
catalog.description: The course explores how the grotesque shaped the history, practice and theory of art in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. The grotesque plays a major role in many modern styles, and its expressive possibilities encompass the capriccio, the carnivalesque and burlesque, the fantastic, and the abject and uncanny. Artists have incorporated the grotesque as a means to push beyond established boundaries, explore alternate modes of experience, and to challenge cultural and aesthetic conventions.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In American Art
catalog.description: Graduate-level seminar dealing with an announced area in American art. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In 19th-Century Art
catalog.description: Graduate-level seminar dealing with an announced area in 19th-century art. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In 20th-Century Art
catalog.description: Graduate-level seminar dealing with an announced area in 20th-century art. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Participatory Forms of Spectatorship in Contemporary Art
catalog.description: This course explores art practices from the second half of the 20th century that challenge spectators to become more actively involved in the reception and even in the production of art. The course will examine the sociopolitical conditions and technological developments which have contributed to the strengthening of participatory tendencies in contemporary art.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Sensing, Feeling, Thinking: Contemporary Art and the Mind
catalog.description: Contemporary artists are challenging viewers to reflect on how they perceive, feel and think. This seminar provides an introduction to the mental processes underlying emotion and visual cognition and familiarizes students with contemporary art practices that reveal the dynamic correlations between body, mind and subjectivity.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In Renaissance Art
catalog.description: Graduate-level seminar dealing with an announced area in Renaissance art. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In Art Of Africa, Oceania And New World Cultures
catalog.description: Seminar in art of Africa, oceania and new world cultures. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In Asian Art
catalog.description: Seminar dealing with an announced area in Asian Art. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Visual Arts Administration
catalog.description: This course on professional arts administration includes assignments in: copyright laws, database management, ethics issues, evaluation design, gallery museum management, grant writing and budgeting, public relations, resume design, tax laws, and website design and management. Students are required to learn relevant computer programs. This course is also open to music and theatre majors. Research requirements for graduate credit are more comprehensive and professional.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Seminar In Baroque Art
catalog.description: Graduate-level seminar dealing with an announced area in Baroque art. May be repeated once, provided there is a change in the area of concentration.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Site-Specific Art: Within and Beyond the Museum Walls
catalog.description: At a time of increased transnational mobility, contemporary artists are conceiving artworks that catalyze an enhanced awareness of the geographical and socio-political conditions of existence and art making. This seminar examines artworks that are produced outside the studio and are inspired by specific natural environments, museum settings and public spaces.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Contemporary Artists of the African Diaspora
catalog.description: This course examines cultural and aesthetic continuities between traditional and contemporary arts and artists in Africa and in the Americas, including the study of contemporary Africans whose cultures had the greatest influence in the Americas, as well as contemporary African-American artists in Brazil, Cuba, Haiti, and the United States.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: From the Parthenon to the Altar of Peace
catalog.description: The course centers on the many different styles of Greek and Roman art from the fifth century B.C. to the early first century A.D. Attention is also paid to the political and literary forces behind its imagery. Three monuments serve as the pillars upon which the course rests: the Parthenon, Pergamon Altar, and the Ara Pacis. The lessons learned about style, the interaction of politics, literature, and art and the foibles of scholarship are intended to be applied to other fields of art history.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Art Museums: History and Practice
catalog.description: This course will familiarize students with the history of art museums and collecting practices. It will cover theories of museum government, curating, and object interpretation. Students will explore changes in the functions of art museums and will develop practical skills for future museum employment.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Directed Studies In Art History
catalog.description: Individually directed studies or research in selected topics or problems in art history. May be repeated up to a total of six hours applicable to a degree program.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Research & Thesis
catalog.description: Production and/or writing of thesis. Usually taken in the last term of candidacy.

catalog.subject: ART-HIST
catalog.title: Research And Dissertation
catalog.description: Dissertation Research and writing in Art History.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Astronomy: Motions of the Cosmos
catalog.description: An introductory exploration of modern topics in astronomy with an emphasis on developing conceptual models for the fundamental laws of gravity and motion crucial to the formation of stars and planetary systems, the growth of black holes and galaxies, and the evolution of cosmic structure.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Introductory Astronomy Laboratory
catalog.description: An introductory exploration of astronomical phenomena and concepts through quantitative laboratory activities requiring data collection, analysis and interpretation. This course is open to students from all majors.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Astronomy: Starlight and Star Stuff
catalog.description: An introductory exploration of modern topics in astronomy with an emphasis on developing conceptual models for the interactions between light and matter crucial to the life and death of stars, the analysis of starlight and interstellar chemistry, and the interpretation of cosmic history.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Scientific Research Preparation
catalog.description: Through completion of immersive and structured hands-on learning activities, students gain generalized practical and technical skills that are in demand for STEM (Science-Technology-Engineering-Math) internships and that are needed for dynamic careers in scientific, engineering, and Tech research and development sectors. Students learn transferable data analysis, critical thinking, problem-solving, coding, technical communication, and technological literacy skills through the realistic application of concepts, tools, and methods commonly employed in basic research. No previous experience with computer coding nor research methods is required.
catalog.prerequisites: Physics 210 or 240, or consent of instructor.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Practical Astronomy
catalog.description: A practical overview of the basic methods of observational astronomy research, including the principles of telescopes, detectors and measurement theory.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 ; and MATH 250 or MATH 268 .

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Stellar Astrophysics
catalog.description: A mathematical and conceptual overview of the observed properties of stars and the fundamental astrophysics of radiative transfer, hydrostatic equilibrium, atomic processes and thermonuclear energy production that govern their structure, atmospheres and remnants.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Galaxies
catalog.description: A mathematical and conceptual overview of the observed properties and astrophysics of galaxies highlighting star formation and evolution, the interstellar medium, the Milky Way, galaxy populations and demographics, active galactic nuclei, and galaxy formation and evolution.

catalog.subject: ASTR
catalog.title: Cosmology
catalog.description: This course provides a foundation in both physical and observational cosmology. Students will acquire both a mathematical and conceptual understanding of the formation and dynamics of the Universe.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 ; and MATH 250 or MATH 268 .

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Preparatory Applied Study
catalog.description: One hour weekly lesson. Limited to two semesters study. Jury examination is required. There shall be a jury which shall be for comments only unless the student is applying for entrance to the 101 level, at which time a graded jury is required. May not be taken for credit toward the major.

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Applied Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: Applied study of a second instrument. One-half hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study. No jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Applied Study for the Non-Music Major
catalog.description: Applied study for the non-music major. One half-hour lesson weekly. No jury required.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be a student in the UMKC Conservatory.

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Studio Class
catalog.description: Experiential lab where students gain orientation and experience with pedagogy, literature, and performance.

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Studio Class
catalog.description: Experiential lab where students gain orientation and experience with pedagogy, literature, and performance.

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Special Applied Studies
catalog.description: One-hour lesson weekly. This course is for pedagogical or review purposes. An audition is required, and a jury for comments only may be held at the discretion of the division. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: BASSOON
catalog.title: Applied Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: One half-hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study. No jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Biomaterials Teaching
catalog.description: Through this course, students will acquire teaching experience in graduate and dental student biomaterials.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Growth & Development 1
catalog.description: A course designed to teach the general principles of normal and abnormal physical, psychological and social growth and development of children and adolescents. The growth and development of the craniofacial structures is emphasized.The diagnosis of malocclusions is stressed. Consideration is given to possible approaches to their treatment.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Genetics and Biochemistry of Cranial Facial Biology
catalog.description: Biochemistry of oral structures and the effect of oral diseases on these structures. This course may not be used to satisfy Cell Biology and Biophysics or Molecular Biology and Biochemistry discipline-specific requirements for the Interdisciplinary Ph.D. programs.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Biomaterials for the Dental Specialist
catalog.description: Discussion of basic biomaterials principles and terminology including explanation of physical, mechanical and surface chemical properties, metallurgy, polymer chemistry, ceramics and composites. Clinical examples of how these principles apply to Prosthodontics, Endodontics and Orthodontics will be presented. Students cannot take both this course and BIO-SCI 5742 for credit.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Oral Pathology
catalog.description: A study of the clinical and histopathologic features of oral diseases, including inflammatory, degenerative, metabolic, and neoplastic diseases and developmental disturbances.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Biomaterials for the Restorative and General Dentist
catalog.description: A thorough discussion of basic biomaterials principles and how they apply to the practice of general and restorative dentistry. Students cannot take both this course and BIO-SCI 5739 for credit.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Advanced Seminar in Dental Biomaterials
catalog.description: The use and behavior of dental biomaterials in Pediatric Dentistry, Prosthodontics, Orthodontics, and Restorative Dentistry will be discussed in depth. Current basic and clinical literature related to these areas will be discussed and research information to improve dental practice will be presented.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Research Instrumentation Used in Dental Biomaterials
catalog.description: A discussion and laboratory use of instrumentation employed in dental biomaterials research. Practical hands-on experience will include calibration and use of specific research equipment including the Instron, metallurgical mounting and polishing equipment, measuring microscope, metallograph, and contact angle goniometer.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Special Problems in Dental Biomaterials
catalog.description: The student will select or be assigned a special research problem including appropriate literature reviews of a special topic in dental biomaterials. Emphasis will be placed on the correlation between basic and clinical research. The design and conduct of clinical research will be discussed.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Elements of the Scientific Method
catalog.description: For the MS, through individualized instruction with thesis committee chair, student will conduct a literature review in preparation for developing a research question leading to the thesis research proposal. For the PhD, students will select and rotate through a minimum of four laboratories in the Department of Oral & Craniofacial Sciences (OCS) conducting a short research project in each. At the end of the semester, a report is required reviewing the research project and the instrumentation in each laboratory. Students are also required to attend the weekly Department of OCS Seminar Series and the monthly Professional Development Seminar Series. Research presentations cover a variety of biological, engineering and psychological disciplines relevant to oral science education and the oral health care profession. Presentations will be by faculty, students, and invited guest lecturers.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Research Methods in Oral and Craniofacial Sciences
catalog.description: MS students will write the thesis research proposal in consultation with committee chair and members plus obtain appropriate IRB and/or IACUC approvals. For the MS degree qualifying exam, the student will write the research proposal, present the research proposal at a committee meeting, and answer related questions. Following the successful completion of the qualifying exam, the research proposal is the basis of the MS thesis project. For the PhD student, laboratory rotations will continue for a second semester as well as attendance at weekly OCS seminar series. As the student identifies a research advisor and research focus for the dissertation project, they will begin reviewing the literature.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Special Problems in Pharmacology
catalog.description: Pharmacologic and therapeutic problems of special interest in the practice of dentistry.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Physiology of Oral Mineralized Tissues
catalog.description: A study of the physiology of the oral hard tissues with emphasis on the mechanisms of the growth, remodeling, and healing of maxillomandibular bones and on the mechanism of dentinogenesis. This course may not be used to satisfy Cell Biology and Biophysics or Molecular Biology and Biochemistry discipline-specific requirements for the Interdisciplinary Ph.D. program.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Teaching Of Dentistry
catalog.description: A consideration of the problems of teaching in dental schools. Each department of the School of Dentistry will report on its teaching methods. The student will observe lectures and laboratory teaching in each department.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Directed Research In Oral and Craniofacial Sciences
catalog.description: Student utilizes beginning research skills to design, conduct and report an individual research project under the direction of the faculty.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Research And Thesis
catalog.description: The satisfactory completion of an original research project. Results of the research and critical review of the pertinent literature are incorporated into a thesis. Credit is awarded after the student's thesis is successfully defended and accepted by the School of Graduate Studies.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Immunopathology
catalog.description: A detailed study of selected topics in immunopathology with emphasis on physicochemical barriers such as cutaneous and mucosal immune systems.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Molecular Biology of Oral Microflora
catalog.description: Lecture and discussion. The course will provide an overview of the ecology of oral microbial flora and its role in oral health and disease. Students will examine the taxonomy and ecology of normal and pathogenic oral microbial flora, acquisition of the oral microbiota and the formation of dental plaque as a biofilm. The course will also explore other aspects of microbial biology, such as; bacterial virulence factors and pathogenesis; host defense mechanisms; systemic complications of periodontal disease; antibiotics and antibiotic resistance. The second part of the course will review the effect of recent advances in molecular biology and protein biochemistry on oral diagnosis and treatment.

catalog.subject: BIO-SCI
catalog.title: Structural Characterization of Dental Biomaterials
catalog.description: A detailed study of the techniques commonly used to determine the composition and structure of dental biomaterials. Surface and near-surface characterization techniques will be emphasized. The student will be expected to complete laboratory projects on the scanning and transmission electron microscopies available in the School of Dentistry.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biology and Living
catalog.description: Introduction to structural organization and functional processes of living systems. For non-biology majors only. Does not count toward biology degree.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biology and Living Laboratory
catalog.description: Exploration of basic biological concepts through laboratory activities requiring data collection and analysis. For non-majors only; does not count toward Biology degree requirements.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: General Biology I
catalog.description: Fundamental studies in biology emphasizing the unity and diversity of life. Topics include the basic chemistry of biological processes, cell types and organelles, energy harvesting and energy producing pathways, cell and life cycles, genetics, DNA structure, genes, transcription, translation, natural selection, population genetics, speciation, and phylogenetic analysis.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: General Biology I Laboratory
catalog.description: Basic laboratory studies in Biology emphasizing the unity and diversity of life. Structure, function, heredity, development, ecology and evolution will be explored.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: General Biology II
catalog.description: Fundamental studies in biology emphasizing the unity and diversity of life. Topics include prokaryotes, fungi, invertebrate-vertebrate zoology and phylogeny, human evolution, plant structure and development, animal development and physiology, ecology (population and ecosystems).

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: General Biology II Laboratory
catalog.description: Basic laboratory studies in Biology emphasizing the unity and diversity of life. Structure, function, heredity, development, regulation of growth and evolution will be explored.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Microbiology and Living
catalog.description: Lectures and demonstrations concerning the cell structure, genetics and physiology of microorganisms and the role microorganisms play in the world around man with an emphasis on medical and clinical aspects of the significance of various groups of bacteria, viruses fungi and other microorganisms. This course is intended for nursing and other allied health students and for non-biology majors interested in life sciences and does not count toward Biology major requirements.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: First Year Seminar
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide students with the skills necessary to achieve success at the university. The curriculum includes time management, study, reading, note-taking and test-taking strategies, health and wellness, and student support services. Additional emphasis will include career exploration, including professionalism, writing a resume, and developing plan of study for degree completion.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Human Genetics
catalog.description: This is a non-majors biology course in human genetics designed for those with little classroom training in the sciences. The focus will be on the nature of human genetic variation and how variation shapes and affects our lives. This includes the structure and function of genes and how genes create traits. The discussion will focus on how genes function in human development through sex determination. The inclusion of human genomic sequencing technology and personal genomics will emphasize several issues related to knowledge and privacy.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Guided Research in Biology
catalog.description: An introduction to basic principles and methods of scientific research in the biological sciences. Students will engage in experimental design, use of bioinformatic tools, molecular graphics, and specialized tools related to different biology disciplines to characterize a specific gene or cell system under the guidance of a faculty member. Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 108 .

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Methods in Biological Research
catalog.description: The course will provide an introduction to laboratory safety and common research methods used in modern biological research. It is intended for students that wish to gain research experience in the School or a career in research.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Cell Biology
catalog.description: Basic concepts of cellular and subcellular structure and function, including supramolecular and organelle structure and organization, bioenergetics, cell growth and cellular communication.
catalog.prerequisites: ( BIOLOGY 108 (or MOTRBIOL 150L), and CHEM 212R ) OR ( CHEM 212R , LS-ANATO 219 , LS-ANATO 219L , and LS-MCRB 121 ).

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Genetics
catalog.description: A modern approach integrating molecular and organismal studies of the general genetics of lower and higher organisms. Chromosomal structure and function, gene transmission, heredity, plasticity and population genetics will be discussed.
catalog.prerequisites: BIOLOGY 108 (or MOTRBIOL 150L), BIOLOGY 109 (or MOTRBIOL 150LZ or MOTRBIOL 100LZ ), and CHEM 212R or LS-ANATO 219 .

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Human Physiology Laboratory
catalog.description: This course is designed to illustrate the important principles of human physiology in a laboratory setting. Using an organ systems approach, the course will feature microscopic work, audio-visual presentations, and student experiments when possible. For non-majors only; does not count toward biology degree requirements.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Introductory Anatomy
catalog.description: Description and discussion of the cells, organs, organ systems and basic tissues of vertebrates with special emphasis on their interrelationships in functional anatomy.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Introductory Anatomy Laboratory
catalog.description: Laboratory investigation of cells, tissues, and organs with special emphasis on their interrelationship in vertebrates.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Careers in Biological & Chemical Sciences I
catalog.description: This course will introduce students to a variety of careers in the biological and chemical sciences. Guest speakers will share information including day-to-day activities on the job, educational requirements, career advancement, and necessary interests and abilities.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Careers in Biological & Chemical Sciences II
catalog.description: This course will help students prepare for their post-undergraduate future. Topics will include communication, skills identification and marketing, how to find employment or internship opportunities, a review of the application process for graduate education and the role of undergraduate research.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: In depth exploration of a topic in biology

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: General Ecology
catalog.description: Introduction to the study of populations, communities, and ecosystems by examining the interrelationships between living organisms and their environments. The role of natural selection and evolution will also be considered. Prerequisites: BIOLOGY 108 (MOTR 150L), BIOLOGY 109 (MOTR 150LZ), or BIOLOGY 102 (MOTR 100L).

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Ecology Laboratory
catalog.description: This course provides laboratory and field experience in ecology. The course will cover topics including statistical analysis and data presentation, terrestrial and aquatic sampling, experimental design and scientific writing.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Invertebrate Zoology
catalog.description: Taxonomy, evolutionary relationships, behavior, reproduction, morphology and ecology of the invertebrates. Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 108 , BIOLOGY 109 , and CHEM 212R .

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biostatistics 1
catalog.description: Introduction to the concepts of probability, statistical reasoning, and experimental design in the biological sciences. The course emphasizes the application of inferential statistics to biological experiments including the use of relevant statistical computer packages.
catalog.prerequisites: MATH 110 or STAT 235 ; or ACT Math sub-score of 28 or higher; or SAT Math sub-score of 660 or higher; or MyMathTest College Algebra score of 70% or higher.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Marine and Freshwater Biology
catalog.description: Introduction to the study of marine ecology, deep-sea biology, oceanic nekton, inter-tidal ecology, estuaries, mangroves and salt marshes, as well as ecology of rivers, lakes, streams, wetlands and human impact on aquatic habitats.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: From Bench to Bedside: Translational Research
catalog.description: This course explores the interplay between basic biological research and bedside clinical practice, delving into the topic “what is translational research?” By engaging with people from the community involved at all levels of translational research, students will gain an appreciation for the civic issues behind medical research, the interdisciplinary nature of research, and the part that Kansas City institutions play in regional life and health sciences.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Vertebrate Zoology
catalog.description: Taxonomy, evolutionary relationships, behavior, reproduction, morphology and ecology of the vertebrates.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Herpetology
catalog.description: The study of amphibians and reptiles, focusing on physiology, ecology, and taxonomy.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Genetics and Developmental Biology
catalog.description: Experimental studies in the genetics, development, and cell biology using eukaryotic model systems with an emphasis on the basic methods of molecular and cellular biology.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Developmental Biology, Genetics and Cell Biology
catalog.description: Experimental studies of genetics and development in selected eukaryotic model organisms with an emphasis on the molecular and cellular mechanism of inheritance.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Microbiology
catalog.description: Fundamental and applied aspects of microbial structure, metabolism, genetics and diversity. Experimental approaches to studying the microbial world will be emphasized.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Microbiology
catalog.description: General microbiological procedures plus advanced work in the areas of microbial physiology and genetics, pathogenic microbiology, virology, applied microbiology and biotechnology.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Microbiology
catalog.description: General microbiological procedures plus advanced work in the areas of microbial physiology and genetics, pathogenic microbiology, virology, applied microbiology, and biotechnology.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Entomology
catalog.description: Anatomy, physiology and identification of insects with emphasis on their environmental adaptations.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Principles of Physiology
catalog.description: Physiological functions and processes of animals at the organ and organ systems levels, including concepts of integrated and homeostatic mechanisms. The relationship between organ function and underlying cellular mechanisms in vertebrates will be emphasized.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Principles Of Physiology Laboratory
catalog.description: This course is designed to illustrate the important principles of human physiology in a laboratory setting. Using an organ systems approach, the course will feature audio-visual presentations and student experiments both during and outside the lab period.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Global Health: New and Emerging Infectious Diseases
catalog.description: This course will discuss infectious diseases that are newly identified, or increasing in prevalence throughout the world. Several aspects of each disease will be discussed, including transmission, symptoms, treatment, prevention, and diagnosis. The course is meant for students interested in a health-related career (medicine, dental, pharmacy, public health), but other students with a basic biology background are welcome.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: General Parasitology
catalog.description: Parasitic protists, worms and arthropods and the disease states they may induce, will be examined in relationship to human, animal and plants hosts.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biological Conservation
catalog.description: Applications of ecology and genetics to the conservation of communities and individual species, including discussion of the Endangered Species Act, extinction processes, and the effects of habitat fragmentation.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biogeography and Biodiversity
catalog.description: Evolutionary and climatological effects on the geographic distribution of organisms, including areas of endemism as well as preservation of biodiversity.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Histology
catalog.description: Animal tissues and their specialization in the organism, with major emphasis on higher organisms.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Histology and Cellular Ultrastructure
catalog.description: Examination of structure/function relationships at the subcellular, cellular and organ levels. Both plants and animals will be examined with emphasis on vertebrates.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Histology and Cellular Ultrastructure
catalog.description: Examination of structure/function relationships at the subcellular, cellular and organ levels. Both plants and animals will be examined with emphasis on vertebrates.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Endocrinology
catalog.description: Study of the physiological functions and controls in human and related mammalian systems, with emphasis on endocrine-directed processes that underlie normal and abnormal metabolic and clinical conditions. The course will be presented in traditional lecture format, and focus on the molecular, chemical, membrane and cellular basis of metabolic homeostatic processes in cells, cytoplasmic compartments and primary organ systems.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Reproductive Biology
catalog.description: Comprehensive overview of current concepts and knowledge regarding male and female reproductive processes, from gametogenesis through early placentation. Includes structural, developmental, physiological and pathophysiological aspects of reproduction.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Invasive Species
catalog.description: Students will study the biological traits that contribute to successful invasions, the ecological and economic impacts of invasive species, and the legal and cultural responses to invasions. Students will develop critical analysis and communication skills by analyzing scientific literature, discussing implications, and presenting arguments in written and oral platforms.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy Laboratory
catalog.description: This class explores anatomical similarities and differences that exist between the major vertebrate groups and relates aspects of anatomy to evolutionary history and function. Students will gain hands-on experience of anatomy through dissection and examination of several model vertebrates. Recommended preparation: BIOLOGY 108 , BIOLOGY 109 , and BIOLOGY 109L .

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Introduction to Mycology
catalog.description: The study of fungi, focusing on taxonomy, life history, ecology, medical significance, and industrial applications.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Plant Biology
catalog.description: An integrative study of growth, development, and reproduction of plants, including structure and function of plant tissues and organs, as well as a survey of the recent advances in genetic engineering, plant defense mechanisms, and medical botany and the usefulness of plants to humans.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Assisting Undergraduate Learning in Biology
catalog.description: This course addresses current issues and pedagogy of teaching biology and providing instructional support for designated undergraduate courses in Biological Sciences. Students meet weekly with the course instructor and assist in the classroom, studio, or laboratory.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Molecular Biology Research Methods
catalog.description: Laboratory studies in biochemistry and molecular biology with an emphasis on modern techniques and quantitative relationships.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Cell Biology Research Methods
catalog.description: This project-based learning course will instruct students on how to employ the scientific method to address biological questions. Students will make observations, propose hypotheses, design and conduct experiments, analyze data, and report conclusions. Additionally, this course will instruct students on the proper usage and maintenance of equipment commonly utilized in research, medical labs, and life sciences industries.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: In depth exploration of a topic in biology. Repeatable toward the major only when the topic changes.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Experience Based Education
catalog.description: This course will allow students to earn credit for experience gained through educational experiences such as service, shadowing, leadership, employment and study abroad.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biostatistics 2
catalog.description: An advanced study of inferential statistics. The course will introduce correlation, linear and categorical regression, and emphasize model selection and multi-model inference. The use of statistical computer software also will be emphasized.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Introduction to Evolution
catalog.description: Discussion of the biological processes that produce organic diversity through phyletic change, including variation, mutation, adaptation, population genetics, natural selection, genetic drift, gene flow, and macroevolution.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Developmental Biology
catalog.description: Principles of development and differentiation of structure during embryology in animals. Molecular, cellular and organismal level concepts and mechanisms will be considered.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Pathophysiology
catalog.description: Pathophysiology will focus on the physiological basis of cellular and tissue function, and the consequences of dysregulated metabolic/cellular expression on essential homeostatic processes in cells, cytoplasmic compartments and primary organ systems.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Molecular Biology and Genetic Engineering
catalog.description: Molecular aspects of gene structure and function, including macromolecular synthesis, gene regulation, genetic transfer and biotechnology will be discussed in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Virology
catalog.description: Survey of the molecular biology of animal, plant, and bacterial viruses. The course will emphasize the molecular mechanisms of virus replication, viral pathogenesis, and the use of virus as model systems to study mammalian cells.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Immunology
catalog.description: A study of the cellular and humoral aspects of the immune response, with emphasis upon the mechanisms involved and the relationship of this response to disease processes.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Biochemistry
catalog.description: One semester course covering the properties of organic compounds important to biological systems. Structures, characterization and reactions of common compounds and their relationship to the building blocks of biological systems will be discussed.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Neurobiology
catalog.description: Neurobiology will consist of the presentation of theory and data concerning cellular and molecular fundamentals of the nervous system, synaptic mechanisms, sensory-motor systems, and higher-order functions of the nervous system.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Evolutionary Ecology
catalog.description: This class explores the scientific concepts and methods underpinning modern understanding of evolutionary ecology as it relates to organisms. Students will gain hands-on experience using techniques that are central to quantitative and qualitative studies of organismal evolutionary ecology.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Foundations of Bioinformatics
catalog.description: Study of the acquisition, storage, retrieval, analysis, modeling, and distribution of information in biomolecular databases. Recent developments in genomics and proteomics and how these databases are used in modern biological research will be emphasized.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: In depth exploration of a topic in biology. Repeatable toward the major only when the topic changes.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Laboratory in Advanced Environmental Microbiology
catalog.description: The course will explore the diversity of soil microbes in the KC area, investigate the ecology of soil microbes and their involvement in nutrient cycles, attempt to culture soil microbes in the lab, and investigate production of natural antibiotics in soil microbiota.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Critical Analysis of Biological Issues
catalog.description: Reading and analysis of scientific literature, including original papers, on a topic of broad biological interest. Critical discussion of experimental methods and results. Writing of scientific reviews and a term paper.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Human Physiology I
catalog.description: BIOL 5399 is an introduction to integrated physiology of the human body, beginning with an emphasis on understanding the foundations of physiologic principles followed by an in-depth study of the physiology of the nervous, endocrine, and muscle systems.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Proposal Writing
catalog.description: This course addresses how to develop a testable hypothesis, and write a NIH-style proposal to convince the reader of the significance of the proposed studies. Students will write a proposal that will form the basis of their oral comprehensive exam in the Cell Biology and Biophysics (CBB) and Molecular Biology and Biochemistry (MBB) disciplines. The is limited to doctoral students with CBB and MBB coordinating disciplines that have a plan of study filed with the School of Graduate Studies.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Gross Anatomy for Nurse Anesthetists
catalog.description: This course will present and examine the anatomic concepts and conditions essential for critical thinking and decision making by the nurse anesthetist. Specifically, the course will provide the foundation upon which patient interventions may be based during the perioperative period.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Gross Anatomy for Nurse Anesthetists
catalog.description: This laboratory course will present and examine the anatomic concepts and conditions essential for critical thinking and decision making by the nurse anesthetist. Specifically, the course will provide the foundation upon which patient intervention may be based during the perioperative period.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Professional Development
catalog.description: The purpose of this course is to facilitate a competitive application to professional health programs for students seeking the M.A. in Biology. Students will gain an understanding of the application process, including decisions about where to apply, assessing fit, developing a personal statement, strategies for letters of evaluation, and the execution of a successful interview.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the M.A. Biology program, or by instructor consent.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Graduate Cell Biology
catalog.description: This course will provide graduate-level students a foundation in the basic principles of cellular biology, focusing on the internal organization and regulation of the cell, cell function within tissues and organisms, and basic molecular genetic mechanisms with additional special topics relevant to human health and disease.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Graduate Biostatistics 1
catalog.description: A first course in probability, sampling, and experimental design. The course will introduce inferential statistics testing for differences in means and their relevance to the biological sciences.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Global Health: New and Emerging Infections Diseases
catalog.description: This course will discuss infectious diseases that are newly identified, or increasing in prevalence throughout the world. Several aspects of each disease will be discussed, including transmission, symptoms, treatment, prevention, and diagnosis. The course is meant for students interested in a health-related career (medicine, dental, pharmacy, public health), but other students with a basic biology background are welcome.
catalog.prerequisites: BA or BS in Biology or related field

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: From Bench to Bedside: Translational Research
catalog.description: This course explores the pipeline from basic biological research to bedside clinical practice, delving into the topic “what is translational research?” By engaging with people from the community involved at all levels of translational research, students will gain an appreciation for the civic issues behind medical research, the interdisciplinary nature of research, and the part that Kansas City institutions play in regional life and health sciences. As a graduate course, students will be asked to use critical thinking in each step of the drug-development pipeline.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be in a graduate program in Biology or instructor consent.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Graduate Histology
catalog.description: Animal tissues and their specialization in the organism, with major emphasis on higher organisms.
catalog.prerequisites: BA or BS in Biology or Chemistry, or permission of the instructor.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Principles of Evolution
catalog.description: Synthesis of the modern concepts of evolution. Discussion of the biological processes that produce organic diversity through phyletic change. Discussed are variation, mutation, population genetics, natural selection and adaptation.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Foundations of Bioinformatics and Data Analysis
catalog.description: Methods and procedures for the storage, retrieval and analysis of information in biomolecular and biological databases. Emphasis will be given to the use of database information in biological research and to recent developments in genomics and proteomics.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Human Genomic Epidemiology
catalog.description: This course is designed for biological researchers and clinicians interested in studying common human diseases using state-of-the-art genomics/genetics epidemiological approaches. The course provides a basic yet comprehensive introduction to key topics in human genome epidemiological research, including basic concepts and methodologies of quantitative/statistical genetics, an introduction to emerging technologies and analytical methods for genomic science, basic study for various types of genomic research approaches, utilization of widely-used software packages for analyses of genomic data, and examples of human genome epidemiology information improving health, and ethical, legal and social issues in the design and conduct of human genome epidemiology studies.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Mammalian Physiology
catalog.description: Study of the physiological functions and controls in human and related mammalian systems, with emphasis on fundamental processes that underlie normal and abnormal clinical conditions.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Pathophysiology
catalog.description: Pathophysiology will focus on the physiological basis of cellular and tissue function, and the consequences of dysregulated metabolic/cellular expression on essential homeostatic processes in cells, cytoplasmic compartments and primary organ systems.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Neurobiology
catalog.description: Neurobiology will consist of the presentation of theory and data concerning cellular and molecular fundamentals of the nervous system, synaptic mechanisms, sensor-motor systems, and higher-order functions of the nervous system.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Professional Skills for Scientists
catalog.description: A one semester course for graduate students in the biomedical sciences covering professional skills necessary for effective interpersonal interaction, communication, and career development. This course incorporates lectures, discussions, and practical components on diverse soft skills topics, such as responsible conduct of research, ethics, conflict management, time management, negotiation, career planning, and leadership. Written and oral communication is emphasized in the context of scientific publishing, conferences, funding applications, and peer review.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be a biology graduate student or instructor consent.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Directed Individual Studies
catalog.description: Intensive readings and/or research in an area selected by the graduate student in consultation with the instructor. Not to be identified with thesis research.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Master of Arts Topics in Biology
catalog.description: Special problems and topics in biology specifically intended to satisfy the project or report requirement for the master of arts degree in biology.
catalog.prerequisites: Nine hours of graduate work in Biology.

catalog.subject: BIOLOGY
catalog.title: Master of Science Topics
catalog.description: Investigation of problems and topics to satisfy the M.S. topics requirement for the Master of Science degree in Cellular and Molecular Biology.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
catalog.description: As an introduction to Biomedical Engineering, the following topics will be covered in the course: Biomechanics, Biomedical Devices, Biomedical Computation & Modeling, Biomaterials, Bioelectronics, Bioimaging, and Biomedical Signal Processing.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: 3D Modeling and Printing
catalog.description: Using current computer aided design tools, 3D modeling and printing for Biomedical Engineering applications are introduced.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Biomedical Instrumentation
catalog.description: The purpose of this course is to provide an opportunity for students to gain a hands-on, in-depth understanding of biomedical instrumentation including: electrophysiology, biomechanics, and medical imaging. To prepare for these topics, an introduction to measurements and instrumentation as well as a review of data sampling and signal processing theory will be provided.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Biomedical Systems Physiology
catalog.description: As the advanced human physiology course for biomedical engineering majors, the following systems will be examined: nervous, cellular, musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, gastrointestinal, and renal. Mathematical models and engineering analyses will be used to describe system performance, where applicable, with an emphasis placed on topics relating biomedical engineering to medical diagnostic and therapeutic applications.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Biomedical Transport Phenomena
catalog.description: Principles of momentum and mass transfer with applications to biomedical systems is the focus of this course. The topics covered will include convection, diffusion, osmosis, conservation of momentum, mass and energy as applied to cellular and organ level transport. A special emphasis will be placed on basic fluid transport related to blood flow, and mass transfer across cell membranes.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Polymers in Biomedical Engineering
catalog.description: This course offers students knowledge about common polymers with a focus on biomedical applications from the fundamentals of polymer physics and polymer chemistry. It will give students a solid foundation in polymeric biomaterial design, synthesis, characterization, process, and applications. Topics covered may include the introduction of polymers in daily life, the theory of polymer chemistry and physics, common synthetic and natural polymers, cell/tissue-biomaterials interaction, biomedical applications of polymeric biomaterials, polymer characterization techniques, and molecular weight measurement and calculation.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Bioelectromagnetics and Bioelectricity
catalog.description: As an introduction to the fields of Bioelectromagnetics and Bioelectricity, this course will cover the interaction between biological tissue and externally incident electromagnetic waves with frequencies that range from DC all the way to the visible range and higher as well as the intrinsically generated electrical signals by biology cells and tissues.

catalog.subject: BMD-ENGR
catalog.title: Biomedical Capstone Design
catalog.description: As the capstone design course for Biomedical Engineering majors, this course will cover modern design theories and methodologies, with an emphasis on the initial stages of the design process, effect of design choices on the earth and living systems, and the principles of embodiment design and the life-cycle considerations.
catalog.prerequisites: Senior Standing, BMD-ENGR 215 , BMD-ENGR 315 , MEC-ENGR 492 , and ENGLISH 225 .

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Cadaver-Based Anatomy I
catalog.description: This course combines lectures with hands on cadaveric-based dissection to foster a deeper understanding of structure, function and spatial relationships of human anatomy. It covers introductory principles of the following systems: musculoskeletal, integumentary, lymphatics, cardiovascular, nervous, and respiratory. In addition, this course covers fundamental concepts regarding structure, function and anatomical relationships of the extremities, thoracic cage and contents of the thorax.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Cadaver-Based Anatomy II
catalog.description: This course combines lectures with hands on cadaveric-based dissection to foster a deeper understanding of structure, function and spatial relationships of human anatomy. This course covers introductory principles of the following systems: gastrointestinal, accessory digestive, endocrine, urogenital, nervous and special sensory. In addition, this course covers fundamental concepts regarding structure, function and anatomical relationships of the abdominopelvic cavity, and contents of the head and neck. A passing grade in an undergraduate anatomy course is recommended preparation to Cadaver-Based Anatomy II-BMS 5502.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Medical and Emergency Management in Rural Disaster Response
catalog.description: This course is designed to equip students with the knowledge and practical skills necessary to manage medical emergencies and disaster response in rural communities. Combining principles of emergency management, public health, and medical operations, the course emphasizes the unique challenges faced by rural areas during disasters such as pandemics, severe weather, and active shooter incidents.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Rural Medical Workforce Development
catalog.description: This course provides hands-on training and theoretical knowledge aimed at developing essential healthcare skills for individuals interested in contributing to rural community health. Through a combination of classroom instruction and practical exercises, students will learn life-saving techniques such as Basic Life Support (BLS) and "Stop the Bleed," as well as foundational healthcare concepts relevant to rural settings.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Field Experience in Disaster Medical Operations
catalog.description: This course involves an immersive three-day hands-on experience in a large-scale simulated disaster exercise. The course requires asynchronous online training and pre-work. In addition, students must commit to 72 hours of field work in assumed roles as civilian medical providers, operating within their designated scope of practice. Coached by professional responders and staff experienced with disaster exercises, students will gain experience with team dynamics, patient tracking, and transport methodologies, while practicing basic and advanced medical interventions on simulated patients.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Introduction to Medical Research
catalog.description: This course familiarizes students with the common laboratory and clinical research methodologies utilized for medical research and improves comprehension of scientific research literature. The course includes lecture and a lab-based component. Students learn how to perform common molecular and cellular biology techniques and maintain a laboratory notebook. Through computer-based activities, students learn the fundamentals of clinical database structure, clinical research study designs, and extracting patient data from the electronic health record (EHR) for research. Data analysis methods are covered for analyzing experimental and clinical datasets, including statistical analyses.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Independent Study
catalog.description: Focused area of study selected by a graduate student enrolled in the MA Biology - Rural Medicine emphasis and approved by the instructor. The focus may include a special research project, focused readings, or intensive study preparation for a medical program admittance test.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Medical Physiology
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide an understanding of basic neurophysiology, with a focus on the autonomic nervous system, including muscle, blood, respiratory and cardiovascular physiology.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: An opportunity to explore in depth topics not included in usual course offerings.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Independent Research
catalog.description: Focused area of research selected by a graduate student enrolled in the MA Biology - Rural Medicine emphasis and approved by the instructor.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Capstone Research
catalog.description: The Capstone Research is a final project in which students will apply their research skills to independently develop and implement a research study that addresses a relevant topic in healthcare or the field of medicine. Students will utilize their knowledge of laboratory techniques, clinical research methodologies and statistical analysis to perform the study and analyze the results. The study will culminate in the form of a traditional written research paper and an oral presentation containing the study background, findings and implications for the field.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Biochemistry 1 - Medical
catalog.description: Presents basic principles of human biochemistry. Addresses structure, function, biosynthesis, degradation and utilization of the major constituents of living systems. Employs an integrative approach to the basic science and clinical medicine aspects of normal and defective metabolism.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Structure Function I
catalog.description: Part 1 of a 4 part series (January-February). Integrated course in anatomy, histology, embryology, physiology and biochemistry. This unit covers introductory principles and the musculoskeletal system.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Structure Function II
catalog.description: This course in the Human Structure Function series specifically covers blood, autonomic, pulmonary, and cardiovascular systems. It is sequenced so that a single organ system may be examined from five disciplines (anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, and embryology). The Human Structure Function series provides a foundation in basic science and clinical medicine that when combined with the next series of courses in the curriculum (Neuroscience, Pathology, Microbiology, and Pharmacology) will prepare students to become a well-informed clinician capable of solving problems in human biology and health.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Structure Function III
catalog.description: The Human Structure Function III course is the sequel to Human Structure Function II and a prequel to Human Structure Function IV. It is an integrated, team-taught approach to studying the human body. This is achieved by sequencing lectures so that a single organ system is viewed from five disciplines (anatomy, biochemistry, embryology, histology, and physiology) in the same time frame. Human Structure Function III will address the GI, endocrine, and reproductive systems and build upon the foundations established in HSF-I and HSF-II.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Gross Anatomy I
catalog.description: Regional study of the anatomy of the back, upper limbs, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis with emphasis on the biomedical applications of the anatomy studied.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Gross Anatomy II
catalog.description: A continuation of BMS 9300 . A systematic and regional study of the anatomy of the maxillofacial and anterior neck structures with emphasis on the biomedical applications of the anatomy studied.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Anatomy of the Head & Neck
catalog.description: A regional approach to the study of the head and neck. Content will include a brief discussion of human anatomy and didactic information on the structures of the head and neck as they relate to the practice of dental hygiene.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Histology
catalog.description: A motivative microanatomic study of the normal morphology of cells, tissues, organs and organ systems to stimulate the learning of terminology and basic cellular structure of the human body.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Medical Neurosciences
catalog.description: Lecture-based course covering major neurological disorders and disease states. Specific neurologic diseases will be correlated to the didactic sessions by clinicians. Laboratory component is oriented around brain dissection sessions. Laboratory experience will demonstrate gross lesions and integrate the lesions with the clinical symptoms. A variety of supplemental audiovisual material also supports the class.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Medical Microbiology
catalog.description: Medical Microbiology begins with a review of the basic scientific principles in virology, bacteriology, mycology, and parasitology. The subsequent portion of the course shifts focus to pathogenesis, epidemiology, and the clinical presentation of human infections. This includes a review of antimicrobial therapeutic regimens including mechanisms of action and clinical settings in which specific agents may be used. Case studies are provided throughout the course to enhance critical thinking, to practice developing reasonable differential diagnoses, and to encourage a rational approach toward management with antimicrobial stewardship.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Human Structure Function IV
catalog.description: Part 4 of a 4 part series (June-July). Integrated course in anatomy, histology, embryology, physiology and biochemistry. This unit covers the head and neck system.

catalog.subject: BMS
catalog.title: Clinical Anatomy of Head and Neck
catalog.description: This is an Advanced Head and Neck Anatomy course with an emphasis on clinical implications of anatomy. The emphasis of the course is not to maximize the number of facts the resident knows but rather to help the resident to understand a three-dimensional model that serves as the foundation to help them avoid treatment complications, recognize and treat pathology as well as effectively communicate oral and dental health issues to patients and colleagues.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Preparatory Applied Study
catalog.description: One hour weekly lesson. Limited to two semesters study. Jury examination is required. There shall be a jury which shall be for comments only unless the student is applying for entrance to the 101 level, at which time a graded jury is required. May not be taken for credit toward the major.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Applied Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: Applied study of a second instrument. One half-hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study. No jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Applied Study for the Non-Music Major
catalog.description: Applied study for the non-music major. One half-hour lesson weekly. No jury required.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be a student in the UMKC Conservatory.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Studio Class
catalog.description: Experiential lab where students gain orientation and experience with pedagogy, literature, and performance.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Instrumental Excerpts
catalog.description: Intended to introduce students to the standard instrumental repertoire for orchestra and chamber ensemble; class meets once weekly for an hour. Students will be expected to prepare and play selected ensemble excerpts.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Studio Class
catalog.description: Experiential lab where students gain orientation and experience with pedagogy, literature, and performance.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Instrumental Excerpts
catalog.description: Intended to introduce students to the standard instrumental repertoire for orchestra and chamber ensemble; class meets once weekly for an hour. Students will be expected to prepare and play selected ensemble excerpts.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Special Applied Studies
catalog.description: One-hour lesson weekly. This course is for pedagogical or review purposes. An audition is required, and a jury for comments only may be held at the discretion of the division. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CELLO
catalog.title: Applied Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: One half-hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study. No jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Physical Basis Of Chemistry
catalog.description: An introductory course in the basic principles applicable to chemistry for students who intend to take but are not adequately prepared to take CHEM 211 . The emphasis is on quantitative relationships and problem solving. NOTE: This course does not count towards a Chemistry major or minor.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Elements Of Chemistry I
catalog.description: A one-term course in general chemistry with special emphasis on organic chemistry and biochemistry. A terminal course that does not meet requirements as a prerequisite for any higher level chemistry course. NOTE: This course does not count towards a Chemistry major or minor.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Elements Of Chemistry, Laboratory I
catalog.description: A one-term course in general chemistry with special emphasis on organic chemistry and biochemistry. A terminal course that does not meet requirements as a prerequisite for any higher level chemistry course. NOTE: This course does not count towards a Chemistry major or minor.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Chemistry, Society, And The Environment
catalog.description: This course is intended to offer a survey of chemical and scientific concepts surrounding current issues. The emphasis will be on the application of fundamental chemical knowledge to allow a full understanding of these issues in the context of currently known facts and theories. Through classroom discussion and application of the scientific method, the ramifications of the issues will be examined. Topics will include pollution, the importance of the chemical industry, its responsibilities to society, and other items of current scientific and environmental interest. NOTE: This course does not count towards a Chemistry major or minor.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Laboratory For Chemistry, Society, And The Environment
catalog.description: This course is offered in support of CHEM 160 . It will consist of field activities, experiments, and demonstrations to reinforce the concepts and ideas presented in that course. NOTE: This course does not count towards a Chemistry major or minor.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Human Nutrition
catalog.description: Introduction to nutrition for health and wellness and the use of chemical energy in the breakdown and synthesis of biomolecules. Nutrition as it applies to a variety of life situations from infancy to older adults. Learning encompasses elements of anatomy and physiology related to nutrition and health. NOTE: This course does not count towards a Chemistry major or minor.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: General Chemistry I
catalog.description: Stoichiometry, gas laws, thermochemistry, atomic structure, molecular shapes and bonding theories. Recommended preparation: working knowledge of College Algebra.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Experimental General Chemistry I
catalog.description: Introduction to the laboratory techniques used in studying the chemical properties of substances. Some quantitative techniques are included.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Experimental General Chemistry II
catalog.description: Introduction to analysis and synthesis. Descriptive chemistry of the more common elements.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 211 and CHEM 211L (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: General Chemistry II
catalog.description: Liquids and solids, solutions, equilibrium, kinetics, electrochemistry and thermodynamics. Introductory course to all advanced work in chemistry.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 211 and CHEM 211L (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Laboratory Safety And Health I
catalog.description: An introduction to laboratory safety and health. Topics to be discussed include good laboratory practice; laboratory hazards; safe chemical handling, storage and disposal; first aid; protective equipment; and federal regulations.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Elementary Organic Chemistry
catalog.description: This one-semester course covers all fundamental principles of organic chemistry, including modern bonding theory, analytical techniques, physical properties, and chemical reactions. This course is designed to satisfy requirements for students in the UMKC Six-Year Medical Program or certain Biology B.A. majors. This course is not recommended for pre-medical, pre-dental, pre-pharmacy or other pre-health students.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 212R and CHEM 212LR (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Experimental Organic Chemistry
catalog.description: Elementary organic chemistry experiments to teach basic laboratory operations.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 212R and CHEM 212LR (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Organic Chemistry I
catalog.description: The two terms ( CHEM 321 , CHEM 322R ) constitute an integrated unit in which the chemistry of aliphatic, aromatic, and some heterocyclic compounds are studied. The study begins with simple monofunctional compounds and ends with polyfunctional natural products.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 212R and CHEM 212LR (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory I
catalog.description: Introduces the student to basic techniques and procedures in isolation, purification, and characterization of organic compounds and simple reactions used in the organic chemistry laboratory. The student will also be trained in the proper way to write a scientific laboratory report.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 212R and CHEM 212LR (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory II
catalog.description: An extension of CHEM 321L . This course builds from the basic techniques, procedures, and writing to more advanced organic operations.

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Organic Chemistry II
catalog.description: Continuation of CHEM 321 .
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 321 and CHEM 321L (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Elementary Physical Chemistry
catalog.description: An introductory course in the principles of physical chemistry for students who have not had calculus.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 320 or CHEM 322R (each with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
catalog.title: Analytical Chemistry I: Quantitative Analysis
catalog.description: Principles of gravimetric, volumetric, electrolytic, and other methods of analysis.
catalog.prerequisites: CHEM 212R (with a grade of C- or better).

catalog.subject: CHEM
