catalog.title: Required Grad Enrollment
catalog.prerequisites: Prerequisite: You must be in the School of Science and Engineering Graduate program.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Voice Class I
catalog.description: A course in the fundamentals of correct voice productions; breathing, breath control, study of vowel forms and consonants. Elementary songs. Poise, posture, and stage presence. This course covers two points of view: development of the student's own voice and the pedagogy of voice-class instruction. A voice audition is required before registration.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Fundamentals of Music Theory for Musicians
catalog.description: An introduction to the rudiments of music theory and aural skills. Designed primarily as a review course for Conservatory students. Non-music majors who desire an accelerated theory fundamentals class may also enroll in this course with the approval of the instructor.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Fundamentals of Music
catalog.description: An introduction to the basic elements of music and music notation, including the study of melody, rhythm, scales and keys, triads, 7th chords, the piano keyboard and the musical staff. Designed primarily for those interested in learning about music but with little or no formal study of music theory.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Improvisation I
catalog.description: A systematic approach to the art of jazz improvisation. Emphasis upon performance as well as analysis.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Beginning Piano for Non-Music Majors
catalog.description: A class for non-music majors to acquire basic piano skills. Popular arrangements and group techniques designed to encourage students to play the piano for pleasure.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Keyboard Skills I
catalog.description: Group instruction focused on developing basic keyboard skills in sight-reading, transposition, harmonization, accompanying, improvisation, technique, and repertoire. Music theory concepts will be reinforced through keyboard applications.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Collaboration for Pianists I
catalog.description: Introductory study of collaborative techniques and vocal and instrumental literature with piano collaboration, for piano students. The class is designed to introduce students to basic principles of collaborative piano playing.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Collaboration for Pianists II
catalog.description: Continuing study of basic collaborative techniques and vocal and instrumental literature with piano collaboration for piano students. The class is designed to develop basic principles of collaborative piano playing for piano students. Continuation of Introduction to Collaboration for Pianists I.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Keyboard Skills I for Piano Majors
catalog.description: Techniques of sight reading , transposition, improvisation and open-score reading.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Keyboard Skills II for Piano Majors
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 114 .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Electronica
catalog.description: An overview of the vast body of music that falls under the label “electronica”. Course consists of a historical survey as students acquire language to talk about music, learn how technology informs the creation of the music, and summarize musical trends and cultural influences on the music. Final project is the creation of a piece of electronica using a musical app on a mobile device or a computer.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Appreciation
catalog.description: Designed for the general University student with little or no music background (non-music majors). An emphasis on the basic elements of music and the historical and stylistic periods, illustrated by examples from different genre, such as instrumental and vocal ensembles, large and small, solo literature for voice and instruments, and dance. This course is offered as an online asynchronous course.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Keyboard Skills II
catalog.description: Continued group instruction focused on developing basic keyboard skills in sight-reading, transposition, harmonization, accompanying, improvisation, technique, and repertoire. Music theory concepts will be reinforced through keyboard applications.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 110 with C or better and CONSVTY 141 with C or better.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History and Development of Rock and Roll
catalog.description: Designed for students with little or no music background, the course is an exploration of American popular music from early Rhythm and Blues and Country Western through Woodstock. Examines in detail the social/racial issues most important to the music and the cultural history of twentieth-century America. The course features online video lectures and numerous interviews with professors and scholars from other disciplines, presenting a perspective of the influence of this music on nearly every area of American life. Students are required to participate in online discussion groups as part of the class. Music majors may enroll for music elective credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to World Music
catalog.description: Introduction to World Music provides tools and paths for you to see the world differently and to enhance diversity by exploring musical traditions from around the world, many of which exist in Kansas City. Through lectures, videos, and live performances, Introduction to World Music will provide insight into the musical cultures of Africa, North America, the Caribbean, India, East Asia, Korea and Latin America and transform your view of our rapidly changing society. Open to all students.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Beginning Composition I
catalog.description: Introduction to the compositional process, including notation, calligraphy and score preparation, styles and forms, and related topics. Discussion and analysis of current works, trends and techniques in music composition. Final project is an original composition. Open to any UMKC student.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Beginning Composition II
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 133 with a focus on instrumentation. Discussion and analysis of current works, trends and techniques in music composition. Final project is an original composition. A weekly one-hour lab is required. Open to any UMKC student with consent of instructor.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 133 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Foundations
catalog.description: This course provides students with foundational information pertaining to the music therapy profession. Course topics include the history of music therapy, populations that music therapists serve, and an introduction to the use of music in therapeutic settings.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Musicianship I
catalog.description: Musicianship I focuses on diatonic harmony through an integration of theory and aural skills. It covers a music fundamentals review, principles of chord construction, four-part writing and harmonic syntax, as well as the application of concepts in analytical assignments and projects, dictation, and singing. Particular attention is given to the development of critical writing skills and the creation of stylistic compositions.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 103 (with a C or higher) or entrance by placement exam.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Musicianship II
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 141 with attention to phrase structure, small forms, and an introduction to chromaticism including such topics as applied chords, simple modulation, and modal mixture. Particular attention is given to the development of critical writing skills and the creation of stylistic compositions.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 110 (grade of C or better) and CONSVTY 141 (grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Muse
catalog.description: This course merges a variety of academic platforms and student activities so that collaboration among disciplines becomes a natural, logical solution to academic, professional, and performing arts challenges. Course content is derived from music history as it relates to Kansas City in the 21st century through examining the ethics of creating the canon. Activities are drawn directly from music history to achieve understanding in Human Values and Ethical Reasoning as they relate to our community.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Composition for Everyone
catalog.description: Learn how to make your own beats! Create music with instruments you invent! Find your own ways of notating music using graphics, text, and images. This course uses a hands-on approach to composition as a means to explore sound and listening to music. Through a progressive series of composition projects, students investigate the sonic organization of musical works and performances, focusing on fundamental questions of making music. This course requires no prior musical training.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Foreign Language For Singing II
catalog.description: A course for Italian diction. Emphasis is placed on sung rather than conversational pronunciation. Required for BM voice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Foreign Language For Singing III
catalog.description: A course for German diction. Emphasis is placed on sung rather than conversational pronunciation. Required for BM voice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Foreign Language For Singing IV
catalog.description: A course for French diction. Emphasis is placed on sung rather than conversational pronunciation. Required for BM voice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Basic Techniques of Audio Recording I
catalog.description: A study of the philosophy, history, and development of audio recording. Practical application of recording techniques and development of recording skills.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Basic Techniques of Audio Recording II
catalog.description: Continuation of study of recording techniques and development of recording skills.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 202 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Improvisation II
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 104 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Experience: II
catalog.description: Primarily assists the site coordinator with some leadership responsibilities.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Experience: III
catalog.description: Equal assisting and leading responsibilities on-site

catalog.description: Some assisting and primarily leading responsibilities on-site.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: UMKC Campus Band
catalog.description: Open to any student with prior instrumental experience, the UMKC Campus Band allows students from across UMKC's campus to study and perform ensemble repertoire from a variety of genres, styles, and historical periods to gain professional-level performing experience that will cultivate personal musicianship, clarify professional goals, and enhance overall music education.
catalog.prerequisites: Ability to play a band instrument

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Keyboard Skills III
catalog.description: Group instruction focused on developing intermediate keyboard skills in sight-reading, transposition, harmonization, accompanying, improvisation, technique, and repertoire. Music theory concepts will be reinforced through keyboard applications.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Intermediate Composition I
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 134 . A weekly one-hour lab is required.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 134 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Intermediate Composition for Non-Composition Majors I
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 134A. A weekly one-hour lab is required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Intermediate Composition II
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 233 with an emphasis on essential listening to contemporary repertoire works. Discussion and analysis of current works, trends and techniques in music composition. Final project is an original composition.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 233 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Intermediate Composition for Non-Composition Majors II
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 233A . A weekly one-hour lab is required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Digital Media for Composers
catalog.description: This course is designed to give students a thorough grasp of studio hardware and software used in composing with digital audio and other media. Topics include digital audio, mixing, MIDI, and synthesis techniques, as well as working with other contemporary media such as video. In addition to three 50-minute lecture/demo sessions per week, 3-5 hours minimum of in-studio work time is expected. Open to anyone regardless of musical training.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Performance Systems
catalog.description: Course builds upon studio techniques gained in Digital Media for Composing to conceptualizing and practicing the computer as an instrument. Students will be exposed to a variety of live performance systems which could include Ableton Live, MAX, PD, and other languages based on the expertise of the instructor. The outcome of the class is for students to perform a concert with the computer and/or other technology as their instrument. In addition to three 50-minute lecture/demo sessions per week, 3-5 hours minimum of in-studio time is expected. Open to anyone regardless of musical training.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Woodwind Techniques and Pedagogy
catalog.description: This course will discuss the fundamentals of playing and teaching woodwind instruments in an authentic setting. In order to achieve this, students are required to develop some performance ability as well as teaching techniques and strategies fo reach particular woodwind instrument. Basic principles, such as embouchure formation and development, fingerings, transposition, intonation, teaching materials, and teaching techniques will be covered. Flute, Clarinet, Saxophone, Oboe and Bassoon will be discussed during this course.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Brass Techniques and Pedagogy
catalog.description: This course will discuss the fundamentals of playing and teaching brass instruments in and authentic setting. In order to achieve this, students are required to develop some performance ability as well as teaching techniques and strategies for each particular brass instrument. Basic principles, such as embouchure formation and development, fingerings, transposition, intonation, teaching materials, and teaching techniques, will be covered. Trumpet, French Horn, Trombone, Baritone, and Tuba will be discussed during the course.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Musicianship III
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 142 . Study of harmonic structures such as Neapolitan and augmented sixth chords, chromatic modulation, and symmetry. Detailed examination of larger forms and genres such as sonata, rondo, art song, and fugue. Particular attention is given to the development of critical writing skills and the creation of stylistic compositions.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 142 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Musicianship IV
catalog.description: Study of late-nineteenth century chromaticism and analytical and compositional methods of twentieth and twenty-first century music, including set theory and twelve-tone theory. Particular attention is given to the development of critical writing skills and the creation of stylistic compositions.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 241 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Marching Band & Jazz Ensemble Techniques
catalog.description: This course is designed to prepare pre-service teachers with pedagogical and organizational techniques for marching band and jazz ensembles in the schools. The course will include developing practical rehearsal techniques for teaching body manipulation in space, designing and evaluating marching band field design and maneuvers, jazz ensemble pedagogy, jazz improvisation pedagogy, and the use of appropriate materials. A field experience component will further student interaction with an active band program that will allow continued examination and development of a philosophy on the role of marching band and jazz ensembles within the school curriculum.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Teaching Matters: A Professional Beginning
catalog.description: A Professional Beginning allows students to explore the professional world of teaching music. Students will begin the process of thinking and acting as professional music educators using readings, discussions, presentations, field experiences, interviews, reflections, and opportunities to practice the skill of teaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Elementary Music Methods
catalog.description: Laboratory course for classroom teachers in which principles of instructional design will be applied to music teaching. Students who have extensive music background may elect CONSVTY 385 in place of CONSVTY 285 .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Studio Class
catalog.description: Experiential lab where students gain orientation and experience with pedagogy, literature, and performance.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: UMKC Aurum Chorale
catalog.description: UMKC Aurum Chorale is a non-auditioned choral ensemble for tenor and bass voices. Aurum sings a diverse repertoire of music and performs in several concerts each year. For select performances, Aurum partners with the soprano/alto chorale, Azure, and is known as the UMKC Choral Union. Any UMKC student can register in advance, but a “placement hearing” is required in order to determine your voice part for the choir.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: UMKC Azure Chorale
catalog.description: UMKC Azure Chorale is a non-auditioned choral ensemble for soprano and alto voices. Azure sings a diverse repertoire of music and performs in several concerts each year. For select performances, Azure partners with the tenor/bass chorale, Aurum, and is known as the UMKC Choral Union. Any UMKC student can register in advance, but a “placement hearing” is required in order to determine your voice part for the choir.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera Theater Ensemble
catalog.description: An introduction to opera performance techniques for opera chorus/ensemble. Major literature for opera choruses may also be surveyed. Course participants are required to perform in the chorus of a UMKC Opera production. This course can be taken at any time during the BM Voice Performance student's degree, and will count towards the requirement of 2 semesters of performing in a UMKC opera production.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera Production
catalog.description: An introduction to the non-performance, production-related aspects of Opera. Students will assume various production responsibilities in a UMKC Opera. Students will be overseen by Opera and Theatre faculty and receive instruction related to the student’s designated production responsibility. This course requirement can be fulfilled at any time during the BM - Voice Performance degree, but not in the same semester the student registers for CONSVTY 301E (Opera Theatre Ensemble) and/or CONSVTY 319 (Opera Role).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Ensemble for Composers
catalog.description: Observation, score analysis, non-performance participating during a semester's rehearsals and performance by a participating Conservatory ensemble. Students a.) keep journals that are periodically reviewed and graded by the composition faculty, and b.) meet with composition faculty periodically to review and discuss issues raised in the ensemble settings.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 234 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Orchestra
catalog.description: Required of all qualified music majors and open to all interested students by audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Band
catalog.description: The Jazz Band comprises saxophone, trombone, trumpets and rhythm section students and performs traditional, modern, and original music. The ensemble is open to all UMKC students by audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Workshop
catalog.description: Jazz Workshop

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Orchestra
catalog.description: The Jazz Orchestra comprises saxophone, trombone, trumpets and rhythm section students of the highest level in the Conservatory and performs repertoire of the highest caliber available. The curriculum is well balanced between traditional, modern, and original music and requires advanced musical and technical facility amongst its members. The class is open to all UMKC students by audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Large Ensemble Rhythm Section Workshop
catalog.description: This course is designed for rhythm section players (piano, guitar, bass, and percussion). Students will work on rhythm section concepts and transcriptions for small ensembles and big bands, as well to learn the music currently being played by CONSVTY 303B (Jazz Band).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Accompanying
catalog.description: This course is designed to improve undergraduate piano students’ collaborative piano skills through intensive coaching. The class will investigate the historical/stylistic context of each work covered, as well as issues common to the musical genre, instrument type, or time period of each assigned piece. Issues inherent to collaborative piano playing will be explored, including score preparation, pedaling, voicing, balance, practice and rehearsal techniques, orchestral reductions, ensemble skills, and professional issues.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Improvisational Music/Media Performance Ensemble
catalog.description: IMP Ensemble explores improvisation in the broadest definition, where listening and responding become a way of real-time creation. IMP is a think-tank of people willing to risk and fail quickly, so a show can go on, using any new individual media to explore the boundaries of the medium and improvisation. No particular instrumental skill is needed, only an open mind. Non-Conservatory students by instructor approval.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Improvisation III
catalog.description: Jazz Improvisation III.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 204 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Chamber Music
catalog.description: A) Strings, B) Woodwinds, C) Brass D) Accordion, E) Percussion, F) Music Nova.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Principles Of Chamber Music
catalog.description: Collaborative music-making in groups of like-instruments (piano ensembles, flute quartets, sax quartets, etc., plus beginning experiences in string quartets, woodwind and brass quintets, etc.). Weekly coaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Principles Of Chamber Music
catalog.description: Collaborative music-making in groups of like-instruments (piano ensembles, flute quartets, sax quartets, etc., plus beginning experiences in string quartets, woodwind and brass quintets, etc.). Weekly coaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Philharmonic Orchestra
catalog.description: With its collaborative environment and diverse repertoire, the Conservatory Philharmonic Orchestra offers an enriching musical experience that supports both personal growth and ensemble excellence. Open to music majors, music minors, all UMKC students and community members.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Wind Ensemble
catalog.description: A select concert band ensemble, modeled on Frederick Fennell's Eastman Wind Ensemble concept, designed for high-level, artistic, public performances of major literature for winds and percussion. Membership in the Wind Ensemble is open to any student who qualifies through audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Wind Symphony
catalog.description: The Wind Symphony comprises wind, brass and percussion students of the highest level in the Conservatory and performs repertoire of the highest caliber available to the medium. The curriculum is well balanced between traditional, modern, and chamber music and requires advanced musical and technical facility amongst its members. The class is open to all UMKC students by audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Chamber Singers
catalog.description: Chamber Singers is a select chamber ensemble of mixed voices and serves as the lab choir for the graduate choral conductors as well as upper-class undergraduate conductors. Typically drawn from the membership of Conservatory Concert Choir and Conservatory Singers, Chamber Singers performs several concerts each year. * This course does not count toward the ensemble requirement for BM Voice Performance and BME Choral Music Education.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: UMKC Choral Union
catalog.description: UMKC Choral Union (formerly University Singers) is a mixed ensemble focusing producing excellence in choral music through the “union” of student, staff, faculty, and community effort. UMKC Choral Union focuses on music for larger chorus and orchestra as well as music from the unaccompanied choral tradition, choral masterworks, and newly composed works from around the world. Open to all singers regardless of experience. Any UMKC student can register in advance, but a “placement hearing” is required in order to determine your voice part for the choir.
catalog.prerequisites: None. Open to UMKC Students, Staff, Faculty, and the greater KC community.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Singers
catalog.description: The premier choral ensemble of the UMKC Conservatory, Conservatory Singers is a highly select group of undergraduate and graduate singers drawn from both the Conservatory and the student population of the University of Missouri-Kansas City. Conservatory Singers perform a diverse repertoire of collegiate and professional level choral literature including major works with orchestra. The ensemble participates in numerous concerts throughout the year, has performed at regional and national conferences, and has engaged in regional touring opportunities. Open to all students by audition only.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Concert Choir
catalog.description: Conservatory Concert Choir is a large mixed ensemble exclusively comprised of undergraduate singers which specializes in the performance of a wide variety of choral music, including classical masterworks as well as spirituals and multicultural choral music. Conservatory Concert Choir participates in numerous Kansas City-area performances each year and was recently a featured ensemble at the Missouri Music Educators Conference in January 2020. Open to all undergraduate students by audition only.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Audio Recording III
catalog.description: Continuation of study of recording techniques and music production skills.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 203 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Keyboard Skills IV
catalog.description: Group instruction focused on developing intermediate keyboard skills in sight-reading, transposition, harmonization, accompanying, improvisation, technique, and repertoire. Music theory concepts will be reinforced through keyboard applications.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Theory
catalog.description: The basics of written jazz harmony and its nomenclature will be addressed. Topics covered will include chords, harmonic progressions, reharmonization, voice leading, dissonance, melody, transcription, analysis and the study of form(s). Notation will be addressed throughout. Students will acquire the fundamentals to pursue jazz improvisation, arranging and composition on a more informed level.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 141 and CONSVTY 142 (grade of C or better)

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Piano Techniques
catalog.description: This course builds on techniques acquired in keyboard skills, employing them in practical situations that will simulate professional work with clients. Students will also develop musical skills with application beyond the piano, including song-leading, transcription, transposition, and knowledge of repertoire.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 223 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Guitar Techniques
catalog.description: Course covers techniques of leading guitar styles from the 1920's to present. Includes listening, analysis, transcription, and performing.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 373G (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Improvisation
catalog.description: The course is an introduction to improvisational models and practices in music therapy. Students will explore the goals, techniques, and uses of improvisational models of music therapy for various populations.
catalog.prerequisites: Music therapy major; CONSVTY 242 and CONSVTY 315 .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Ear Training and Listening
catalog.description: This course offers basic fundamental techniques needed to improve aural perceptions in both the translation of hearing into writing and the performance of reading into singing and playing in the jazz idiom. Introduction and practice in singing, aural recognition and writing of intervals and short, simple melodies. Also includes rhythm, memory and improvisational drills.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera Role Performance
catalog.description: Preparation, rehearsal and performance of a role in an opera production at UMKC. This course may count toward the 2 semester opera performance requirement for the BM in Vocal Performance degree. Credit for non-performing duties such as assistant directing or assistant stage managing may be available with approval of the Vocal Studies faculty and the current Stage Director.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Alexander Technique for Performers
catalog.description: This course introduces performers to the Alexander Technique, a tool for enhancing physical awareness, movement, and presence on stage. Designed for actors, musicians, and dancers, this course will explore the principles of this method and how they can be applied to improve performance quality and reduce performance-related tension.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Pedagogy I
catalog.description: Instructional strategies for teaching the beginning piano student including methods, materials, repertoire, technique and the use of music technology. Various aspects of establishing and managing a piano studio will also be addressed.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Pedagogy - Supervised Teaching I
catalog.description: Supervised practicum designed to demonstrate lesson planning and activities for beginning students through the observation of experienced teachers and various supervised teaching experiences.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Pedagogy II
catalog.description: Instructional strategies for teaching the intermediate and advanced piano student, including methods, materials, repertoire, technique, and the use of music technology.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 325 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Pedagogy - Supervised Teaching II
catalog.description: Supervised practicum designed to demonstrate lesson planning and activities for students of various levels through observation of experienced teachers and various supervised teaching experiences.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 325A (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Ear Training
catalog.description: Study of atonal and highly chromatic tonal aural problems, complex rhythms, and recognition of instruments.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Instrumentation
catalog.description: An introduction to the instruments of the symphony orchestra and rudiments of scoring. Classification of instruments and learning to write for all Western transposing instruments.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Orchestration I
catalog.description: An introduction to the instruments of the symphony orchestra and rudiments of scoring. Meets concurrently with CONSVTY 331 ; the third credit hour is required for music composition and music theory majors.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Composition
catalog.description: The primary objective of this course is for the student to create a substantial portfolio work. One on one instruction will focus on techniques and artistic methods as well as expression. Group seminars will facilitate a student’s ability to articulate to others their concepts, techniques and aesthetic choices. Working in groups also encourages and trains a student to give positive constructive feedback to fellow students. May be repeated for credit.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 234 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Electronic Music Composition
catalog.description: This course focuses on creating an original music composition in any style utilizing the full range of digital audio or MIDI hardware, software ad techniques available to the student. In addition to weekly meetings arranged with the instructor, 5-8 hours per week of studio time is required. May be repeated for credit.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 235 or CONSVTY 236 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Principles of Arts Business
catalog.description: This Arts Business course is in an online format and will provide an overview of the many different careers and business practices in the arts industries. The course content will highlight the variables considered when creating, selling, and marketing a variety of items in different mediums.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Arts Entrepreneurship
catalog.description: This course will teach students how to design a business model, refine that business model, and take action. This course will take students through several models and frameworks that can be used to create new ventures (for-profit, not-for-profit, social ventures), create value within existing organizations, and pursue an entrepreneurial career in the arts.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Anatomy for Music Therapy Practice
catalog.description: This course is an introduction to basic human anatomy and pathology with an emphasis on applicability to multiple aspects of music therapy practice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Styles and Genres in Music
catalog.description: This course will introduce students to the major stylistic periods and genres in Western musical history through a chronological, case-study based approach.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Methods in Musicology
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the field of musicology through research, writing, analysis of primary sources, and an exploration of methodologies. Topics vary according to course instructor.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History of Music in Western Civilization I
catalog.description: A chronological study of music in Western civilization with emphasis on periods and styles from early times to the death of Bach. Outside listening required.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History of Music in Western Civilization II
catalog.description: A chronological study of music in Western civilization from 1750 to the present. Outside listening required.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 351 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History And Development Of Jazz I
catalog.description: History of Jazz from its beginning through the present, using recordings, films and musical examples. Emphasis on major historical trends, including Early Jazz, Ragtime, Dixieland, Swing, Bebop, Cool Jazz, Hard Bop, Free Jazz, Jazz-Rock Fusion and modern developments. This course makes use of the Marr Sound Archive, and is appropriate for all students throughout the UMKC Campus.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History and Development of Jazz II
catalog.description: This course builds upon material learned in CONSVTY 353A to concentrate in depth on notable artists, bands, and contributions from those in other roles (e.g., promoters, managers, critics) who have guided the development of jazz history.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 353A (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History and Development of Jazz II
catalog.description: This course contextualizes jazz within the musical culture of the twentieth century. It concentrates on the lives, bands, and works of people who have been instrumental in the development of various jazz styles. This course makes use of the Marr Sound Archive.
catalog.prerequisites: ENGLISH 225 and CONSVTY 353A (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Choral Literature
catalog.description: Includes listening and analysis as they relate to programming and educational issues in choral ensemble setting. May be repeated for credit.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 380 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Wind Band Literature and Lab
catalog.description: Designed for the student working with beginning and intermediate levels of wind/percussion students. Includes critical analysis and evaluation of literature and literature selection as it relates to educational issues and programming in wind/percussion ensemble settings. Includes an application phase in a wind band rehearsal/performance setting providing opportunities realistic opportunities for observation and teaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: String Literature
catalog.description: Includes listening and analysis as they relate to programming and educational issues in string ensemble settings. May be repeated for credit.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 381 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Literature I
catalog.description: A survey of study through analysis, reading, listening and performance of literature for stringed keyboard instruments from the Renaissance period to 1850. Special attention given to the development of instruments, forms, techniques, performance practices and idiomatic styles.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Piano Literature II
catalog.description: A study through analysis, reading, listening, and performance of piano repertoire from 1850-present day. Special attention given to the development of instruments, forms, techniques, performance practices and idiomatic styles.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy in Wellness and Intergenerational Settings
catalog.description: This course provides students with foundational information pertaining to the music therapy profession. course topics include the history of music therapy, populations that music therapists serve and an introduction to the use of music in therapeutic settings.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Yeah, Yeah, Yeah: The Cultural and Musical Impact of the Beatles
catalog.description: This course will explore the career and music of the Beatles by examining their impact on popular culture in Britain and the United States. Students will learn about popular song forms, recording techniques, and lyric writing and analysis. They will also employ video and audio media for projects, and engage with readings that approach the Beatles both historically and culturally.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Capstone
catalog.description: This seminar course assists students in creating a research or clinical-based capstone project.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 435 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Instrumental Excerpts
catalog.description: Intended to introduce students to standard instrumental excerpts. Students will be expected to prepare and play selected excerpts for their instrument.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Skills Lab
catalog.description: This course provides students with development, practice, and mastery of clinical music therapy skills. Course topics include, clinical musicianship, repertoire development, and group leadership skills.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Choral/Vocal Techniques
catalog.description: Laboratory applications of vocal pedagogy, ensemble rehearsal technique, literature selection, and performance practice. Students will participate in singing and observation activities in a large ensemble setting with an emphasis on critical analysis of technical and pedagogical issues.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 380 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Survey Of Wind And Percussion Instruments
catalog.description: An overview of basic wind and percussion instruments used in public school settings. Includes embouchre formation, hand position, sound production, and pedagogical issues encountered in beginning situations.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Survey Of String Instruments
catalog.description: An overview of basic string instruments used in public school settings. Includes hand position, bowing, sound production, and pedagogical issues encountered in beginning situations.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Collaborative Piano I
catalog.description: Study of collaborative techniques and vocal literature.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Collaborative Piano II
catalog.description: Continuation of CONSVTY 376 .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Instrumental Ensemble Rehearsal Techniques & Lab
catalog.description: Laboratory applications of large instrumental ensemble (strings, winds, percussion) pedagogy, ensemble rehearsal technique, and performance practice. Students will participate in playing, observation, rehearsal activities in a large ensemble setting with an emphasis on critical analysis of technical pedagogical issues and ensemble performance preparation. Includes an off-campus course meeting.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 358 , CONSVTY 381 and Large Ensemble (each with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Instrumental Ensemble Rehearsal Lab
catalog.description: Laboratory applications of wind/percussion pedagogy, ensemble rehearsal technique, literature selection, and performance practice. Students will participate in playing, observation, and rehearsal activities in a large ensemble setting with an emphasis on critical analysis of technical pedagogical issues and ensemble performance preparation. This course may meet off-campus.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 358 , CONSVTY 381 , large ensemble requirement (each with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Clinical Applications - Group Leading Techniques
catalog.description: This course provides an opportunity for music therapy students to apply learned skills to musical situations they will encounter as music therapists. Course will include a range of group leading skills applicable for varied music therapy settings and with distinct populations including special education, older adults, medical, neurologic, and wellness.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Clinical Applications - Music Therapy Interventions
catalog.description: This course provides an overview of music therapy techniques (i.e. songwriting, lyric analysis, relaxation, music videos, and rhythmic stimulation) as utilized with various ages and populations for therapeutic goal achievement. Course content includes leadership, musical, and therapeutic relationship skills as well as community project components for skill application.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Clinical Applications: Music Therapy Singing Techniques
catalog.description: This course provides students with specific training in singing varied vocal styles that apply to the diverse musical settings they will encounter as professional music therapists.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Clinical Applications - Music Therapy Repertoire
catalog.description: This course provides a survey of song repertoire used within music therapy practice across various client/patient populations, and within different therapeutic interventions. The study of accompaniment skills necessary to play suggested repertoire is also included.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Basic Conducting - Choral
catalog.description: A study of the basic techniques of all rhythms, patterns, subdivision of beats, dynamics, starting, stopping, and giving cues through conducting in class. Elementary study of the score as to form and harmonic content will be discussed.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Basic Conducting - Instrumental
catalog.description: A study of the basic techniques of all rhythms, patterns, subdivision of beats, dynamics, starting, stopping, and giving cues through conducting in class. Elementary study of the score as to form and harmonic intent will be discussed.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Choral Conducting
catalog.description: A study of choral techniques including voice tryouts, placement, attack, release, blend, vocal development, diction, and rehearsal techniques through actual experience of conducting in class.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 380 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Instrumental Conducting
catalog.description: A study of instrumental conducting techniques through actual conducting situations in instrumental groups. Primary objective will be the study of instrumental rehearsal techniques.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 381 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Elementary Music Methods
catalog.description: Basic principles of curriculum planning for music education, investigation of current methods and approaches, and practical teaching experience in laboratory setting. For music majors and non-majors who have extensive musical backgrounds.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 , CONSVTY 411C (each with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Secondary Music Methods - Instrumental
catalog.description: The organization, scheduling and program building techniques of middle school and high school band and orchestral programs. Areas of study will include curriculum, pedagogical techniques, classroom management, music library organization, budgeting procedures, and basic instrumental techniques.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Secondary Music Methods - Choral
catalog.description: The organization, scheduling and program building techniques of middle school and high school choral programs. Areas of study will include curriculum, pedagogical techniques, classroom management, music library management, budgeting procedures, and basic vocal techniques.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Analysis
catalog.description: Analysis offers students the opportunity to learn and apply multiple analytical techniques to complete movements and larger pieces of music by focusing on the study of pitch, rhythm, form, aesthetics, and issues of performance.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Foundations I
catalog.description: This course provides the clinical student practice of evidence-based direct services, procedures, and documentation of the music therapy treatment process (assessment, setting goals and objectives, treatment plan, interventions, data collection, and evaluation). Students will participate in practical experiences and clinical supervision in the context of community services for children or adults.
catalog.prerequisites: Music therapy major; CONSVTY 142 and CONSVTY 123 ; or permission of the instructor.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Foundations II
catalog.description: This course continues the clinical student practice of evidence-based direct services, procedures, and documentation of the music therapy treatment process (assessment, setting goals and objectives, treatment plan, interventions, data collection, and evaluation). Students will participate in practical experiences and clinical supervision in the context of community services for children or adults. Additionally, students will explore issues regarding diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice in music therapy practice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Yoga for Performers
catalog.description: Yoga for Performers (YFP) is an entry point into the discovery of yoga, intended to stimulate and provoke performers, some of whom might not otherwise be aware that yoga is a healthy and viable option for their development. The course is open to all, but will focus especially on issues related to musical performance.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Improvisation IV
catalog.description: Continuation of Jazz Improvisation III. This course features analyses of the blues, free improvisation focusing on rhythm changes and bi-tonal/polytonal chords, as well as styles from Dixieland to contemporary jazz. A strong emphasis is placed on solo construction and development of individual styles.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 304 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Philosophical and Pragmatic Foundations of Music Education
catalog.description: This course experience guides students in developing philosophical and social/historical frameworks along with practical skills to assist them in addressing varied opportunities and challenges as a music educator in contemporary American schools.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Audio Intern Program
catalog.description: Practical recording experience interning with Conservatory recording and music production labs with one lecture weekly.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Therapy Principles and Applications
catalog.description: This course provides knowledge of music therapy services for people with behavioral, neurological, motor, and medical problems. Course content will focus on population characteristics and needs, literature on music therapy to address these needs and applications to clinical work in music therapy.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music in Therapy:Adults
catalog.description: Lecture and clinical demonstration of theory and practice of music therapy with adult clients.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music in Therapy: Children
catalog.description: Lecture and clinical demonstrations of theory and practice of music therapy with children.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Internship
catalog.description: A minimum of 900 hours of supervised clinical experience at a Rostered site approved by the American Music Therapy Association or an Affiliate site approved by UMKC Conservatory Music Therapy faculty, to be taken after all other course work for the music therapy degree, excepting any advanced coursework, is completed.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Music Therapy Principles and Applications
catalog.description: This course provides knowledge of music therapy services for wellness as well as people with emotional, social, and behavioral problems. Course content will focus on population characteristics and needs, literature on music therapy to address these needs and applications to clinical work in music therapy. Additionally, instruction in music therapy program development and implementation will be provided.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Field Experience in Music
catalog.description: To introduce music students to a critical examination of the complex nature of teaching, learning, children, and the music classroom/ensemble setting. Students will be expected to spend 30 hours observing, participating, planning and teaching in an assigned music classroom environment during the semester.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Field Experience in Music
catalog.description: To introduce music students to secondary school settings and further develop observation, planning and teaching skills. Students will be expected to spend 30 hours in a middle/ junior high school music classroom and 30 hours in a high school music classroom for a total of 60 hours during the semester.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 411A (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Field Experience in Music
catalog.description: To introduce music students to elementary school music settings and continue to refine observation, planning and teaching skills in secondary school music settings. Students will be expected to spend 30 hours in an elementary school music classroom and 30 hours in either a middle school/junior high or high school music classroom.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 411B (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Student Teaching Music in Elementary School
catalog.description: Observation, planning and teaching in an elementary music classroom setting. Students will be expected to spend a minimum of seven weeks teaching full-time under supervision.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 411C (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Student Teaching Music in Secondary School
catalog.description: Observation, planning and teaching in a middle school/junior high or high school music classroom setting. Students will be expected to spend a minimum of seven weeks teaching full-time under supervision.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 411C (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Holistic Wellness in the Arts
catalog.description: This course explores holistic wellness strategies for musicians and performing artists, emphasizing physical, mental, emotional, and pragmatic well-being. Students will engage in practical activities, reflection, and discussion designed to cultivate sustainable artistic habits, reduce performance-related stress, and prevent injury. By integrating evidence-based wellness principles with musicianship, students will develop a personal and pedagogical toolkit for long-term health, resilience, and creative fulfillment.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera Workshop
catalog.description: Introduction to stagecraft, movement and acting for opera. Special emphasis on creating active aria, recitative and art song performances.
catalog.prerequisites: THEATRE 102 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Scene Study
catalog.description: Preparation, rehearsal and performance of scenes from opera, operetta and music theatre. Scenes will be determined and assigned based on student's needs and development. One-act operas may also occasionally be produced in this class.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera Role Preparation and Audition Techniques
catalog.description: Students will work on specific audition techniques for the operatic solo singer, which may include dramatic interpretation of repertoire, stage movement, resume building, and other aspects to assist the performer in the audition process.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 417 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Theory Review For Graduate Students
catalog.description: An intensive review with emphasis placed on analysis.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Aural Skills Review for Graduate Students
catalog.description: An intensive review of ear training and sight singing.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Musicianship Enrichment
catalog.description: An intensive review of the essential skills and ideas necessary to attain fluency in Western music theory with an emphasis on analysis and aural skills.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be a graduate music student in the Conservatory.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Business Jazz And Commercial Music
catalog.description: An introduction to the various elements of the music industry, including production, marketing, unions, contracts, broadcasting, licensing agreements and copyrights.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Arranging for Choral Groups
catalog.description: Practice in transcribing vocal music of the current pop idiom. Analysis and writing in contemporary harmonic idioms. Stylistic analysis of solo and choral writing in operettas and musical plays. Scoring for mixed voices, men's voices, and women's voices.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Arranging Instrumental
catalog.description: Arranging Instrumental.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Arranging for Small Ensembles
catalog.description: This course will teach the art of Calligraphy as well as the techniques of arranging and orchestration for small jazz ensembles for up to five horns. The course will also include an in-dept study of basic voicings, instrumental sonorities, and some extended forms using intensive listening and score study. UMKC combos, or top Kansas City professionals, will perform final assignments.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 311 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Arranging for Big Bands
catalog.description: This course is a continuation of Jazz Arranging for small ensembles. It will cover the basics of arranging and orchestration techniques for big bands. It includes an in-depth study of basic voicing and instrumental sonorities using intensive listening and score study. The students will have a chance to hear their final arrangements performed at the end of the semester by the Concert Jazz Band.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 426B (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Tonal Counterpoint
catalog.description: A study of tonal counterpoint in the 18th century and beyond, with a focus on stylistic composition and in-class performance.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Post-Tonal Theory
catalog.description: Analysis and writing in contemporary styles.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 242 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Orchestration
catalog.description: A detailed study of the scores of major orchestral and wind ensemble works, plus the application of orchestrational concepts in the creation or orchestration of an original piece of music.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 331 or CONSVTY 234 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Senior Composition
catalog.description: Final semester of private instruction moving towards students’ portfolio completion and capstone presentation. Student will work closely with faculty member to identify and move towards their career goals after graduation.
catalog.prerequisites: Two semesters of CONSVTY 333 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Composition Capstone
catalog.description: Preparation and performance of the student's original compositions at one or more events sponsored by UMKC Conservatory, with a total of 50 to 60 minutes of performance time.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 433 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Psychological Foundations of Music
catalog.description: The study of the psychological aspects of music including perception, cognition, affect, and preference. An introduction measurement and experimental research including statistical techniques.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Computer Literacy for Musicians
catalog.description: Computing skills for the music teacher. Study of the computer as a tool for music majors who will teach in public school music classes, direct ensembles, or teach at the college or university level. Hands-on practice with file creation and editing, graphics and character set generation, data analysis, preparation of computer based instruction, and data retrieval. For upper level undergraduate and graduate students.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Keyboard Techniques I
catalog.description: This course is designed for jazz majors to develop skills needed to harmonize tunes at the piano and effectively comp in the mainstream jazz group. It is meant to give the student an organized approach for exploring any harmonic style at the keyboard.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 110 ; must be a jazz major.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Keyboard Techniques II
catalog.description: This course builds upon techniques in accompaniment, improvisation, and composition at the keyboard begun in CONSVTY 440 (Jazz Keyboard Techniques I) with a move toward more advanced repertoire and harmonic complexity.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music and Film
catalog.description: Designed for the general university student, this course will survey the use of music in cinema. It will include sections on music, technology, the film medium and the various ways in which music adds to the cinematic experience. Music majors may enroll for elective credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Seminar in Musicology
catalog.description: Offers a rotating option of topics in musicology drawn from the research interests and expertise of the musicology faculty.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Seminar in Music Theory
catalog.description: Advanced Seminar in Music Theory offers a rotating option of topics in advanced music theory drawn from the research interests and expertise of the music theory faculty.
catalog.prerequisites: CONSVTY 390 (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Vocal Literature I
catalog.description: Literature for the solo voice. A course covering the literature from 1600 to present times, illustrated by recordings and members of the class and the instructor. Required for B.M. voice majors.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Vocal Literature II
catalog.description: A continuation of CONSVTY 457 .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz/Commercial Music Pedagogy
catalog.description: This course is designed to develop skills in the teaching of jazz and commercial music. Students will be exposed to a variety of materials, techniques and philosophies and trained in various techniques of rehearsing and conducting jazz ensembles, including the study of scores and recordings of different styles and rehearsal of the Conservatory's jazz ensembles. Includes an emphasis on structuring jazz and studio music curricula at the collegiate level.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Independent Study
catalog.description: Intensive reading, research projects, creative work, or special performance in the student's major field, selected by the student in consultation with the appropriate faculty.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Performing Arts Capstone
catalog.description: A capstone course intended for the planning and execution of a significant project in the student’s area(s) of interest, which demonstrates an understanding and proficiency in one or more elements studied in music, theatre, dance, or a combination of disciplines. Supervised by a member of the faculty, the project incorporates research and documentation, as well as a public exhibition, performance, or presentation.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Pedagogy of Music Theory
catalog.description: Pedagogy of Music Theory

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Pedagogy of Instrumental Music
catalog.description: A study of the pedagogical materials and methods used in teaching applied instrumental music.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar-Workshop in Music
catalog.description: Special courses in techniques, theory, and repertoire taught by the Conservatory staff and visiting specialists.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar-Workshop In Music
catalog.description: Seminar-Workshop In Music

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar-Workshop in Music
catalog.description: Special courses in techniques, theory, and repertoire taught by the Conservatory staff and visiting specialists.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research Problems
catalog.description: Individual study under the direction of a faculty advisor, leading to the writing of a formal paper. A public, non-graded presentation of the paper with performance examples is required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Comprehensive Review
catalog.description: This course is required of all graduate students studying music in the UMKC Conservatory and allows those students to synthesize their graduate-level work through a series of questions or an in-depth project.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Arranging
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide an in-depth exploration of jazz arranging techniques at an advanced level. Students will build upon foundational arranging skills to develop a deeper understanding of jazz styles, harmonic practices, ensemble voicing, and orchestration for various jazz ensembles. Emphasis will be placed on analysis of classic arrangements, original composition, and the workshopping and performance of practical arranging assignments.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Industry Insights
catalog.description: This course covers trends in the music industry. Through critical analysis, case studies, and interaction with industry professionals, students will explore various facets of the industry, from intellectual property rights to digital distribution, pedagogy and research.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Styles and Genres in Music
catalog.description: Styles and Genres in Music presents an overview of Western music history through three lenses: chronology, genre, and musical style. It is intended for students who have previously studied music history and wish to take a broader view of music history than the view offered through period-specific classes.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Internship
catalog.description: Students will work in a structured and supervised internship with a professional arts organization in Kansas City. Students will receive guidance from course faculty and the internship supervisor from the venture at which they work.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Stage Role
catalog.description: This course is for the preparation of a stage role in the operatic or musical theatre repertoire within UMKC Conservatory's lyric theatre season.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate student in the Conservatory; Audition required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Orchestra
catalog.description: The Conservatory Orchestra comprises string, wind, brass and percussion students of the highest level in the Conservatory and performs repertoire of the highest caliber available to the medium. The repertoire includes the great works for orchestra considered the “standard repertoire” from approximately 1770 to today, and includes orchestral, opera, and choral/orchestral works. Sensitivity to outstanding musicianship, historical styles, and appropriate performance practices are required. In addition to the highest expectations as an instrumentalist, your ability to apply intellect and spirit in meaningful ways during rehearsals and concerts is also demanded. Membership is open to any student who qualifies through audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Workshop
catalog.description: Jazz Workshop consists of small ensembles featuring winds, brass, and rhythm section members performing and studying jazz literature under the leadership of a jazz faculty member.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Orchestra
catalog.description: The Jazz Orchestra is open to saxophone, trombone, trumpet and rhythm section students of the highest level in the Conservatory; the Orchestra performs repertoire at the highest possible caliber. The curriculum is well balanced between traditional, modern, and original music and requires advanced musical and technical facility amongst its members. The class is open to all UMKC students by audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Principles of Chamber Music
catalog.description: The study and performance of chamber music for strings, piano, winds, brass, and voice. Weekly coaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Philharmonic Orchestra
catalog.description: With its collaborative environment and diverse repertoire, the Conservatory Philharmonic Orchestra offers an enriching musical experience that supports both personal growth and ensemble excellence. Open to graduate students.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Wind Ensemble
catalog.description: A select concert band ensemble, designed for high-level, artistic, public performances of major literature for winds and percussion. As a member of this Wind Ensemble, you are contributing to the three hundred year legacy of concert band music in the western world. Sensitivity to outstanding musicianship, historical styles, and appropriate performance practices are required. In addition to the highest expectations as an instrumentalist, your ability to apply intellect and spirit in meaningful ways during rehearsals and concerts is also demanded. Membership in the Wind Ensemble is open to any student who qualifies through audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Wind Symphony
catalog.description: The Wind Symphony comprises wind, brass and percussion students of the highest level in the Conservatory and performs repertoire of the highest caliber available to the medium. The curriculum is well balanced between traditional, modern, and chamber music and requires advanced musical and technical facility amongst its members. The class is open to all UMKC students by audition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Chamber Singers
catalog.description: Chamber Singers is a select chamber ensemble of mixed voices and serves as the lab choir for the graduate choral conductors as well as upper-class undergraduate conductors. Typically drawn from the membership of Conservatory Concert Choir and Conservatory Singers, Chamber Singers performs several concerts each year and serves as the choral ensemble for the majority of the graduate choral conductor recitals. Open to all students by audition only.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Conservatory Singers
catalog.description: The premier choral ensemble of the UMKC Conservatory, Conservatory Singers is a highly select group of undergraduate and graduate singers drawn from both the Conservatory and the student population of the University of Missouri-Kansas City. Conservatory Singers perform a diverse repertoire of collegiate and professional level choral literature including major works with orchestra. The ensemble participates in numerous concerts throughout the year, has performed at regional and national conferences, and has engaged in regional touring opportunities. Open to all students by audition only.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Graduate Piano Pedagogy I
catalog.description: This course will provide an introduction to piano pedagogy by focusing on best practices for teaching elementary piano students. Topics will include average-age piano methods, technical concepts for the elementary student, rote teaching strategies, learning modalities, motivation theories, andragogy, business practices, and technology for teaching. After briefly reviewing several historical piano methods, students will examine current piano methods and assemble a curriculum that will be used to teach a weekly 30-minute lesson to a beginning piano student.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Graduate Piano Pedagogy II
catalog.description: This course will examine pedagogical topics related to intermediate students. Topics will include intermediate repertoire by standard composers, technical considerations for intermediate students, effective practice strategies, sight reading, memorization, and strategies for teaching phrasing. After reading through a variety of standard repertoire from Levels 3-7, students will compile an anthology of intermediate pieces with annotated practice guides. They will also perform selections during an in-class recital.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Instrumental Excerpts
catalog.description: Intended to introduce students to standard and advanced instrumental excerpts. Students will be expected to prepare and play selected excerpts for their instrument.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Foundations I
catalog.description: This course provides the first-semester clinical graduate student practice and implementation of direct services, procedures, and documentation of the music therapy treatment process (assessment, setting goals and objectives, treatment plan, interventions, data collection, and evaluation). Students will participate in supervision and clinical experiences within the context of community-dwelling older adult populations.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Graduate Music Theory Review
catalog.description: An intensive review of the essential skills and ideas necessary to attain fluency in Western music theory with an emphasis on fundamentals, analysis, and aural skills.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be a graduate music student in the Conservatory.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music History Review
catalog.description: Graduate-level review of music in Western civilization from antiquity to the present. Outside listening is required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: The Teaching Performer
catalog.description: The class will focus on teaching techniques for the performing musician, highlighting the advantages of becoming distinguished as a performer and a pedagogue. Premised on the synergistic relationship between teaching and performing, the class will provide a structure for clarifying the essential elements of teaching and musical artistry, and connecting them to such tangible situations as setting up a studio, teaching a master class, interviewing for a job, judging competitions, and recruiting students. The class will provide resources for individuals interested in being university applied faculty, music pedagogy teachers, and professionals looking to add effective teaching to their artistic repertoire.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Teaching and Learning in Music
catalog.description: This course explores the fundamental principles of music learning and provides opportunities for students to practice applying those principles to music teaching. Students will analyze their effectiveness at structuring meaningful learning experiences when teaching others in authentic settings (by analyzing videos from rehearsals, lessons, or classrooms) and when structuring learning experiences for themselves (by analyzing videos of practice).

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Systems and Strategies for Music Teaching
catalog.description: This course explores the philosophies and techniques of music teaching within authentic teaching contexts. Student will analyze their teaching efficacy, structure meaningful assessment strategies, and develop teaching techniques that produce sustained motivation and momentum for learners.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Independent Study
catalog.description: Intensive reading, research projects, creative work, or special performance in the student's major field, selected by the student in consultation with the appropriate faculty.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Master's Jazz Recital
catalog.description: Capstone Experience in the Master of Music in Performance -- Jazz emphasis degree.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Accompanying for Pianists
catalog.description: In-depth study of vocal and instrumental collaborative repertoire and techniques, through individually assigned projects with student partners in the Conservatory. Masterclass-style coaching and student input will facilitate the teaching of pedagogical principles in collaborative piano playing.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Studies in Music and Gender
catalog.description: Variable topics focusing on connections and intersections between music and gender; may include study of such topics in particular historical periods (e.g., Baroque, Classical), geographical locations, in specific areas of gender studies (e.g., queer studies, women in music), and/or noted musical works and composers.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Career Paths in Composition
catalog.description: This course is an introduction to career paths in composition. Two overlapping threads will be discussed which follow academic and entrepreneurial trajectories. Students will gain knowledge of aspects of college teaching, as well as aspects of freelance career building in composition.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate Composition Major in the Conservatory

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Stage Role Plus
catalog.description: This course is for the preparation and performance of a stage role in the operatic or musical theatre repertoire within UMKC Conservatory’s lyric theatre season.
catalog.prerequisites: Two semesters of CONSVTY 5116 ; Audition required

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Opera Workshop: Audition Techniques
catalog.description: Students will work on specific audition techniques for the operatic solo singer, which may include dramatic interpretation of repertoire, stage movement, resume building, and other aspects to assist the performer in the audition process.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a graduate student in the Conservatory to take this course.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Current Issues and Trends in American Music Theory
catalog.description: This course introduces graduate music majors to current issues and trends in American music theory. Through surveys of prominent journals, article reviews and presentations, class discussion, and a final research or review article, students will be introduced to the variety of music-theoretical subfields, learn about the types of questions music theorists explore, practice the conventions of academic writing, and explore the connections between music theory, music performance, teaching, and composition.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Topics in the Analysis of Popular Music
