catalog.description: Variable topics focusing on analytical approaches and methods for popular music and associated genres; may include study of topics in particular historical periods, genres, and/or noted musical works and composers/artists.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Theory Seminar in the Works of a Composer
catalog.description: Intensive analytical study of the music of a specific composer. Variable topic as selected by the instructor. May be repeated if a different topic.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Analytical Procedures
catalog.description: An introduction to recent methods of stylistic and formal analysis for tonal, post-tonal, and popular music repertoires.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Analysis II: 1600-1900
catalog.description: Theory and analysis of selected works from the 17th through the 19th century.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Analysis III: 20th Century to the Present
catalog.description: Theory and analysis of selected works from the late 19th century to the present.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Schenkerian Theory and Analysis
catalog.description: An introduction to the theories and analytic methodology of Heinrich Schenker (1868-1935).
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Tonal Counterpoint
catalog.description: Analysis and writing in tonal counterpoint based on the music of J.S. Bach, including composition in forms such as canon, invention and fugue.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Post-Tonal Theory
catalog.description: This course explores theoretical and analytical approaches to post-tonal music, including centricity, pitch-class, set theory, serialism, indeterminacy, and minimalism. Students will develop skills in analyzing post-tonal structures while considering aesthetic and compositional contexts.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Aspects of Time and Music
catalog.description: A course offering a broad-based, multi-disciplinary exploration of time preparatory to an in-depth study of some of music's primary temporal aspects; these focus on complex treatments of rhythm and meter in tonal music.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Orchestration
catalog.description: Analysis of advanced orchestration techniques with a focus on relatively recent music for large instrumental ensembles. Discussion of student works-in-progress for orchestra or wind ensemble.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Composition Seminar in the Works of a Composer or Genre
catalog.description: Intensive analytical and compositional study of a specific genre or compositional trend. Variable topic as selected by the instructor. May be repeated if a different topic.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Composition
catalog.description: Intensive work in advanced composition in the large forms for various vocal and instrumental ensembles and orchestra. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Electronic Music Composition
catalog.description: Creative, original composition of music in diverse styles utilizing the full range of equipment and techniques available. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Computer Music Language Study
catalog.description: This course is designed to fulfill the computer language option of the foreign language requirement for DMA students in composition. Focus will be on development and mastery of skills in computer languages specifically related to musical composition, such as MAX or Csound, or in compositional uses of more general languages such as html, C, and Lingo.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Electroacoustic Music Aesthetics and Analysis
catalog.description: An overview of the context and practice of electroacoustic music in two parts: 1) new aesthetic parameters of sonic composition made possible by technology; and 2) creating a cogent analysis of a work by developing individual, personalized analytical tools. Offered in rotation with CONSVTY 5534 and CONSVTY 5534B .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Improvisation in Music Therapy
catalog.description: This course is designed to learn, lead, and participate in the theory and practice of improvisation in music therapy for clients and therapists.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Administration of Music Therapy
catalog.description: This course is designed for the person who wishes to become a music therapy professor either entering into an existing program or starting one's own program. It also may be valuable to those considering academia or to be better informed about the academic process when dealing with music therapy programs.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Methods in Elementary Music
catalog.description: Organization and design of elementary music classes. Areas of study include methods, materials and program building.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Methods In Instrumental Music
catalog.description: Organization and rehearsal techniques of instrumental classes and performance ensembles Areas of study include methods, materials and program building.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Methods In Choral Music
catalog.description: Organization and rehearsal techniques of choral classes and performance ensembles. Areas of study include methods, materials and program building.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Theories and Practice of Music Therapy
catalog.description: This course addresses the history and development of the music therapy profession in the United States and other countries. This course is open to music therapy graduate students.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Clinical Supervision in Music Therapy
catalog.description: This course prepares the music therapist for clinical supervision of music therapy students across training levels and situations. The course includes both theoretical background on supervisee development, issues of clinical supervision, and practical application and skill development in the area of clinical supervision of music therapy students.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Psychology of Music
catalog.description: The study of psychological aspects of music including acoustical phenomena and factors affecting musical preference, perception and taste. A review of related literature and basic methodology for experimental investigation and quantification of related variables will be included.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Clinical Experience
catalog.description: This course provides the graduate student with board certification in music therapy an opportunity to refine and enhance current clinical skills and to develop individually specified American Music Therapy Association Advanced Level Competencies. Students will demonstrate the ability to integrate advanced competencies in musicianship, theory and clinical practice. Students will conform to the AMTA Code of Ethics and standards for Clinical Practice and the CBMT Scope of Practice. The course includes a weekly seminar and clinical rotations at a mutually agreed upon clinical facility.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar In Music Therapy
catalog.description: This course is designed to address relevant topics in the theory, practice and research of music therapy to promote an advanced level of practice in the music therapist. Topics will be based on faculty scholarship and advanced practice expertise, as well graduate student interest. Course structure will involve weekly meetings with the instructor and independent research and reading by the student.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Jazz Revolutions: A Historical Perspective
catalog.description: Jazz Revolutions surveys the styles and innovations of jazz musicians who are considered pioneers in the development of jazz. It then places those musicians in a rich cultural and musical context, showing the impact those innovators had on their contemporaries and the musical practices of today both inside and outside of jazz.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera History
catalog.description: The history of opera from its origins to the present.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Opera Literature
catalog.description: A survey of opera literature, opera synopsis, and operatic stagecraft from 1600 to present.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Musicology Seminar
catalog.description: This seminar focuses on an in-depth study of an issue, topic, or discourse related to music history and practice, engaging literature and methods across musicology and related fields. Variable topic as selected by the instructor. May be repeated if a different topic.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of the Medieval and Renaissance Eras
catalog.description: This course provides a stylistic and historical survey of music composed between about 400 and 1600, focusing on specific themes and trends that unite the period commonly known as the Medieval and Renaissance eras. Students will explore the place and function of music in pre- and early modern society, examine how sacred and secular music responded to the social, cultural, and religious transformations that occurred during this period, and learn strategies for aurally recognizing and distinguishing this music.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of the Medieval Era
catalog.description: Seminar in the music of the Middle Ages, from 800 to 1400.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Of The Renaissance
catalog.description: Seminar in the music of the Renaissance, from 1400 to 1600.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of the Baroque Era
catalog.description: Seminar in the music of the Baroque era, from 1600 to 1750.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of the Classical Era
catalog.description: Seminar in the music of the Classical era, from 1750 to 1828.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of the Romantic Era
catalog.description: Seminar in the music of the Romantic era from 1828 to 1914.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Since 1900: 1900-1945
catalog.description: Seminar in music from 1900 to 1945.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music Since 1900: 1945 to the Present
catalog.description: Seminar in music since 1945.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar: Choral Traditions in Western Music
catalog.description: This course examines the role of choral singing and choral music in the Western art music tradition, focusing specifically on the functions performed by various types of choirs throughout history.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar: Nationalism In Music
catalog.description: This course examines the relationship between music in the Western world and the large critical umbrella of “nationalism,” tracing how national identity (expressed through politics, religion, class and economics, social values, philosophy, and more) contributed to musical activity.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: American Musical Theater
catalog.description: A survey of trends in the American musical theater from the 18th century to the present.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music and Film
catalog.description: This course will survey the use of music in cinema. It will include sections on music, technology, the film medium and the various ways in which music adds to the cinematic experience.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of Asia
catalog.description: This course surveys music in East Asia, from historical styles to traditional music to contemporary composition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Music of Latin America
catalog.description: Survey of selected musical traditions (sacred and secular, fold, traditional, and concert music) and representative composers of Central and South America.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: History And Literature Of Chamber Music
catalog.description: A study of masterpieces of chamber literature, vocal and instrumental, from various periods, through research, listening, and performance.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Vocal Literature: French Melodies
catalog.description: In-depth study of the French melodies of Duparc, Faure, Debussy, Ravel, and Poulenc.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Vocal Literature: German Lieder
catalog.description: In-depth study of the German lieder of Schubert, Schumann, Brahms, Wolf, Mahler, and Strauss.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Vocal Literature: Nationalistic Art Songs
catalog.description: In-depth study of Nationalistic art songs of Russia, Scandinavia, Spain, and Middle Europe.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Vocal Literature: 20Th Century Amer & Engl Art Songs
catalog.description: In-depth study of the 20th Century American and English art songs.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Graduate Piano Literature Seminar
catalog.description: Advanced study of piano literature through research, analysis and performance. Topics will vary from semester to semester.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Collaborative Literature for Piano with Strings
catalog.description: Study of all forms of string repertoire involving collaboration with piano including sonatas, duos, short pieces and concerti. Instructor approval required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Collaborative Literature for Piano with Woodwinds and Brass
catalog.description: Study of all forms of woodwind and brass repertoire involving collaboration with piano including sonatas, duos, short pieces and concerti. Instructor approval required.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Contemporary Issues in Music Education
catalog.description: This course guides graduate students in exploration of philosophical and social/historical frameworks as a foundation for addressing opportunities and challenges as a music educator in contemporary American schools.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Professional Aspects Of College Teaching
catalog.description: Designed for graduate students planning a career in college teaching. Covers preparation of job application materials; presentation of a master class; interviews with a search committee and dean; faculty loads and evaluation procedures; tenure and rank, and relationships with students, colleagues and administrators.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Vocal Diction
catalog.description: This course is designed to review and hone diction skills in Italian, French, and German on the level of professional opera, recital, and oratorio performance; vocal literature is approached through the text with both reading and singing practice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research for Music Teachers
catalog.description: This course examines common practitioner-based research designs used by music educators. During this class, students will learn about and complete projects that utilize rigorous research design procedures and concepts.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Choral Conducting – Styles and Techniques, Masters Level
catalog.description: Students will learn advanced choral conducting techniques, rehearsal strategy, and performance practice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Choral Conducting – Styles and Techniques, Doctoral Level
catalog.description: Students will learn advanced choral conducting techniques, rehearsal strategy, and performance practice.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Choral Conducting - Style
catalog.description: A study of conducting problems of music of the Renaissance, Baroque, Classic, Romantic and Twentieth century; further examination of performance problems associated with choral performances of madrigals, chamber music, a cappella works and music utilizing advanced compositional techniques. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Choral Conducting-Rehearsal Techniques
catalog.description: An advanced study of methods and rehearsal procedures in the development and organization of choral performance; includes concepts of tone quality, diction, programming, and development of communication skills. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Instrumental Conducting
catalog.description: An introductory study of the techniques of instrumental conducting. An overview of conducting topics, including score preparation, rehearsal techniques and performance problems.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Instrumental Conducting - Orchestra
catalog.description: A further study of the techniques of instrumental conducting, including such topics as string techniques, performance practice, baton technique and the art of accompaniment.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Instrumental Conducting - Band
catalog.description: A further study of the technique of band conducting, including such topics as wind/percussion techniques, performance practice, baton technique, and contemporary wind chamber repertoire.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Designing Systematic Inquiry in Music Education
catalog.description: This course is designed to stimulate thinking about music education research and apply it to work in the music classroom. Students will read and synthesize research in music and human learning, and develop skills to apply empirical research to the classroom without overstating the findings. The course will culminate in a proposal for an academic portfolio project that demonstrates a potential to contribute to the field while being informed by published research in music education.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Descriptive Research in Music
catalog.description: This course examines common descriptive research designs and statistical concepts used by music therapists and music educators. During this class, students will learn about and complete projects that utilize nonparametric and parametric statistical tests.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar In Orchestral Literature
catalog.description: Advanced study of a variety of styles, periods, and analytical procedures encountered by orchestral conductors. Content will vary from semester to semester. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar In Wind/Band Literature
catalog.description: Advanced study of a variety of styles, periods, and analytical procedures encountered by instrumental conductors of wind ensembles/bands. Content will vary from semester to semester. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Seminar In Choral Literature
catalog.description: Each seminar is concerned with the conductor's viewpoint of a segment of the literature from the specified historical periods and styles, and explores the analysis, interpretation, historical context, and conducting problems of that literature. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Academic Portfolio
catalog.description: Creative synthesis of coursework or clinical experience resulting in original products such as research documents, pedagogical materials, technology applications, music compositions or arrangements, and musical improvisation applications. Portfolio item may not include materials used to meet admission requirements. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Academic Portfolio II
catalog.description: Additional coursework or clinical experience resulting in original products.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: A seminar in selected topics in various fields and idioms of music. May be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Special Topics

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Special Topics

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Special Topics

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Special Topics

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Special Topics

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Group Piano Pedagogy
catalog.description: Study of teaching techniques and materials related to teaching group piano at the college level. Course responsibilities include both observation and supervised teaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Pedagogy of Music Theory
catalog.description: Study and application of methods, philosophies, materials and current trends in music theory pedagogy. Students engage in supervised teaching, research projects, and observations of music theory faculty.
catalog.prerequisites: Graduate music students in the Conservatory who have passed the theory matriculation exam or equivalent and CONSVTY 5523 .

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Pedagogy I-General
catalog.description: An overview of basic pedagogical practice including modes of instruction, feedback, reinforcement, and assessment. Students will review current literature in this area and develop a project related to their own teaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Pedagogy of Music History
catalog.description: Techniques and materials related to teaching music history and music appreciation combined with supervised teaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Pedagogy of Instrumental Music
catalog.description: A study of the pedagogical materials and methods used in teaching applied instrumental music.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Piano Pedagogy
catalog.description: Study of teaching techniques and materials related to teaching applied piano at the collegiate level. Course responsibilities include both observation and supervised teaching.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction To Research And Bibliography In Music
catalog.description: A survey of procedure in bibliography, research, and scholarly writing.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Introduction to Research and Bibliography in Music
catalog.description: A survey of procedures in bibliography, research, and scholarly writing.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research and Analysis in Music and Behavior
catalog.description: This course provides students with an introduction to research in music and human behavior. Course topics include literature review, proposal writing, design, data analysis and scholarly writing styles used in music research.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research Applications in Music and Behavior
catalog.description: Further study in the area of research in music and behavior. Data gathering procedures specific to music, research ethics in music, preparation for publishing in music journals and in-depth critiques of important literature in music education, music therapy and performance are addressed.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Master's Recital
catalog.description: Preparation and presentation of a public solo or ensemble recital demonstrating advanced performance skills and interpretive maturity. Students will design and perform a recital program approved by their applied faculty and/or area committee. The recital serves as a capstone experience for the degree and reflects the student’s artistic growth.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research Problems
catalog.description: Individual study with a member of the graduate faculty that will culminate in a final project. The project must be completed within two consecutive semesters, submitted to and graded by the supervising professor, and submitted to the Associate Dean of Graduate Studies for archiving.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research Problems In Computer Languages And Music
catalog.description: Individual study with a member of the adjunct, associate, or graduate faculty. Study will culminate in the production of a project (computer program, CD-ROM,composition, or other document) that demonstrates skills in computer languages specifically related to music. This course fulfills the computer language option of the foreign language for DMA students in composition.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Advanced Research and Bibliography In Music
catalog.description: Advanced procedures in bibliography, research, and scholarly writing.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Practicum In Music Education
catalog.description: Individual conference course requiring the development of a research paper in a special subject and designed to resolve a practical problem of special interest to the student. Conference.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Recital
catalog.description: Preparation and presentation of a public solo or ensemble recital demonstrating advanced performance skills and interpretive maturity. Students will design and perform a recital program approved by their applied faculty and/or area committee. The recital serves as a capstone experience for the degree and reflects the student’s artistic growth beyond the master's level.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Conducting Performance Paper
catalog.description: Individual study with the student's conducting teacher. Study will culminate in the writing of a formal paper addressing aspects of a doctoral conducting performance.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Additional Doctoral Recital
catalog.description: The additional doctoral recital is supervised by the applied professor. The recital is graded in the same manner as other recitals for the Performance degree and can count for one doctoral research point.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Recital Paper II
catalog.description: Additional individual study with the student's applied teacher. Study will culminate in the writing of another formal paper addressing aspects of a doctoral recital.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Conducting Performance Paper
catalog.description: Additional individual study with the student's conducting teacher. Study will culminate in the writing of another formal paper addressing aspects of a doctoral conducting performance.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Recital Paper
catalog.description: Individual study with the student's applied teacher. Study will culminate in the writing of a formal paper addressing aspects of a doctoral recital.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Research Problems
catalog.description: Individual study with a member of the adjunct, associate, graduate or doctoral faculty. Study will culminate in the writing of a scholarly paper.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Research Problems II
catalog.description: Additional study with a member of the adjunct, associate, graduate or doctoral faculty. Study will culminate in the writing of another scholarly paper.

catalog.subject: CONSVTY
catalog.title: Doctoral Music Product
catalog.description: Individual study with a member of the adjunct, associate, graduate, or doctoral faculty. Study will culminate in the writing of a creative, original composition, arrangement or edition of music.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Introduction To Professional Counseling
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the professions of counseling and counseling psychology as practiced in a variety of settings. The course provides and overview of basic concepts of mental health, client problems, history of the profession, ethical and professional standards, counseling in a multicultural and pluralistic society, and licensure and credentialing. The course also orients students to the counseling program at UMKC. May be taken prior to admission.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Fndtns Of Elementary & Secondary School Counseling
catalog.description: The course will present an overview of theory and practice in the field of school counseling and will examine the roles and functions of school counselors. For School Counseling Emphasis only.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Diagnosing and Treatment Planning
catalog.description: This course covers psychological disorders and other reactions in clients encountered by counselors and psychologists in contemporary psychological service systems. The course focuses on learning current diagnostic criteria, making differential diagnosis, and evidence- based treatment planning. Attention will also be given to the influence of culture on behavior and treatment.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: School Counseling Programs
catalog.description: This course will provide knowledge and skills in the development and management of comprehensive school counseling programs, including program planning, implementing and evaluation.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Career Development I
catalog.description: Theories of career development and vocational choice and their implications in counseling. Emphasizes knowledge of occupational and career information sources and use of these data by counselors and counseling psychologists. Open to any student who has been admitted to an advanced degree program.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Lifespan Human Development
catalog.description: This course examines theories and research related to biological, cognitive, and social development across the lifespan within the layers of the multidimensional context of people's lives. Special attention is given to the role of social class, gender, ethnicity, and culture in development.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Assessment Methods In Professional Counseling
catalog.description: This course provides an understanding of assessment process and assessment techniques. Students will develop skills in selection, administration, and interpretation of representative assessment instruments.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Theories of Counseling
catalog.description: Theoretical positions in counseling; significance of these theories in professional practice. To be taken prior to CPCE 5531 .

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Special Counseling Methods - Substance Abuse
catalog.description: Theories and methods of counseling as applied to clients with substance abuse problems. Includes assessment, treatment strategies, and evaluation. Skills practice in implementing methods.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Theory And Methods Of Sexual Counseling
catalog.description: The focus of this course is on sexual development and the acquisition of therapeutic skills to work with problems relating to human sexual functioning and sexual dysfunctions.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Introduction to Play Therapy
catalog.description: Course covers the philosophy and rationale for using play media in counseling with children and the history of play therapy. The client-centered theoretical approach will be examined with an emphasis on creating and maintaining a relationship with the child that allows for the effective use of play media.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Skills for Counseling and Psychotherapy
catalog.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the fundamental concepts and methods of counseling and psychotherapy. Students will apply ethical and multicultural principles to the helping relationship while learning the basic methods of humanistic, psychodynamic, and cognitive behavioral approaches as they relate to the helping process. A main focus of this course is the acquisition of basic helping skills. Students will also become familiar with counseling and therapy outcome research, and they will develop self-awareness and an ability to evaluate their skills as counselors/clinicians.
catalog.prerequisites: Admitted to the Clinical Psychology PhD program OR Counseling MA students must have co- or pre-req of CPCE 5520 .

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Counseling Practicum I
catalog.description: Closely supervised therapeutic counseling with individuals; translation of theory into practice; clinical and professional techniques and issues.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Counseling Practicum II
catalog.description: Supervised therapeutic counseling with individuals and consultation in professional settings.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Couples And Family Therapy Practicum
catalog.description: Supervised application of theories and methods of family therapy with individuals, couples and families.
catalog.prerequisites: CPCE 5531 and CPCE 5542 ; and CPCE 5551 and CPCE 5541 (or co-requisites).

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: School Counseling Practicum
catalog.description: This course is the school counseling practica and as such is focused on skill development, case conceptualization, and effective practice in the delivery of direct and indirect school counseling services in the K-12 school setting.
catalog.prerequisites: CPCE 5530 & CPCE 5553 (pre or co-), CPCE 5502 & EDUC-C&I 5517 (for students who are not certified teachers)

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Continuing Counseling Practicum
catalog.description: Supervised therapeutic counseling with individuals.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Theories And Methods In Group Counseling
catalog.description: Theories and research in group counseling, including knowledge and skills in establishing and maintaining a counseling group; effective group leadership; therapeutic factors in groups; strategies for group development; and ethical and multicultural considerations in group work. Requires participation in a professional growth group.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Couples And Family Therapy
catalog.description: Introduction to family relationships and the application of life cycle stages to working with couples and families. Focus also includes the study of a range of family configurations and issues with attention to diversity.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Theories and Techniques of Family Systems Therapy
catalog.description: A study of major family systems theories and their applied practices in family therapy. Students will develop skills in family assessment techniques and family therapy processes.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Psychology of Stress and Trauma
catalog.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the psychology of stress and trauma. Students will learn about the effects of stress and trauma, as well as counseling interventions that address the effects of stress and trauma. Specifically, students will learn about vicarious trauma, the psychophysiology of stress and trauma, diagnostic and assessment-related issues with stress and trauma, therapeutic approaches to working with trauma survivors, multicultural and social justice considerations, and trauma therapy as applied to specific populations.
catalog.prerequisites: CPCE 5500 or admission into psychology doctoral program or departmental consent.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Suicide Prevention
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide students with an understanding of suicide prevention from the perspective of a counselor. The major focus of the course will be on learning assessment and treatment strategies. Attention will also be given to statistics and research related to suicide. In addition, ethical considerations and common symptoms, experiences, and co-occurring disorders will be discussed.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Organization And Administration Of Counseling Programs
catalog.description: Organization, administration, and planning of counseling programs with emphasis on their practical aspect; counseling practice in schools and agencies; intraprofessional relationships; legal and ethical considerations. Course to be taken near completion of the master's program.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Counseling in a Pluralistic Society
catalog.description: Addresses the needs of diverse populations served by counselors and addresses developing intervention methods of working with these populations. Focuses on advocacy and change agent roles of counselors.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Ethics And Professional Issues In Counseling
catalog.description: This course is designed to examine the major ethical and professional issues within the counseling profession. More specific, ethical dilemmas and professional issues relevant to the practice of mental health, marriage and family, school and substance abuse counseling are the major foci of this course. In addition, instruction is designed to enhance student understanding of the ethical standards such that students can effectively apply the critical thinking necessary to practice ethical behavior with clients, professional colleagues, consultees, and the communities in which they work.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Internship in Counseling
catalog.description: This course is designed for MA students on internship. Internship in Counseling provides students with the opportunity to practice counseling and function professionally in a counseling setting, as well as become aware about the many issues encountered by professional counselors. This course also offers students the opportunity to discuss and examine their experiences, which will require them to think reflectively about a wide range of counseling issues, including human and cultural diversity in this field.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Internship In Counseling I
catalog.description: First semester of a sequence of applied experiences in a planned, supervised program. Seminar accompanies internship experiences.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Internship In Counseling II
catalog.description: Second semester of a sequence of applied experiences in a planned, supervised program. Seminar accompanies internship experiences.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: School Counseling Internship
catalog.description: This class is a supervised internship in a school setting. Students have the opportunity to strengthen their skills and mature in their understanding and practice of professional school counseling.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: A course designed to deal with a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors, and prerequisites to be listed in the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Prevention, Consultation, and Program Evaluation in Community Settings
catalog.description: Course provides an overview of mental health consultation and collaboration in community settings. Models and theories of consultation and considerations for ethical practice in diverse settings are reviewed. The course also introduces prevention and program development and evaluation as roles for professional counselors. The course will briefly review the history of prevention, and allow students to develop a prevention program for a population of interest.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Individual Studies
catalog.description: Review of the research and trends relative to selected problems.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Research And Thesis
catalog.description: Research and Thesis

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Objective Personality Assessment
catalog.description: This course is designed to help students develop knowledge and skills related to the selection, administration, and interpretation of some representative objective personality assessment instruments used in counseling/clinical settings. Students will also learn to integrate data obtained from an assessment battery to write comprehensive psychological reports.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Survey Of Research In Counseling Psychology
catalog.description: Survey of significant research in counseling psychology. Critical evaluation of research procedures, instrumentation, and clinical application of results.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Advanced Counseling Practicum
catalog.description: Advanced supervised therapeutic counseling with individuals and supervised consultation in clinical settings.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Assessment Practicum
catalog.description: The practicum for assessment of children, adolescents, and adults covers the administration of psychological evaluations and includes maintaining a caseload of assessment evaluations. Specialized assessment evaluations and conceptualization issues as well as special topics are covered, with evaluations for ADHD and learning disorders emphasized.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Continuing Advanced Counseling Practicum
catalog.description: Supervised therapeutic counseling with individuals, beyond the advanced level.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Supervision Practicum
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide students with an opportunity to practice supervision. Students will be assigned 2 to 3 counselors-in-training from a CPCE 5531 and CPCE 5532 practicum class to supervise over the course of a semester. The practicum instructor will provide weekly supervision.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Internship In Counseling Psychology
catalog.description: Applied experiences in a professional setting under supervision of licensed psychologists.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Special Problems
catalog.description: Individual studies; thesis exploration; special reading.

catalog.subject: CPCE
catalog.title: Research And Dissertation
catalog.description: Research and Dissertation.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Network Architecture I
catalog.description: This course provides an introduction to fundamental concepts and principles in the design and implementation of computer communication networks, their protocols, and architectures. Topics to be covered include: layering, and addressing, naming, routing, internetworking, Internet protocols, reliable transfer, congestion control, link control, multiple media access, and network measurement and management.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Network Architecture II
catalog.description: In this course, advanced principles, protocols, and architectures of computer networks will be studied with specific emphasis on emerging technologies. The focus will be on the latest networking protocol designs with particular attention to the TCP/IP and application layers.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Network Routing
catalog.description: Algorithms, protocols and analysis for network routing. Routing in different networks such as circuit-switched networks, Internet, broadband networks, and transmission networks are covered.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: This course is intended to allow faculty and visiting scholars to offer special courses in selected topics.
catalog.prerequisites: Prerequisite: You must be in the School of Science and Engineering Graduate program.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Advanced Special Topics
catalog.description: A lecture course presenting advanced research level topics. This course is intended to allow faculty and visiting scholars to offer special courses in selected research areas.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Directed Readings
catalog.description: Readings in an area selected by the doctoral student in consultation with a doctoral faculty member. Arrangements must be made prior to registration.
catalog.prerequisites: Prerequisite: You must be in the School of Science and Engineering Graduate program.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Research and Dissertation Research in Telecommunications and Computer Networking
catalog.description: Doctoral Research in Telecommunications and Computer Networking.

catalog.subject: CSEE
catalog.title: Required Graduate Enrollment
catalog.description: Required Graduate Enrollment.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Analysis of Movement
catalog.description: This course in movement analysis will explore various aspects of modern dance. The topics that will be introduced are related to: the differences between ballet vocabulary and modern dance vocabulary, the reason and method behind the creation of modern dance, codified modern dance techniques versus non-codified modern dance techniques, Laban Movement Analysis, the principles of the Graham technique versus folding/unfolding, the Doris Humphreys technique and Lester Horton’s fortification. Class discussions, readings, and examples of various works will be used to analyze these topics. Basic improvisational techniques will be utilized to explore these topics.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Pedagogy and Analysis
catalog.description: A study of ballet pedagogy, the structure of classical ballet steps, and analysis of movement including basic anatomy, vocabulary and the aesthetics of ballet.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique and Theory I
catalog.description: Fundamentals of technique of classical ballet at the intermediate level with attention given to strengthening, stretching, anatomical alignment, and developing the ballet aesthetic. This course includes pointe work. Non-Majors by audition.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique and Theory I
catalog.description: This intermediate level dance course is based on the technique and theory of Lester Horton and fundamental elements of Martha Graham. Designed to fortify, stretch, and strengthen the body, the technique is codified into a series of studies designed to cover a wide range of movement vocabulary. Non-Majors by audition.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 141B .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique and Theory II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 141M .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Men's Class I
catalog.description: This course is designed to meet the needs of the male dancer and will focus on developing the technique, strength, and agility needed for a professional career.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Men's Class II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 213C .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Composition I
catalog.description: An introduction to dance composition focused on the exploration of improvisation, spatial design, sources of movement, and the basic elements of space, time, shape, and motion with additional emphasis on dynamics, rhythm, and sound sources for choreography. With these skills, students are building a foundation and developing tools in creating choreography.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Composition II
catalog.description: Continuation of Composition I, further exploring of the fundamentals of choreography including locomotion studies, categories of motion, axial movement and sequential and non-sequeter movement. Focusing on the development of solo works and developing choreographic process.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Composition III
catalog.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of choreography, including the development of dance compositions through the exploration and definition of specific studies, including floor design, shape design, motion design, and time design. Restricted to dance majors.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory III
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 142B at the intermediate/advanced level including pointe. Restricted to dance majors.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique And Theory III
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 142M , on the intermediate/advanced level. Restricted to dance majors.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory IV
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 241B , at the intermediate/advanced level including pointe work.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Technique And Theory IV
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 142M , on the intermediate/advanced level.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Jazz
catalog.description: A study of Western Theatrical Dance focusing on Jazz and Afrp-Caribbean based forms.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Dance Science and Kinesiology
catalog.description: Dance Science and Kinesiology is a study of the body which relates specifically to the needs of dancers. Emphasis is placed upon an understanding of the skeletal system, the muscular system, their specific importance to dance technique, kinesiology, and dance injuries and prevention.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Pilates
catalog.description: A non-impact body conditioning method based on principles of abdominal and scapular stabilization. Introduction to the essential and intermediate mat work, which consists of non-weight bearing exercises. Designed to give the student an understanding of the principles and muscular emphasis behind the Pilates method. Proper alignment, full range of motion, and patterned breathing will be emphasized.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Fundamentals of Body Alignment and Pilates
catalog.description: A course that is designed for students to develop a greater understanding of body alignment and how to strengthen body alignment through muscular conditioning and Pilates. Non-impact body conditioning exercises that focus on proper alignment, full range of motion, muscular strengthening, core strengthening, muscular imbalances, patterned breathing, and injury prevention will be emphasized. Developing total body strength, alignment, and flexibility through a series of researched dance specific exercises that are carefully designed to reach all muscle groups are presented.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: History Of Dance I
catalog.description: A study of the development of Western theatrical dance forms, from its roots in the European court through the 20th century. Beginning with a brief overview of 'early dance,' emphasis will be placed on the study of Renaissance theatre spectacles to the rise of the professional dancer culminating with the 20th century contemporary ballet. This course includes outside reading and writing intensive requirements.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: History Of Dance II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 305 exploring the development of dance as a 20th century Western theatre dance form. Development of modern dance, modern dance pioneers, modern dance development in Europe, African-American contribution to modern dance, modern dance influence on the ballet and the Avant-Garde and Post Modern movements will be studied. Outside reading and writing intensive requirements included.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Conservatory Dance Ensemble
catalog.description: A course designed for the performance component of the BFA degree. Students develop and refine professional performance skills through a diverse repertory of choreographic works and backstage theatre activities. All aspects of a complete performance experience including rehearsals, backstage operations, crew activities, sound operation, stage management, costume management, videography, and company class are developed, culminating with fully produced theater performances, special projects, collaborations, and lecture demonstrations.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Partnering/Pas De Deux I
catalog.description: This course is designed to meet the needs of the 300/400 level ballet student and will teach the elementary skills of partnering such as turns, lifts, promenades, and balances.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Partnering/Pas De Deux II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 313A .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Composition IV
catalog.description: In this course, students will cover varying strategies and methodologies for choreographing on groups of dancers and collaborating with composers. Essential elements of form and structure will underlie all choreographic investigations, as will the connections of these formal subjects to content and meaning.
catalog.prerequisites: DANCE 218B (with a grade of C or better).

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Advanced Choreographic Design
catalog.description: In this course, students will cover varying strategies and methodologies for choreographing on groups of dancers and collaborating with composers. Essential elements of form and structure will underlie all choreographic investigations, as will the connections of these formal subjects to content and meaning.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory V
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 242B , at the advanced level including pointe work. Restricted to dance majors. Repeatable up to 6 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique And Theory V
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 242M on the advanced level. Restricted to dance majors. Repeatable up to 6 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory VI
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 341B . Repeatable up to 6 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique And Theory VI
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 341M . Repeatable up to 6 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Dance Technique Non-Majors
catalog.description: The applied and theoretical study of dance including traditional dance vocabulary.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Repertory I
catalog.description: Modern Dance Repertory is an advanced course for modern dance majors to study and perform the repertoire and works of renowned contemporary choreographers. It is a parallel to the Ballet Variations course which teaches the repertoire of ballet master works.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Repertory II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 405A .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Repertory III
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 405B .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Repertory IV
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 405C .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Advanced Pas De Deux I
catalog.description: Advanced pas de deux is designed to meet the needs of the 400 level ballet student with emphasis placed on perfecting advanced partnering skills. Students will have opportunity to learn pas de deux from great ballets giving students the experience and stamina of dancing entire pas de deuxs. The course provides coaching on both a stylistic approach and a technical approach to the performance of materials presented in class.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Advanced Pas De Deux II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 413A .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Men's Variations I
catalog.description: Men's Variations is designed for the male ballet dancer. Students will have the opportunity to learn and perform renowned variations from the Romantic, Classical, and Neo-Classical periods of ballet. This class will give the male student a true professional coaching experience in their training as they prepare for stage.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Men's Variations II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 414A .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Variations I
catalog.description: Variations is designed for the 400 level ballet student. The course will teach female variations to the pre-professional student. Students will have the opportunity to learn and perform renowned variations from Romantic, Classical and Neo-Classical periods of ballet. Students will also work in traditional practice tutus/costumes in order to give them a true professional experience in their training as they prepare for the stage.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Variations II
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 415A .

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Dance Forms I
catalog.description: Dance Forms I is a two-part course that allows a more diverse study of dance technique styles. The first portion of this course is the study of Hip Hop. Emphasis is placed on Hip Hop vocabulary, style, and culture. The second portion of the course offers Contemporary Dance based on the techniques of ballet and modern movement using collective information as a tool to apply movement investigation.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Dance Forms II
catalog.description: Dance Forms II is a continuation of Dance Forms I offering another two-part course that allows a more diverse study of dance technique styles. The first portion of this course is the study of dances from the African Diaspora, based movement of dances from Continental Africa, the Caribbean, and the Americas. The second portion of the course is Acting for Dancers, which explores imaginative means of communication through purely physical terms.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory VII
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 342B at the pre-professional level including pre-professional pointe work. Restricted to dance majors. Repeatable up to 9 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique And Theory VII
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 342M at the pre-professional level. Additionally, this course is designed to prepare the student for auditioning and acquiring a performing career. Longer combinations with an emphasis on quick retention of material presented in class will be stressed. Restricted to dance majors. Repeatable up to 9 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Ballet Technique And Theory VIII
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 441B , on the pre-professional level including pre-professional pointe work. Repeatable up to 9 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Modern Dance Technique And Theory VIII
catalog.description: Continuation of DANCE 441M on the pre-professional level. Repeatable up to 9 credit hours.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Senior Capstone Project I
catalog.description: The first semester of the Senior Capstone Project includes planning, organization, and preparation of the final senior project of performance and choreography. Utilization of production techniques, creation or selection of repertoire of a solo work, and beginning the creation of original choreographic work in group form utilizing the tools previously developed from the student's work in composition will be presented during two scheduled showings during the semester. Recommended preparation: DANCE 319B and appropriate technique levels.

catalog.subject: DANCE
catalog.title: Senior Capstone Project II
catalog.description: A continuation of DANCE 493 , the second semester of the Senior Capstone Project, is the culmination and juried public performance of a fully produced concert on the main stage to fulfill the requirements of the BFA in Dance. The student will present an original choreographic group work. In addition, the student will perform in two different dance idioms; including a solo that is self-choreographed or an approved masterwork.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Operative Dentistry I Lecture
catalog.description: An introduction to the prevention and principles of the restorative treatment of dental caries.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Operative Dentistry I Laboratory
catalog.description: Restorative procedures discussed in DENT 6305 are performed on laboratory manikins.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Transitions: Charting Your Professional Future I
catalog.description: This course is the first in a sequence of courses throughout the dental education curriculum designed to prepare the graduate dentist in the knowledge, skills and values of ethics, professionalism and practice management. The courses use self-assessment and strategic planning as foundations and lead the students through identification of personal and professional aspirations, and culminate in building each student's competence in dental practice management.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Transitions: Charting Your Professional Future II
catalog.description: This course is the second in a sequence of courses throughout the dental education curriculum designed to prepare the graduate dentist in the skills and values of professionalism, practice management and ethics. This course builds on strategic planning foundation to gain an understanding of personal financial management in the context of personal and professional goals in the field of dentistry.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Patient Care I
catalog.description: This course introduces the dental student to the foundation knowledge and skills and values for the provision of oral health care. This includes infection control, cubicle set-up and breakdown, dental assisting, patient/operator positioning, patient vital signs, radiographic techniques, patient communication and basic concepts of oral health and disease. Students will assist third and fourth year students in various clinical areas after appropriate preparation, and will provide oral hygiene instruction for elementary age students.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Dental Behavioral Science
catalog.description: An introduction to the basic principles of behavioral science as they relate to oral self-care and professional practice. Topics include basic principles of human behavior, adherence, motivational interviewing, dental fears, chronic orofacial pain, and conflict management. Students will complete an in-depth motivational case report and a communication competency exam with selected patients.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Applied Biochemistry
catalog.description: This is a course geared to the biomedical foundation knowledge of dental students. The course is composed of six sections focused on clinically important topic areas each culminating with a clinical presentation. Course content will intentionally emphasize new knowledge areas in cancer, inflammation, genetic diseases, metabolic diseases, mineralized tissues in health and disease, oral health, hormone action, and blood coagulation/wound healing.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Patient Care II
catalog.description: This course builds on the skills introduced in DENT 6310C with a review and the continuation of the clinical rotations. In addition, students will learn the steps of a basic oral diagnosis, and will demonstrate their understanding with graded peer exams and by performing selected portions of a diagnosis on two clinic patients with the assistance of a 3rd or 4th year dental student.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Patient Care III
catalog.description: This course introduces preventive theory necessary to provide patient care. Students are introduced to fundamental clinical procedures including dental deposits, gingival assessment, identification and classification of periodontal diseases, and periodontal probing. The information learned in this course continues in fall, second year (Patient Care IV) where student are introduced to basic periodontal instrumentation skills to assess and treat simple patients.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Dental Morphology
catalog.description: The Dental Morphology lecture/laboratory course introduces the student to the anatomy of the oral cavity and structures of the stomatognathic system. A thorough review of dental anatomy and dental terminology of the primary and permanent dentition is presented. The students' knowledge of dental morphology is reinforced by constructing wax models of the permanent dentition.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Fundamentals of Occlusion and Fixed Prosthodontics
catalog.description: This lecture & laboratory course will review the fundamental principles of dental occlusion, the anatomy and function of the stomatognathic system, and foundational knowledge of fixed prosthodontics.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Ethics and Professionalism
catalog.description: An introduction to basic concepts of ethics and professionalism. Systems of ethical decision making are introduced and applied in the context of oral health care and interprofessional practice. Students will explore their own ethical values and apply this knowledge to issues in professional education.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Clinical Decision Making in Dentistry
catalog.description: An experiential course that uses current controversies to facilitate development of skills needed for making valid decision in clinical dentistry. Students will apply basic principles of database searching, research design and methodology to the critical analysis of contemporary dental literature. This one-hour course will: 1) Provide the student with training to perform successfully on the portions of the national boards that deal with research design and methodology; and , 2) give the student skills sufficient to search for, locate, and evaluate valid information related to clinical questions in contemporary dentistry.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Introduction To The Histopathology Of Oral Tissues
catalog.description: A comparison of the microscopic anatomy of healthy and diseased oral tissues.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Patient Care IV
catalog.description: Students will apply skills and didactic knowledge learned in previous lecture and lab courses to a clinical setting. Students will perform dental procedures in a clinic-based project to further enhance their clinical skills. The students will have multiple patient-based experiences, which may include recall exams, oral health risk screenings, prophylaxis, and operative procedures. This course will prepare the student to transition to patient care.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Wellness Strategies and Practice for Dental Professionals
catalog.description: Dental students will obtain social, cognitive and emotional knowledge and skills to effectively navigate an academically rigorous environment. Students will learn basic theories for stress management, explore interventions for stress management and engage in the practice of intervention skills. Students will benefit from behavior modification techniques gained in the course and be able to transfer those skills to enhance communication and interpersonal interactions during patient care.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Dental Research Experience
catalog.description: This mentored study course focuses upon experience gained in both an area of dental research as well as the process of research in working with an established dental researcher.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Transitions: Charting Your Professional Future III
catalog.description: This course is the third in a sequence of courses throughout the dental education curriculum designed to prepare the graduate dentist in the skills and values of professionalism, practice management and ethics. This course builds on strategic planning foundation established in year one to gain an understanding planning for development of a dental practice.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Transitions: Charting Your Professional Future IV
catalog.description: This course is the fourth in a sequence of courses throughout the dental education curriculum designed to prepare the graduate dentist in the skills and values of professionalism, practice management and ethics. This course continues the strategic planning framework as the dental practice business plan is developed. The focus for this course is on managing the finances of a dental practice.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Operative Dentistry II Lecture
catalog.description: A continuation of DENT 6305 . Principles of cavity preparation, materials and techniques are stressed.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Operative Dentistry II Laboratory
catalog.description: A continuation of DENT 6305L . Restorative procedures are performed on laboratory manikins and extracted teeth.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Advanced Restorative Dentistry I
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the materials, procedures, and concepts to aesthetically optimize a patient's oral health and function within the context of comprehensive person-centered care. This includes evaluation of the patient from diagnosis, treatment planning, and treatment options utilizing traditional and digital dentistry with emphasis on the importance of patient diversity, values, norms, and goals.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Introduction to Oral Surgery & Pain Management I
catalog.description: This course introduces students to foundational concepts of oral surgery and pain management. The course consists of lectures, demonstration and pre-clinical practice and simulation in the safe and effective use of local anesthetics in dentistry and basic intraoral surgical procedures. This course includes patient assessment for intraoral procedures, and instrumentation and techniques required to anesthetize a patient and extract teeth. Students will participate in practical experiences to begin to build skills in the necessary techniques to manage patient’s pain and perform basic surgical procedures.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Pathology I Lecture
catalog.description: The general etiology of disease; circulatory and metabolic disorders; degenerative processes; inflammation; infection and immunity; tumors; and organ system pathology.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Pathology II
catalog.description: A study of developmental defects, inflammatory diseases, and neoplasia of the oral region.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Complete Removable Prosthodontics
catalog.description: This course will introduce the dental student to concepts and procedures involved in the rehabilitation of the completely edentulous patient. Information presented will include proper clinical examination techniques, an evaluation of the findings and their impact on treatment and treatment options. The student will become familiar with the clinical steps involved in the fabrication of complete dentures and the rationale supporting these procedures. Laboratory steps as they relate to clinical treatment procedures will also be discussed. There will be additional information presented regarding single complete dentures, immediate dentures, overdentures, implant-retained complete dentures, and rebasing and relining techniques.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Complete Removable Prosthodontics I Laboratory
catalog.description: Students are introduced to laboratory and clinical steps in the fabrication of complete dentures. Students learn the use and manipulation of dental materials associated with complete removable prosthetics. Clinical experiences involve the fabrication of a complete set of dentures for a clinic patient under faculty supervision. Foundational knowledge and skills are practiced leading to clinical competency.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Removable Partial Prosthodontics
catalog.description: The study of the terminology, design, theory, and basic procedures in removable partial denture construction in addition to diagnosis and treatment planning will be stressed through the lectures.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Removable Partial Prosthodontics Laboratory
catalog.description: In the laboratory the students will learn to plan, design, and prepare the mouth for a prosthesis. They will demonstrate understanding of concepts and methods by applying them to the solution of problems. The student will: develop critical thinking and problem solving related to diagnosis, planning and treatment; make decisions based on current empirical and published evidence; make custom trays for final impression, and record bases and wax rims for recording jaw relationship.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Periodontics I
catalog.description: Basic disease mechanisms involved in the evolution of the inflammatory periodontal lesion, i.e., the interaction of the host tissues with the oral microbial flora are introduced. The full range of periodontal and peri implant conditions are covered. The course reinforces the science of periodontology and its relationship to the clinical practice of periodontics. Students gain an understanding of the basic knowledge of periodontics, the foundation of subsequent courses addressing anti-infective and surgical therapies, and periodontal/restorative dentistry relationships.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Fixed Prosthodontics I Lecture
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide the foundation knowledge needed by the novice to formulate clinical judgments in the areas of treatment planning, tooth preparation, and the selection and use of dental biomaterials for the restoration of single teeth with fixed prosthodontic restorations. The topics covered also include provisional restorations, impressions materials and technique, dental cements, and laboratory aspects involved in the fabrication of cast gold crowns.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Fixed Prosthodontics I Laboratory
catalog.description: The second course in the fixed prosthodontic curriculum is designed to provide foundation knowledge needed by the novice to formulate clinical judgments in the areas of treatment planning, tooth preparation, and the selection and use of dental biomaterials for the restoration of missing teeth with fixed partial dentures and implants.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Fixed Prosthodontics II Lecture
catalog.description: The second course in the fixed prosthodontic curriculum is designed to provide foundation knowledge needed by the novice to formulate clinical judgments in the areas of treatment planning, tooth preparation, and the selection and use of dental biomaterials for the restoration of missing teeth with fixed partial dentures and implants.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Fixed Prosthodontics II Laboratory
catalog.description: The second laboratory course in fixed prosthodontics is focused on the replacement of missing teeth with fixed partial dentures and implant restoration. Projects build the skills to begin development of clinical competence in fixed partial dentures and implant restorations.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Dental Management of the Medically Complex Patient
catalog.description: This course focuses on the understanding of medical conditions and compromised states that patients present with, enabling the clinician to develop dental treatment plans that are safe and compatible with their medical status.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Oral Radiology Lecture
catalog.description: Radiation physics, radiation biology, quality assurance, imaging principles, radiation hygiene, radiographic interpretation and techniques of intra-oral survey are presented.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Pediatric Dentistry I Lecture
catalog.description: The overall goal of this didactic course is to provide the student with the fundamental knowledge necessary to provide comprehensive dental care to pediatric patients. In addition, this course strives to develop an attitude towards learning such that the student will seek opportunities to further his/her knowledge and skills in pediatric dentistry subsequent to graduation. Finally, this course is intended to sensitize students to their responsibility as health care providers for the children in their community.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Endodontics I Lecture
catalog.description: An introductory course in endodontics emphasizing pulp and periapical biology and pathology. Extra emphasis will be placed on endodontic diagnosis of non-odontogenic facial pain, problems with anesthesia in endodontics and treatment planning.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Orthodontics: Growth And Development
catalog.description: Certain malocclusions and dental deformities can occur due variations in growth and normal developmental process. In order to treat and understand these problems, an in-depth and through understanding of craniofacial growth and development is necessary. Understanding how and when the face and head is actively growing will enable the clinician to redirect facial growth to reduce the severity of forming skeletal/ dental malocclusions. Since orthodontic treatment may involve the modification and/ort manipulation of skeletal growth, it is important not only to understand dental development but also physical, physiologic and psychosocial development. This course is designed to address these needs.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Introduction to Oral Surgery & Pain Management II
catalog.description: This course builds on the fundamental concepts in oral surgery and pain management presented in Dent 6412 to prepare students for patient care in oral surgery and management of pain for provision of dental care. The lectures will focus on treatment needs of the medically compromised surgical patient, ability to safely and adequately deliver local anesthesia, non-pharmacological management of pain as well as OTC and prescription medications for pain management. The course will also focus on appropriate case selection for a general dentist. In the pre-clinical lab portion of the course, students will participate in exodontia simulation and local anesthesia administration.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Endodontics II Lecture
catalog.description: A continuation of the study of endodontics emphasizing non-surgical endodontics, surgical endodontics and post-endodontic treatment.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Endodontics Laboratory
catalog.description: The preparation and filling of root canals of extracted teeth in the laboratory setting.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Review of Pre-Clinical Dentistry
catalog.description: A combination of online lectures, selected readings and independent study designed to reinforce and integrate concepts contained in the pre-clinical dental curriculum.

catalog.subject: DENT
catalog.title: Intro to Comprehensive Patient Care
catalog.description: The purpose of this course is to introduce the student to the clinical environment and to familiarize him/her with comprehensive patient care. In addition, it allows the student to develop and interpret basic diagnostic aids that enable him/her to arrive at a diagnosis and treatment outline, the beginning steps of comprehensive care. Patient care is provided following the outlined treatment plan. The student will apply the principles/concepts of patient care.
