Graduate students will be assigned a specific research paper.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Environment, Resources And Economic Growth
catalog.description: This course focuses on the theory and policy issues involved in resource recreation and depletion; environmental destruction, preservation and recreation; and the interrelation of these problems of and prospects for economic growth.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Mathematical Economics
catalog.description: An introduction to mathematical methods as applied to the questions addressed by economists. The principal methods to be applied are matrix algebra and differential calculus in the context of optimization. Other topics may include integral calculus, differential equations, difference equations, or linear and non-linear programming.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Econometrics
catalog.description: An introduction to the empirical side of economics. Estimation theory and the properties of commonly used estimators are covered. Some of the more important topics dealt with are: multiple regression, heteroscedasticity and autocorrelation in regression analysis, analysis of variance and the use of qualitative variables in regression analysis. Hands-on work with computer software designed for econometrics is stressed. No experience with computers necessary.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Monetary Theory And Policy
catalog.description: A study of the nature and functions of money and the financial system, with emphasis on monetary theory and its application to current banking and financial problems. Recent contributions to monetary theory and current literature.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Public Finance
catalog.description: Problems of public and private sector decision making of revenue-expenditure policies and an examination of the actual legal, political and economic policies for revenues and expenditures of federal, state and local governments.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: State And Local Government Finance
catalog.description: This course investigates the role, problems and relative importance of municipal governments in the United States. Such areas as the demand for public services, tax and expenditure policies, and intergovernmental fiscal relations will be explored in detail. Case studies of state and local governments will be introduced to emphasize the problems and proposed solutions arising in modern municipal governments.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Economic Policy
catalog.description: Analysis of the confluence of political and economic behavior, the economics of collective action.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: International Finance
catalog.description: This course emphasizes the global activity and balance of payments implications of government taxation, expenditure and monetary policies under various capital market conditions. Major topics include: exchange rates and the balance of payments; national income determination in an open economy; integrated and non-integrated capital markets; economic growth stabilization policies and the quest for global economic stability.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Institutional Economic Theory
catalog.description: Analysis of impact of modern philosophy and developments in social sciences on economic theory.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Urban Economics
catalog.description: An inquiry into the economics of location decisions and the influence of these on urban growth and on the real estate market; the evaluation of urban transportation and other public services; an examination of economic development of ghetto neighborhoods.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Political Economy of Food Systems
catalog.description: This course examines our food and agriculture system within the global economy. This means exploring the role of different actors in influencing policies as well as exploring the role of various social institutions that structure our individual relationship with food systems. The course also discusses various alternative agricultural initiatives such as local food, organic farming, food justice/sovereignty movements, diversified farming, and agroecology.
catalog.prerequisites: ECON 201 or ECON 202 or ECON 420 or permission of the instructor.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Industrial Organization
catalog.description: The structure, conduct, and performance of American industry. Historical evolution of American industry; alternative industrial systems. Antitrust policies and their alternatives. Technological change and industrial performance.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Economics Institutions and Policies
catalog.description: This course focuses on the economic system analysis of labor market phenomena in the context of historical-institutional development and labor market policies, this course is offered winter semester only.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Labor Economics
catalog.description: An examination of the theories of wage determination, the economic effects of wage determination upon the wage structure, the distribution of national income, employment, and an introduction to collective bargaining.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Radical Political Economy
catalog.description: This course will cover the ideas that constitute radical political economy. It will show how radical political economy can be used to examine current economics and social problems and will outline possible economic structures of utopian visions.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Readings In Economics
catalog.description: Intensive reading and/or research in an area selected by the student in consultation with the professor in any of the following fields: (a) economic theory, (b) history of economic thought, (c) labor economics, (d) urban economics, (e) monetary and fiscal policy and theory, (f) international economics, (g) economic development. (h) comparative economic systems, (i) public finance, (j) public policy toward business, (k) quantitative economics.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Practicum in Urban Economic Development
catalog.description: The Practicum in Urban Economic Development provides students with the opportunity to integrate and apply the knowledge and skills developed through previous coursework to real-world problems of urban economic development. Working on collaborative, service-learning projects in partnership with both community and metropolitan-level organizations, students will engage with the process of applied urban economic development in a team-structured context. Student teams will be each be responsible for one term project over the course of the semester. The course will culminate with the public presentation of project outcomes.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Internship
catalog.description: The course allows the student to participate in cognate, approved internships of a professional nature.
catalog.prerequisites: ECON 201 and ECON 202 ; completion of 75 credit hours and undergraduate major or graduate student in Economics.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Macroeconomic Analysis
catalog.description: The course presents the main theories of output and employment, as well as of the determinants of economics growth. It also critically examines the different approaches to inflation, fiscal policy, the role of money and interest rates. The method followed combines macroeconomic theory with elements of history of economic analysis, and it is divided into five main modules: output and employment, inflation and the Phillips Curve, Economic Growth, fiscal policy and money and interest rate determination. Knowledge of differential calculus and optimization is required for the course.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Microeconomic Analysis
catalog.description: This course provides students with a basic understanding of the neoclassical approach to understanding consumers and firms. The course focuses on partial equilibrium analysis under certainty, and the techniques of constrained optimization and comparative statics applied to economic situations. The focus is on theoretical models used in the neoclassical approach and how they may be employed in empirical and policy analyses. In addition, the course will also discuss the drawbacks of this approach to understanding economic life. The course presumes basic knowledge of differential calculus and optimization.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Heterodox Economics
catalog.description: The course examines various theoretical approaches and topics, both historically and currently, that constitute heterodox economics. In particular the course deals in depth with the mathematical and economic properties of heterodox production and price models. After reviewing the mathematics of linear production-price models, the module will examine Leontief, Sraffian, and other heterodox price and production models.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: American Economic History Since 1865
catalog.description: The course deals with the emergence of Industrial America since 1865. It will cover the rise to dominance of the large modern corporation, with the problem of economic and social instability and stability, with the rise of trade associations, cartels, and government regulation in an unstable economy, and with the evolution of American economic policy and national economic planning.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: American Labor History
catalog.description: This course examines the history of work and the working class in the U.S. from 1750 to the present. We will focus on the transformation of the workplace, the rise of the union movement, the nature of cultural and political organizations, workers' relationships with other social groups, and the role played by gender, race, and ethnicity in uniting or dividing the working class.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Comparative Economic Systems
catalog.description: Contents vary depending upon the instructor's design for the course.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced History Of Economic Thought
catalog.description: This seminar uses issues raised in the reading of two 'classic' primary texts, Adam Smith's An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776) and John Maynard Keynes's The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money (1936), as points of departure for the examination of a series of topics in the history and development of economics and alternative paradigms in the discipline. These investigations will lead us to the study of a number of other seminal articles, representing alternative approaches in the field. Topics include competition, accumulation, path dependence and endogenous technical change, cumulative causation, the laws of return, money and credit, capital theory, and more.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Controversial Issues In Recent Economic Literature
catalog.description: This course will focus on theoretical and policy-oriented controversies that have occurred in economic in the 20th century. The type of controversies covered include, but are not restricted to, money, unemployment, business cycles and economic growth, pricing and administered prices, capital controversy, labor theory of value controversy, and free trade vs. protectionism. While the course concentrates on recent debates, it identifies the origins of the modern disputes in earlier controversies. For each controversy, its real world importance and policy implications are discussed.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for Urban Economic Development
catalog.description: An advanced quantitative methods course featuring the application of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) to the problems of urban economic development. Surveys federal, state, and local geospatial and attribute data resources, including Census Bureau TIGER files, and provides training in geodatabase construction and management. Geospatial processing, editing, and address geocoding are also covered. Formal analytical methods (cartographic aesthetics and visualization, spatial analysis, exploratory data analysis, network analysis, crime analysis, etc.) are all applied in the context of the problematics of urban and regional economic development.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Economic Development
catalog.description: Contents vary depending upon the instructor's design.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Economic Cycles And Growth
catalog.description: A critical review and evaluation of economic analysis and the forces of economic fluctuation and growth; and analysis of statics, dynamics, monopolistic competition, the role of the interrelationships of the market structure and other institutional forces as they relate to fluctuations and growth. An emphasis will be made on the critical evaluation of recent literature in the field of economic analysis related to fluctuations, growth, statics, dynamics, market structure and the reinterpretation of economic fluctuations, growth, forecasting and overall economic behavior. An analysis of the technological, monetary, and fiscal policy implied by economic trends and growth will also be discussed.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Law And Economics
catalog.description: This course will examine the use of economic principles in the analysis and applications of public and private law. Emphasis will be given to the efficiencies of laws in meeting social objectives, how laws can be modified to become more economically efficient, and the uses of economics in the actual practice of the law. Issues covered will include proofs of liability in antitrust, contracts and employment law using statistical and economic analysis, and the calculation of economic damages in commercial, employment and personal injury/death litigation.. Graduate students will be assigned a specific research paper..

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Mathematical Economics
catalog.description: This course introduces the fundamental mathematical methods used in advanced economics. This includes matrix algebra as used in economics as well as differential and integral calculus in the context of optimization and cost/benefit analysis. Basic linear economic models are introduced, as are unconstrained and constrained optimization applied to economic problems. Other topics may include differential equations, difference equations, and linear and nonlinear programming as time permits.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Econometric Methods
catalog.description: This course provides mathematically grounded training in applied econometrics, emphasizing statistical inference and empirical modeling with cross-sectional, time-series, and panel data. Students develop graduate-level theoretical foundations in econometrics while applying statistical methods using R to estimate models, interpret results, and critically assess empirical research. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to design and carry out independent econometric analyses and engage rigorously with econometric applications in contemporary academic journals and books. No programming experience necessary.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Readings In Quantitative Economics
catalog.description: Readings from the economic literature which stress advanced mathematical or econometric tools. A general subject matter is selected by the student with the consent of the instructor.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Monetary Theory And Policy
catalog.description: A study of the nature and functions of money and the financial system, with emphasis on monetary theory and its application to current banking and financial problems; recent contributions to monetary theory and current literature.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Theory Of Public Finance
catalog.description: An inquiry into the scope and nature of economics with emphasis on the nature of the public sector including a brief study of welfare criteria along with the study of ability to pay, benefit theory of taxation, and expenditure theories.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: State And Local Government Finance
catalog.description: This course investigates the role, problems and relative importance of municipal governments in the United States. Such areas as the demand for public services, tax and expenditure policies, and intergovernmental fiscal relations will be explored in detail. Case studies of state and local governments will be introduced to emphasize the problems and proposed solutions arising in modern municipal governments.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Economic Policy
catalog.description: Analysis of the confluence of political and economic behavior, the economics of collective action.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced International Trade
catalog.description: This course emphasizes the global allocation of resources and distribution of income under various commodity market conditions and government trade policies. Major topics include: comparative advantage; terms of trade; the distribution of gains and losses from trade; perfect vs. imperfect competition; tariffs, quotas and other barriers to trade; exchange rates and the balance of payments; preferential trading arrangements; international factor movements and multinational corporations.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced International Finance
catalog.description: This course emphasizes the global activity and balance of payments implications of government taxation, expenditure and monetary policies under various capital market conditions. Major topics include: exchange rates and the balance of payments; national income determination in an open economy; integrated and non-integrated capital markets; economic growth, stabilization policies and the quest for global economic stability.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Socialist Economic Systems
catalog.description: The course will deal with the theoretical analysis of socialist economic theory, Marxian and non-Marxian, and/or of socialist economics systems such as those of Eastern Europe, the Chinese mainland and elsewhere. The emphasis of the course will vary depending upon the instructor's design for the course.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Regional Economics
catalog.description: The economics of spatial relations, emphasizing basic location and land utilization theory and the role of transport will be considered at the micro-level. Keynesian and neoclassical growth theories and contemporary policy approaches to regional growth and decline are analyzed.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Institutional Theory
catalog.description: This course introduces advanced institutional theory through an examination of the evolution, organization, and allocation functions of the modern industrial economy. It explores the contributions and limitations of conventional economic concepts and engages philosophical and theoretical interpretations of economic institutions in light of modern developments in philosophy and social science.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Urban Economics
catalog.description: The study of the city as a dynamic system of interrelated and interdependent markets. Significant markets in cities include land, housing, labor, transportation and public services.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Industrial Organization
catalog.description: The structure, conduct and performance of American industry. Historical evolution of American industry; alternative industrial systems, antitrust policies and their alternatives. Technological change and industrial performance.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Labor Economics, Institutions and Policies
catalog.description: This course focuses on the economic analysis of labor market phenomena in the context of historical-institutional development and on labor market policies. This course is offered winter semester only.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Racial Inequality & Public Policy
catalog.description: This course will provoke open debate and discourse about public policy responses to racial inequality. The emphasis is on stimulating participants to think about and to analyze critically the range of strategies offered for reducing racism and racial economic inequality.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Human Resource Economics
catalog.description: An analysis of the factors determining the productivity of human resource: education, nutrition, job training and work environment. An analysis of work patterns, wage patterns, and the impact of automation. Graduate students will be assigned a specific research paper on a topic to be decided with the instructor.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Advanced Political Economy
catalog.description: This course gives students a comprehensive introduction to the history and modern practice of political economy, with particular emphasis on Marxian and Classical political economy. Topics include: value theory, class theory, economic reproduction, economic crisis, the theory of history, and methodology.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Graduate Seminar In Labor Economics
catalog.description: Content of seminar will vary from semester to semester depending upon the instructor's design for the course.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Selected topics in theoretical and applied economics.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Research And Planning Seminar
catalog.description: The objective of this research seminar is to apply the quantitative techniques and theoretical constructs of economics to an urban-regional problem. Students are required to formulate and evaluate present economic models, and then complete a research project.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Research And Thesis
catalog.description: Directed specialized research.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium In Advanced Macroeconomics
catalog.description: The course presents different controversial topics on macroeconomics, fiscal and monetary policy and economic growth, both from a heterodox and orthodox views, in closed and open economies. It is divided into three main modules: controversial issues on investment and growth in neoclassical theory, controversial issues on demand led growth models and, finally, controversial issues on open economy macroeconomics. The course presuposes knowledge on differential calculus and linear algebra, optimization techniques and differential equations.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium In Advanced Microeconomics
catalog.description: This course focuses on business enterprises and the business behavior with emphasis on production, costs, pricing, price-quantity models of the economy, as well as labor markets and microfoundations of heterodox macroeconomics. Advanced study of the business enterprise draws on modern developments in microeconomics emphasizing imperfect information and the absence of third-party contract enforcement. It focuses on how incentives, strategic behavior, and self-enforcing arrangements shape economic outcomes. The effects of different arrangements of control rights and residual claimancy are studied empirically and theoretically.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium on Advanced History of Economic Thought
catalog.description: The course examines advanced topics in history of economic thought.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Topics In Economic Theory
catalog.description: This course deals with advanced topics in Institutionalism, Post Keynesian, and other heterodox economic theory. May be repeated with different topic.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: History Of Economics In The 20th Century
catalog.description: The history of 20th century economics is concerned with a number of interdependent issues, including the institutional organization of economics at universities; the historical development of the structures and social networks that make-up the economic paradigms of neoclassical economics, Marxian economics, Post Keynesian economics, and other heterodox economics; and the role of institutional and state power to maintain the dominance of the neoclassical paradigm. The aim of the course is to introduce students to this institutional/organizational history.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium In Econometrics
catalog.description: This course examines modern econometric methods for causal inference and empirical research design. After reviewing probability, regression, and panel data methods, the course develops the potential outcomes framework and identification strategies using Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). Topics include Matching methods, Instrumental Variables, Regression Discontinuity Design, Difference-in-Differences (including staggered adoption), Shift-share instruments, and Synthetic Control methods. Emphasis is placed on research design, identification assumptions, robustness analysis, and the development of original empirical research proposals.
catalog.prerequisites: ECON 5501 , ECON 5502 , ECON 5521 , ECON 5525 , or equivalents.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium on Monetary Theory and Policy
catalog.description: This course explores advanced monetary theory and policy, examining recent debates and current research practices, as well as classic articles on monetary theory and policy.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Financial Macroeconomics
catalog.description: This course will introduce the student to the central role of financial analysis in macroeconomic analysis and to theories of macroeconomics instability based on the integration of finance and macroeconomics. It will examine modern finance theory and modern approaches to financial analysis, paying particular attention to the contributions made by Fisher and Keynes.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Evolution Of American Industrial Society
catalog.description: Drawing on economic and organizational theory, the course will concentrate on the evolution of American industrial technology, the American business enterprise, and the organization of American industries and markets since 1870.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium In Advanced Health Economics
catalog.description: This course is designed as a seminar with a special emphasis on analysis of econometric methods to assess issues in health care. The topics are developed from a theoretical and applied perspective. Familiarity with personal computers is necessary. Special emphasis will be given in the selection of course topics to the interests and backgrounds of participants.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Teaching Methods And Course Design
catalog.description: This course is designed to prepare students for the challenge of teaching economics. Students will be taught how to write a syllabus; how to prepare for class; how to plan learning activities; how to become skillful in leading discussion; how to present an effective lecture; how to test and assess student learning; how to develop effective group projects; how to motivate their students for lifelong learning. Students will be required to design a course to be taught at the 200-, 300 or 400-level. The student will prepare a complete set of course materials, including a lecture outline, a list of require readings, useful handouts, course materials, including a lecture outline, a list of require readings, useful handouts, course assignments, exams, etc. The course should incorporate an interdisciplinary approach and should emphasize an 'active learning' component, designed to promote a 'rich learning experience.' The student will work closely with an appropriate member of the faculty.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Colloquium On Political Economy
catalog.description: This course is designed as a seminar and will take into account theory and policy analysis from alternative perspectives. The topics covered will include philosophical foundations of contemporary theory and policy, the organization of production information and finance, resource and environment, wealth and income distribution, public and private policy and planning. Stress is placed on contemporary research and students are expected to become involved in research projects.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Special Doctoral Readings In Economics
catalog.description: Special research topics in Economics at the Doctoral level.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Pre-Dissertation Research
catalog.description: Directed selected research for Economics leading to preparation and completion of doctoral dissertation in the interdisciplinary doctoral program.

catalog.subject: ECON
catalog.title: Doctoral Dissertation
catalog.description: Directed selected research for Economics in the interdisciplinary doctoral program.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Language & Literacy across the Disciplines
catalog.description: Principles and application of disciplinary literacy in the middle and secondary classroom. Class will be primarily composed of discussion and lecture. As a part of the course, teacher candidates will inquire into and analyze disciplinary practices in 5-12 schools.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Language and Literacy Across the Disciplines
catalog.description: Principles and application of disciplinary literacy in the middle and secondary classroom. Class will be primarily composed of discussion and lecture. As a part of the course, teacher candidates will inquire into and analyze disciplinary practices in 5-12 schools.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the school of education.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Teaching Of Reading
catalog.description: This graduate language and literacy course explores foundational theories and research that have influenced literacy instruction and assessment in the United States. In particular, this course examines critical sociocultural theories and high leverage literacy practices for diverse learners.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Early Literacy and Language Development
catalog.description: This graduate language and literacy course emphasizes learning theories related to language acquisition, continuums of emergent literacy development, and corresponding teaching methods for literacy instruction and assessment of diverse learners. This course also prepares teachers and reading professionals to implement continuous professional learning related to language acquisition and emergent literacy with other teaching professionals.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Adolescent Practicum in Literacy Assessment and Intervention
catalog.description: This course ensures learners understand the purposes, strengths, and limitations of different literacy assessments in order to assess adolescent students’ proficiencies. The course will focus on identifying cognitive, motivational, and sociocultural factors that contribute to literacy success for the adolescent student in order to design and teach literacy intervention lessons with a struggling adolescent reader. As part of the practicum experience, learners are trained on communicating assessment results and implications to a variety of audiences.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Advanced Literacy Assessment and Evaluation
catalog.description: This graduate language & literacy course engages teachers and literacy specialists in building foundational knowledge, analyzing, and administering intelligence and achievement tests focusing on a range of skills and abilities. The course foregrounds research-based, developmentally-appropriate theoretical frameworks and measures of cognitive functioning and academic achievement, as well as formative and summative literacy assessment practices through a variety of advanced level methods.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Seminar In Reading
catalog.description: In this seminar, candidates will be introduced to the discourse of literacy research, understand commonly used practitioner research designs, become critical consumers of literacy research, and expand their knowledge of the extant body of literature on literacy and literacy for diverse learners.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Elementary Practicum in Literacy Assessment and Intervention
catalog.description: This culminating elementary practicum is designed for graduate students in Language & Literacy. This course prepares teachers to demonstrate proficiency in meeting the literacy needs of struggling readers and diverse learners in an elementary school setting and engaging in peer coaching and active self-peer analysis in order to improve their own instructional practices. Note: As this is the culminating course in the degree program, students are encouraged to implement learning concepts, practices, and assessments from previous coursework as appropriate during this practicum course.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Reading Instruction for K-12 English Language Learners
catalog.description: This course investigates ways to differentiate reading instruction to meet needs of English Language Learners with different levels of language proficiency and at different developmental and academic levels. The course focuses on research findings related to literacy development of diverse learners and ways to strengthen diverse classroom communities. This is an elective course in Language & Literacy and does not have prerequisites.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Teaching Reading Improvement: Secondary, College, and Adult Levels
catalog.description: Classroom and laboratory techniques for upper level reading instruction; including study skills; reading speed and flexibility, and vocabulary improvement.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Organizing And Guiding The Reading Program
catalog.description: This course examines, analyzes, and develops effective K-12 schoolwide literacy programs that include intervention support systems for responding to the needs of all students in diverse contexts. In addition, the course will focus on program goals, the roles and responsibilities of personnel, materials, fostering collaborative leadership, and creating a school culture that focuses on literacy.

catalog.subject: EDRD
catalog.title: Dyslexia and Related Learning Differences
catalog.description: This advanced level graduate language and literacy course analyzes theories of atypical literacy development, with a specific focus on identification and awareness of the ways that language processing affects speech, reading and spelling. Students will explore the coexistence of dyslexia with related learning differences and will plan instructional interventions for students with literacy special needs.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: An undergraduate course designed to deal with a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors and prerequisites to be listed in the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: An undergraduate course designed to deal with a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors and prerequisites to be listed in the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: An undergraduate course designed to deal with a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Literature For Adolescents
catalog.description: Focus upon literature for adolescents and ethnic literature, specifically, and upon the special reading interests of the adolescent in relation to the methods and materials of reading in grades 7-12, generally. Attention to literature selection standards, censorship, individualized instruction, and reader response.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: A course designed to deal with a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors and prerequisites to be listed in each semester's bulletin.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Individual Study
catalog.description: Guided study of a selected topic in education.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Advanced Diagnostic And Treatment Procedures In Reading
catalog.description: Significant aspects of reading disability; diagnostic testing; case report writing; interpretation of test data; implications of test data for recommendations.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Individual Studies
catalog.description: Review of the research trends relative to selected problems in education. By prior arrangement with instructor.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Practicum In Curriculum And Instruction
catalog.description: A field experience which provides an opportunity for the application of current research in the area of curriculum and instruction to an educational setting.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Special Problems
catalog.description: Individual studies; thesis exploration, special reading.

catalog.subject: EDUC
catalog.title: Dissertation Curriculum And Instruction
catalog.description: Dissertation Curriculum And Instruction

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Special Education Law, Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), and Transition
catalog.description: This course provides students with knowledge of special education law, the individualized education program (IEP), and transition-related instruction (i.e., preparation for post-high school education employment, independent living, and community integration) for students with disabilities. The field experience will include observation of meetings with families and other professionals.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the teacher preparation program.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Theories of Behavior and Policies in Special Education
catalog.description: This course is designed as an introductory undergraduate level class that introduces the special education teacher candidate to Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and its application in the classroom. The course addresses managing classroom behavior and that of individuals who present more challenging behavior including students with mild disabilities. Students must have completed a background check to do the required field experience for this course, which includes observations and working with youth with disabilities.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the Teacher Education Professional Program.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Educating Exceptional Children And Youth
catalog.description: An introductory course in special education concerning issues, theories, and practices for educating the exceptional student in both general and special classrooms or settings; identification and educational intervention procedures for children and adolescents with exceptionalities; including students with behavior disorders, students with learning disabilities, students with speech/language impairments; students with visual impairments, students with physical disabilities, students with hearing impairments, students with multiple disabilities, and students identified as gifted.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Assessment and Data Literacy in Special Education
catalog.description: This is a foundations course in the undergraduate degree sequence in special education of children and youth with mild/moderate disabilities. The focus of the course is to provide the teacher candidate an understanding of formal and informal assessment and how to apply assessment tools in an applied setting. This course is applicable to candidates who plan to work with students with exceptional learning needs. The course will present the strengths and limitations for assessments as it relates to special education and students with special needs.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to Teacher Education Professional Program, background check.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Cognition and Language Development in Mild/Moderate Cross-Categorical Disabilities
catalog.description: This is a specialized methods course in the undergraduate degree sequence in special education of children and youth with mild/moderate disabilities. This course examines normal and atypical development and cultural and linguistic diversity of students with exceptional learning needs. Candidates will practice collaborative and reflective decision-making and problem solving in areas such as: (a) developmentally sequenced activities, (b) receptive and expressive language, and (c) communication and augmentative communication skills.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to Teacher Education Professional Program

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Teaching Students with Mild/Moderate Cross-Categorical Disabilities
catalog.description: This course is the second methods course in a sequence for undergraduate students in the special education program. Teacher candidates will learn instructional methodologies, informed by best practice, to assess, plan and, implement instruction across multiple content areas, including science, social studies, math, writing, and reading. Students will learn to differentiate instruction in order to address specific learning needs of individuals with mild/moderate cross categorical disabilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Behavioral Intervention and Instructional Support in Special Education
catalog.description: This is the second course of two courses addressing challenging behavior in the classroom setting. Candidates will reflect critically on social/affective curricular goals for children and youth with mild-moderate cross-categorical (MM/CC) disabilities. Candidates will learn best practices based on principles of Applied Behavior Analysis and apply those practices in designing behavior intervention plans for managing challenging behaviors. Students will create positive behavioral supports, collect functional behavioral assessment data, and use that data to develop behavior intervention plans.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Special Education Law, Individualized Education Programs (IEP's), and Transition
catalog.description: This course provides students with knowledge of special education law, the individualized education program (IEP), and transition-related instruction (i.e., preparation for post-high school education employment, independent living, and community integration) for students with disabilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Theories of Behavior and Policies in Special Education
catalog.description: This course introduces the special education teacher to Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and its application in the classroom. The course addresses the management of classroom behavior, including individuals who present more challenging behavior, such as students with mild disabilities. Students learn how to apply ABA-based principles, interventions and strategies in special education and general education settings. The course includes discussion and applications to research-practice-theory.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Methods I: Introduction to Teaching Students with Mild/Moderate Cross-Categorical Disabilities
catalog.description: Examines theories and practices which are effective in addressing learning difficulties of students with mild-moderate disabilities. Focuses on understanding learner characteristics with the purpose of differentiating instruction related to academic, behavioral, and social skills presented by students with mild/moderate disabilities.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the Special Education program or consent of instructor.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Assessment for Special Educators
catalog.description: This is a foundations course in the master's degree sequence focused on the special education of children and youth with mild/moderate disabilities. This course provides understanding and practice in formal and informal evaluation and is applicable to candidates who plan to work either directly (as special educators) or indirectly (as special education administrators) with students with exceptional learning needs. Students learn to engage in the critical analysis of assessment issues confronting the field of special education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Cognition & Lang Dev In Mild/Mod Cross-Categorical Disabilities
catalog.description: This is a specialized methods course in the master's degree sequence in special education of children and youth with mild/moderate disabilities. This course examines normal and atypical development and cultural and linguistic diversity of students with exceptional learning needs. Candidates will practice collaborative and reflective decision-making and problem solving in areas such as: (a) developmentally sequenced activities, (b) receptive and expressive language, and (c) communication and augmentative communication skills. The field experience will include working observations and working with children and youth with disabilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Methods II: Teaching Students with Mild/Moderate Cross-Categorical Disabilities
catalog.description: Students learn academic and behavioral strategies to plan instruction, deliver instruction, and evaluate student and teacher performance in order to promote critical thinking and content literacy across all content areas, including science, mathematics, reading, writing, and social science. Prior to taking the course, a background check must be completed in order to do the required 10-hour field experience for this course. The field experience will include observations and working with children and youth with disabilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Introduction To Mild/Moderate Cross-Categorical Disabilities
catalog.description: This is the initial foundations course in the master's degree sequence in special education of children and youth with mild/moderate disabilities including students with learning disabilities, students with behavioral disorders, and students with physical or other health impairments. It is designed to provide candidates who are new to the field of special education with a foundation for working with students who have exceptional learning needs. Prior to taking the course, a background check must be completed in order to do the required 10-hour field experience for this course. The field experience will include observations and working with children and youth with disabilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Practicum in Special Education
catalog.description: The purpose of this course is to provide a field-based experience in a setting with students with mild/moderate cross-categorical disabilities. This field experience affords candidates classroom experience either in their own instructional settings or under the tutelage of a master teacher. Placement sites reflect the multicultural diversity found in special education classrooms (K-12). The practicum will include observations, working with children and youth with disabilities individually and in small groups, as well lesson preparation and presentation.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Practicum II – Special Education
catalog.description: Provides second tier field-based experience in a setting with students with mild/moderate cross-categorical disabilities. This field experience affords candidates classroom experience either in their own instructional settings or under the tutelage of a master teacher. Placement sites reflect the multicultural diversity found in special education classrooms (K-12). Experiences include observations, working with children and youth with disabilities individually and in small groups, as well as lesson preparation and presentation.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Understanding and Addressing Challenging Behavior in the Classroom
catalog.description: An examination of validated practices based on principles of Applied Behavior Analysis for managing challenging behaviors, facilitating formal behavioral assessment, creating positive behavioral supports, conducting functional behavioral assessments, and developing behavior intervention programs. Candidates reflect critically on social/affective curricular goals for children and youth with mild-moderate cross-categorical (MM/CC) disabilities and relate the theoretical, research, and practical strategies of behavior change models in an applied setting. Experiences include interactions with teachers, parents, and paraprofessionals, in order to understand and remediate student behavior problems. Prerequisite: Admission to program, EDUC-SP 5515 , or consent of instructor.
catalog.prerequisites: Prior to taking the course a background check must be completed in order to do the required 10 hour field experience for this course The field experience will include observations and working with children and youth with disabilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Applied Behavior Analysis for Teachers: Understanding and Applying Theories of Behavior
catalog.description: This course is designed as an introductory graduate level class on behavior and is the first of two courses on behavior. The course addresses aspects of managing and motivating learners with special needs placed in general education settings based upon the principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA). Topics include student acquisition of knowledge and skills related to ABA behavior principles theory and history of ABA, ethical considerations of ABA, understanding the principles of reinforcement and punishment, identifying the nature of consequences maintaining or decreasing specific behaviors; and operationally defining behavior. Prior to taking the course a background check must be completed in order to do the required 10 hour field experience for this course. The field experience will include observations and working with children and youth with disabilities
catalog.prerequisites: Prerequisite: Admission to program, EDUC-SP 5515 , or consent of instructor.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Collaborating with Families and Other Professionals
catalog.description: This is a methods course in the master's degree sequence in special education of children and youth with mild/moderation disabilities. The course presents principles and procedures for fostering collaborative partnerships among family members, caregivers, educators, and human service personnel that lead to outcomes of individual and mutual empowerment. Candidates will engage in reflective thinking on their personal philosophical beliefs and interweave these beliefs with the skills needed to work with the multicultural issues facing families of children and youth with mild/moderate cross-categorical disabilities and other professionals. Prior to taking the course a background check must be completed in order to do the required 10 hour field experience for this course. The field experience will include observations and working with families of children and youth with disabilities and education professionals.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Characteristics, Hist & Thrys: Emotional Disturbance In Children
catalog.description: An investigation of theories, classification, etiology, incidence, and characteristics of children with emotional/ behavioral disorders.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Student Teaching in Special Education
catalog.description: This is the final clinical course in the master's degree sequence in special education of children and youth with mild/moderate disabilities. The purpose of this course is to provide a field-based experience in a setting where candidates will be fully responsible for designing curriculum and teaching students with mild/moderate cross-categorical disabilities. Placement sites reflect the multicultural diversity found in special education classrooms (K-12). This course requires candidates to apply content learned throughout the master's degree program in an authentic setting. Student teaching involves a full time commitment to the field for 16 weeks.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Special Topics In Education
catalog.description: A course designed to deal with a special education topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors, and prerequisites to be listed on the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: EDUC-SP
catalog.title: Individual Studies
catalog.description: Review of the research and trends relative to selected problems in special education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Foundations Of School Leadership & Organization
catalog.description: Participants will study as cohort team members actively engaged in clinical/practical endeavors in schools, concepts and theories focused: 1) to understand and apply modern leadership and organization development theory in relation to school organizational cultures; 2) to understand both the development of productive school relationships and the theoretical concepts of the legal responsibilities of schools in the society; 3) to develop a plan for principal certification based upon participant needs and experiences; and 4) to build school cultures that are collaborative, participative, reflective, and self renewing.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Building Administration And Management
catalog.description: Participants will study and apply theories and concepts as members of a Cohort Team doing clinical work in schools designed to study, learn, and practice the management and administrative responsibilities of building level leaders including principal roles, personnel issues, school business management, community relations, supervision of staff, and to know the legal responsibilities relating to teachers, student and public rights.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Student, Staff And Organization Development
catalog.description: Participants will study as a member of a cohort team doing clinical work in school and developing the ability: 1) to gain knowledge of, and practice in developing 'learning organizations'; 2) to assist teachers and other staff members of a school in structuring classrooms around the learning and development of all students; 3) to lead and develop urban schools that are culturally diverse where learner outcomes and performance are not related to race, class, or gender; and 4) to provide leadership related to developing school structures that are outcome oriented.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Instructional Supervision
catalog.description: Principles of supervision, factors influencing effectiveness of instruction, including the evaluation of teachers.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: School Finance
catalog.description: Sources of revenue for public education; distribution of monies for education; budget construction; accounting procedures; and theories for financing education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Governmental And Legal Aspects Of Education
catalog.description: Current and recent legislation affecting education; court cases related to education; emerging patterns of modern juris-prudence; administrators' responsibilities regarding legal decisions.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Governmental And Legal Aspects Of Special Education
catalog.description: An examination of current and recent legislation affecting special education; emerging patterns of modern jurisprudence; and special education teacher and administrator legal responsibilities.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Leadership for School Improvement
catalog.description: The content of this course has a focus on identifying and using data to make school improvement decisions. Students will be engaged in readings, activities, and reflections that discuss the importance of using data for decision-making at the building and district levels of school leadership.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission into the Educational Administration Program.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Data Driven Leadership for Reculturing Schools
catalog.description: The challenges facing urban education are complex and may be understood from a myriad of perspectives including historical and socio-cultural underpinnings, economic and political contexts, and pedagogical/achievement orientations. This course will bring together some of these arguments as they relate to what school leaders can do to promote a community of adult leaders who use data th make decisions for the success of all children. Such a challenge includes working as educational leaders to reculture schools to increase opportunities for all students to learn. For some schools this task involves closing the persistent achievement gap that may exist among groups of students which requires disaggregating data by race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, gender, and special educational needs.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Administrative Roles For Instructional Leadership
catalog.description: This course meets a requirement for administrator certification in Missouri and Kansas in the area of school improvement and leadership. The course focuses upon leadership roles necessary for creating a supportive climate for change and for implementing improved instructional programs.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Philosophical Inquiry And Education
catalog.description: An examination of issues, problems and controversies discussed in educational and related literature, utilizing criteria and techniques of logical and philosophical analysis. The focus is on the development of critical thinking abilities as applied to theories, positions and arguments in educational and related contexts.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Cultural Foundations Of Education
catalog.description: Examines education and schooling as cultural phenomena. This course focuses on an analysis of education and schooling as both cultural transmission and cultural change and the practical implications. Also included is a philosophical/ theoretical examination of varying relationships between dominant and minority cultures.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Philosophical Foundations Of Education
catalog.description: Introduction to the study of philosophical problems implicit in educational issues. Focuses on the application of a number of philosophical concepts and skills to a variety of controversies, policies, and theories in education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Historical Foundations Of Education
catalog.description: Study of the development of educational policy, practice, and theory in relation to changes in social institutions and thought. Focuses on the analysis of contemporary educational problems in the light of historical perspectives.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Sociological Foundations Of Education
catalog.description: An analysis of issues involving the role of schools in society, the relationship between education and other social institutions, and contemporary social developments which have major implications.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Educational Leadership and Human Resources
catalog.description: This course has been designed to develop students' proficiencies in school human resource management and its importance to positive outcomes for student learning. The course focuses on human resource components that are essential to effective schools.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission into the Educational Administration EdD Program.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Educational Leadership and Organizational Behavior
catalog.description: This course has been designed to develop the students' proficiencies in school organization and management to provide positive outcomes for student learning. The course focuses upon organizational behavior and development and its components that are essential to effective school.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission into the Educational Administration EdD Program.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Current Topics in Urban School Leadership
catalog.description: Current Topics in Urban School Leadership

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Organization And Administration Of Higher Education
catalog.description: Organizational patterns; administrative roles and procedures; establishment of policies, institutional development; and public and private financing of higher education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Student Affairs Administration In Higher Education
catalog.description: Study of the objectives, organizational structure, and current issues of student affairs administration as they relate to the academic program, the campus environment, and the needs of students; analysis of the functions of different services.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: The College Student
catalog.description: An examination of today's college students. Review and study of demographics, relationships of students and colleges, nature of student communities, new student populations and the impact of college on students and their educational development.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Legal Aspects Of Higher Education
catalog.description: Study of legal issues within higher education. Focus is on state and federal law and regulations as they pertain to issues ranging from academic freedom to governance and administration. Focus on strategies for preventive law is a major component of the course.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Advanced Student Development Theory
catalog.description: A focused and in-depth examination of developmental theories related to the college student. This course builds on information presented in EDUC-UL 5556 .

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Current Issues In Community Colleges
catalog.description: A course responsive to the contemporary issues in community college administration, addressing interesting and important topics that fall outside the scope of other courses in the higher education curriculum. Students will have an overview of the role of community colleges within the larger organization of colleges and universities in the U.S. higher education system.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Leadership In Higher Education
catalog.description: Focus on leadership, connections among different approaches to leadership, different forms of power, and different leadership behaviors. A series of opportunities to think systematically about leadership and to increase a student's personal leadership capacities in higher education will be provided.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: History Of Higher Education
catalog.description: Study of the evolution of the constituencies within different types of American higher education institutions. The development of professional, practical, and graduate education will be examined as will 20th century alternatives to the liberal arts colleges and research university models.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Racial And Ethnic Diversity, And Cultural Understanding
catalog.description: An exploration of the ideological and historical construction of education for social equality, and subsequent issues of race, ethnicity, and class that influence colleges and universities in the U.S. today.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Higher Education Capstone
catalog.description: This course will provide a culminating experience for students in the Higher Education Master's program. All aspects of higher education administration will be examined and synthesized to enhance student ability to understand and operate in a complex setting.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Internship In Higher Education
catalog.description: Applied experiences in a planned, supervised program. Seminar accompanies internship experiences.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Administrative Practicum
catalog.description: Assigned administrative responsibilities under supervision of practicing educational administrators. The field experiences are supplemented with seminars and a written log recording those experiences. Provides candidates opportunities to interact with stakeholders, synthesize and apply content knowledge, and develop and refine professional skills.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Internship In Administration
catalog.description: Applied experiences in a planned, supervised educational administration program. Seminar accompanies internship experiences.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Special Topics In Educational Leadership
catalog.description: A course designed to deal with a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors, and prerequisites to be listed on the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Seminar
catalog.description: Discussion and evaluation of literature in Education Administration.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Individual Studies
catalog.description: Review of the research and trends relative to selected problems in education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Seminar In The History Of American Urban Education
catalog.description: A study of the historical development of American urban educational institutions and ideas and of how that development is embedded within the broader context of social, political, and economic change in the United States.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Introduction to Doctoral Study
catalog.description: This course is designed as an introductory course in the doctoral sequence for the EdD in Educational Administration with an emphasis in Higher Education. The course is designed to introduce students to the tasks and processes involved in the completion of the doctoral requirements. It is required for all entering doctoral students.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Historical Methods in Educational Research I
catalog.description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of historical research methods with a particular focus on issues in education. Students will learn how to critically analyze and interpret educational history through various methodological approaches, including archival research, oral history, and historiography. Emphasizing both theory and practice, the course equips students with the skills to engage in rigorous historical inquiry that explores the evolution of educational thought, policy, and practice.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Historical Methods in Educational Research II
catalog.description: Building on foundational knowledge of historical research methods, this advanced course deepens students' engagement with the analysis and interpretation of educational history. Students will expand their methodological expertise through specialized techniques such as comparative historical analysis, digital history, and critical historiography, applying these tools to more complex and nuanced educational research topics. By the end of the course, students will have produced a project proposal outline that demonstrates their capacity to engage with complex historical questions and provides new perspectives on how historical developments continue to shape modern educational theory, policy, and practice.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Analysis Of Educational Theory Formation
catalog.description: Study and application of criteria for evaluating the adequacy of educational theories and evaluating the relevance to theories of research studies.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Media, Government, and Public Relations
catalog.description: This course addresses key leadership challenges and decision making in today’s complex world, particularly regarding effective district/school communication. It utilizes selected readings and case studies to move beyond theory to evaluation, application, and synthesis.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Educational Leadership for Change and Organizational Effectiveness
catalog.description: This course is designed to deepen understanding of leadership and professional practices by engaging students in the study, critique, and application of contemporary leadership research and theory. Students examine leadership models, organizational change processes, and strategies that foster continuous, data-driven school improvement. Emphasis is placed on the role of educational leaders as agents of change, facilitators of inclusive decision-making, and stewards of democratic and ethical practice. Students apply analytical and reflective methods to evaluate how leadership theory translates into practice and influences school culture, community partnerships, safety, and organizational capacity.
catalog.prerequisites: Enrollment in the Ed.D. or Ph.D. in Education-Educational Leadership Policy and Foundations program or instructor permission

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Advanced Educational Supervision
catalog.description: Principles and concepts of educational supervision and implementation.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: The Superintendency
catalog.description: Analysis and overview of the nature, functions and activities of the public school superintendency including: historical and philosophical foundations; board-staff and other governing body relationships and functions; professional staff relations and management; public relations and communication; inter-governmental relations and responsibilities, and the functions of planning, direction and supervision of the instructional enterprise.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Topics In Higher Education
catalog.description: Organization of higher education, public and private financing; accreditation; academic freedom; policy development; community relations; curricular patterns, selected current issues.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Policy Issues in Higher Education
catalog.description: This course is intended for those whose roles as educational leaders requires them to participate in the analysis and development of policies associated with educational programs and practice. Students will be able to understand the characteristics of a well developed policy agenda, obstacles to policy implementation, and interpretations related to policy implementation. Concurrently, institutional, political, economic, social, and moral consequences of various policies will be explored.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Apprenticeship And Conference In College Training
catalog.description: Apprenticeship experience in preparing, conducting, and evaluating college teaching under the direction of and in conference with supervising professors. Some attention to student personnel and administration in higher education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Financial Aspects Of Higher Education
catalog.description: This course is designed for graduate students with a basic understanding of the area of Higher Education Administration. The course examines basic concepts and principles of finance in higher education in the United States. Students are expected to: Develop an understanding of 1) the issues and fiscal problems of higher education, 2) the roles and responsibilities of financial officers in higher education, and 3) possible future trends in the financing of higher education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Supervision and Management of People
catalog.description: The purpose of this course is to provide a broad overview of staffing practices in the field of higher education, especially student affairs. The course will assist students to be better professionals, to learn the literature as it relates to supervision, and to begin basic skill development. Other course content includes issues surrounding staff selection, staff orientation.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Studies In Philosophy Of Education
catalog.description: Study of special topics in the philosophy of education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Effective Practices II
catalog.description: This course builds on the general understanding of leadership and professional practices developed in Leadership in Education Effective Practices I. The course addresses key leadership challenges and decision making in today's complex work world. The course uses reading on selected issues, case discussions, and role plays to move beyond theory and understanding to application and effectiveness.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Problems And Issues In Education & Urban Leadership
catalog.description: This course serves as the capstone class for all doctoral students in educational leadership, policy and foundations. The course requires analysis of successful dissertations in urban education and prepares students to write their own dissertation relative to urban study and education.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Special Problems
catalog.description: Individual studies; thesis exploration, special reading.

catalog.subject: EDUC-UL
catalog.title: Dissertation in Educational Leadership, Policy and Foundations
catalog.description: This course provides structured time and guidance for doctoral candidates to make significant progress toward the completion of their dissertation. Students will set clear goals, timelines, and strategies for successful completion with their professor. Emphasis is placed on cultivating productive research and writing habits, maintaining regular communication with mentors and/or support networks, and making effective use of resources. Through consistent engagement, proactive problem-solving, and iterative refinement of their work, students will advance their research, strengthen scholarly skills, and move purposefully toward the final defense of their dissertation.

catalog.subject: ENDO
catalog.title: Endodontology 1
catalog.description: This course is designed to introduce the first year endodontic resident to the field of advanced endodontics. It will provide introductory information and guidance which will serve as a basis for follow on course work in ENDO 5702 through ENDO 5706 .

catalog.subject: ENDO
catalog.title: Endodontology 2
catalog.description: This course is designed to continue the transition of the general dentist into a first year endodontic resident in the field of advanced endodontics. It will build upon material taught in previous courses of instruction as well as introduce completely new material to the resident.

catalog.subject: ENDO
catalog.title: Endodontology 3
catalog.description: This course is designed to complete the transition of the general dentist into a first year endodontic resident in the field of advanced endodontics. It will build upon material taught in previous courses of instruction as well as introduce completely new material to the resident.

catalog.subject: ENDO
catalog.title: Endodontology 4
catalog.description: This course is designed to transition the first year into a second year resident in the field of advanced endodontics. It will be a reinforcement of material taught in previous courses of instruction as well as the introduction of completely new material as made available. This semester is the primary time the Resident completes their data collection for their research project.

catalog.subject: ENDO
catalog.title: Endodontology 5
catalog.description: This course is designed to continue the transition of the general dentist into a more proficient second year resident in the field of advanced endodontics. It will build upon material taught in previous courses of instruction as well as introduce completely new material to the resident.

catalog.subject: ENDO
catalog.title: Endodontology 6
catalog.description: This course is designed to complete the transition of the general dentist into a fully independently practicing endodontist. It will build upon material taught in previous courses of instruction as well as introduce completely new material to the resident.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Introduction to Academic Prose
catalog.description: This course introduces students to college-level reading, writing, and rhetorical analysis. Students will analyze and create texts, focusing on threshold concepts of writing, multiple rhetorical situations, and cultural matters related to writing. Students will also learn to analyze, revise and edit their own work, and use academic documentation.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Literary Monstrosities
catalog.description: This course explores representations of monsters in literature. Students are introduced to different ways of thinking about monstrosities from a range of cultural and historical perspectives, as well as through a variety of materials in order to approach this question from an interdisciplinary perspective.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Writing About Literature
catalog.description: This course is designed to be taken either prior to or concurrent with a student's first literature course. It introduces students to literary criticism in its broadest, most generic sense, as a stylized response to reading. Students in the course will be introduced to different approaches to writing about literature, to methods of generating ideas, and focusing and developing a topic.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Popular Literature
catalog.description: This course is designed to help students develop a fuller understanding of the human condition by exploring a range of accessible, bestselling fiction and non-fiction from a variety of periods and places, historic and contemporary. The course may include popular stories, songs and ballads, the scripts of blockbuster plays and films, best-selling novels, and widely distributed nonfictional prose.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Introduction To Undergraduate Study In English
catalog.description: An investigation of reading, writing, and research practices associated with studies in English. Students will learn about multiple forms, genres, and critical approaches, as well as encounter texts from various historical periods and places.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: World Literature in English
catalog.description: This course helps students develop a fuller understanding of the human condition by exploring accessible literary texts in English by non Euro-American writers. The course provides historical, economic and political contexts and is designed for students who enjoy learning about global cultures by reading and discussing a diverse range of bestselling literature.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Introduction To Drama
catalog.description: Beginning with an intensive study of a few plays analyzed to elicit general principles, the course moves on to consider several representative examples of each of the major periods and types of Western drama, from the Greeks to the present.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Introduction To Fiction
catalog.description: Students will be introduced to the study of fiction as a literary art form. Students will continue to develop their understanding of fiction-writing in preparation for more advanced courses in literature and creative writing. Coursework will focus on close reading of short and long forms of fiction selected from a range of literary periods and world literature. Students are expected to interpret and analyze various forms of fiction and write critically about the role of fiction as a form of cultural discourse.

catalog.subject: ENGLISH
catalog.title: Introduction To Poetry
