catalog.description: This introductory course is designed to give an overview of a wide variety of technical, interpersonal, documentation, and managerial skills needed to become an effective systems administrator.

catalog.subject: INFO-TEC
catalog.title: Database Administration
catalog.description: This course covers, database administration, setup and tuning of DBMS. Not for Graduate credit.

catalog.subject: INFO-TEC
catalog.title: Data Analytics
catalog.description: This course introduces the essential characteristics of diversified data and its vast applications in real world. Students learn how to collect, store, process, and report massive amounts of structured and unstructured data according to principles of data science lifecycle. The course also examines how scope of data analysis methodologies can guide to select right statistical or machine learning models for decision making. A literature review of the latest research articles / case-studies and student’s presentation is emphasized to promote student-centered learning. The practical part of this course covers development of predictive models using python.

catalog.subject: INFO-TEC
catalog.title: Practical Network Security
catalog.description: This course examines common threats to computer network security and discusses various techniques to mitigate those threats. The course material is supplemented with lab assignments that implement network security tools and use them to build a small secure network. It discusses information hiding, traffic monitoring and control, intrusion detection, and security policy. Note: NOT FOR GRADUATE CREDIT.

catalog.subject: INFO-TEC
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Selected topics in specific areas of Information Technology/ Computer Science. May be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.subject: INFO-TEC
catalog.title: Internship
catalog.description: Students may participate in structured internships under the joint supervision of an employer and a faculty member. The student must carry out significant professional responsibilities that also have academic merit. The number of credit hours is based on the quality of the academic experience. Available for credit/no credit only, and students must be in good standing with a least 18 credit hours of CS/IT counting towards the degree.

catalog.subject: ITALIAN
catalog.title: Elementary Italian I
catalog.description: Intended to give the student the ability to read prose of ordinary difficulty and to understand and speak simple Italian.

catalog.subject: ITALIAN
catalog.title: Elementary Italian II
catalog.description: Continuation of ITALIAN 110 .

catalog.subject: ITALIAN
catalog.title: Special Intermediate Italian Topics I
catalog.description: Instruction of Italian on the second-year/intermediate level introducing new methods of foreign language teaching or special texts and topics not normally offered through regular courses. May not be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: LATIN
catalog.title: Elementary Latin I
catalog.description: Elementary Latin I introduces students with no previous Latin experience to the fundamentals of Latin grammar. The course is continued with LATIN 120 .

catalog.subject: LATIN
catalog.title: Elementary Latin II
catalog.description: Elementary Latin II is a continuation of LATIN 110 . This course focuses on the fundamentals of Latin grammar and morphology, and students will read longer Latin passages.

catalog.subject: LATIN
catalog.title: Second Year Latin Readings I
catalog.description: This course introduces students to extended readings from Roman authors in Latin. Students’ knowledge of basic Latin grammar, vocabulary, and morphology will be reviewed and reinforced.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Method
catalog.description: This course will provide an introduction to legal reasoning and analysis, including reading cases, statutes, and regulations; case synthesis and application to facts, statutes and regulations; and standards of review

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: US Legal Framework
catalog.description: This course will provide an introduction to the U.S. Legal System, including the powers of the different branches of government, checks and balances on governmental powers, function and importance of the Constitution, the importance of judicial power and the common law, the role of administrative regulation, and the functioning and importance of Federalism. The course will also provide an introduction to the foundational areas of legal study such as contracts, torts, property, criminal law, civil procedure and constitutional law.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Professional Writing with Legal Issues
catalog.description: This course will provide instruction in effective written communication when dealing with legal issues, including structure, style, and citation. Written formats will include email, letters, memoranda, and guidelines.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Research for Non-Lawyer Professionals
catalog.description: Introduction to research sources in the U.S. and techniques to systematically process and solve basic legal research problems found in professional settings involving law but without direct supervision of lawyers.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Professional Ethics
catalog.description: Students will explore basics of ethical reasoning and the influence of communities of practice in organizational settings and learn about the professional regulation of legal services and the professional responsibilities of attorneys through problem study and discussion.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Learning from the Work Environment
catalog.description: This course will explore dimensions of professional development of non-lawyers in a work environment, including the capacity for reflection, deliberate improvement in knowledge and skills, and the ability to form meaningful professional relationships with lawyer and non-lawyers. Students will have an opportunity to reflect on and analyze professional ethics in the context of the work environment.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Capstone Portfolio
catalog.description: This course gives students the opportunity to reflect on their achievement of the learning outcomes for the MLS program. Students will collect, showcase, and present work product completed during the program. Assignments will include reflection papers, assembling a portfolio, preparing a final presentation to a panel, answering questions about achievement of the learning outcomes and demonstrating competence in the learning outcomes for the program.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Master of Legal Studies Bridge
catalog.description: This course is designed to allow JD students to transition from the JD program to the MLS program. The course will supplement the student’s JD training so that student’s educational program will meet the objectives of the MLS program. This course has flexibility in the modules that may be included depending on the needs of the individual student.
catalog.prerequisites: At least one semester (15 credit hours) of courses in the JD program

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Contract Formation, Review and Drafting
catalog.description: Introduction to contract law doctrines, the method and practice of contract review, and basic elements of contract drafting

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Privacy Regulation
catalog.description: Provides a basic overview of laws that regulate privacy and provide security and protection of personal data including the common law, various federal laws (such as HIPAA and FTC regulation) and state privacy laws

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Wellness Compliance
catalog.description: Provides a basic overview of laws that influence the impact of a wellness program or business, including laws such as federal incentive law, HIPAA and data privacy, civil rights discrimination, state licensure and scope of practice laws, and FDA regulation of wellness products and devices

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Health Care Compliance
catalog.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of health care compliance using the topics covered by the Health Care Compliance Association (HCCA) as a guide, including such topics as compliance administration, policies and procedures, oversight and committees, enforcement and reporting requirements, screening of employees and vendors, billing and coding basics, auditing and monitoring, education and training, investigations, fraud and abuse laws, and HIPPA

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Corporate Compliance
catalog.description: Provides a basic overview of compliance systems used for corporations and other businesses, including various federal and state laws such as the Securities Act, the Securities Exchange Act, Sarbanes Oxley, Dodd-Frank, and Corporate Transparency Act as well as applicable state laws such as a state’s General Corporation Law, and the actions required to comply with those laws such as policies, training, reports and filings.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Equal Employment Opportunity Compliance
catalog.description: This course will address compliance with various employment and anti-discrimination laws by covering topics such as employment at will, wage and hour law, and law related to various types of discrimination, including race, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity, age, religion, and disability.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Technology Competency
catalog.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to advance their knowledge in the software skills used by professionals who work on legal issues including word processing, visual communications, cloud computing, document automation, data analytics, and project management.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Administrative Law
catalog.description: Introduction to the administrative process; role, function and processes of administrative agencies; policy issues of administrative government; judicial review of agencies and regulations

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity & the Law
catalog.description: This course will examine the evolving status of sexual orientation and gender identity in the law. The course will start with a brief history of the LGBT+ rights movement, before looking at issues that arise with relation to sexual orientation and gender identity. Subjects covered include criminal justice and the penal system, public accommodations, employment discrimination, domestic relations, treatment and care of LGBT+ youth, and the Constitution.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Insurance Law
catalog.description: Nature of insurance, nature of insurance contract, special rules of construction, standard policy provisions, first-party and third-party insurance; principles of insurance regulation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Law, Medicine and Bioethics
catalog.description: A study of bioethics and selected legal and ethical issues in medicine with focus on decision-making at the beginning and end of life; reproductive rights and assisted reproductive technologies; the patient-provider relationship (fiduciary, treatment, confidentiality, and disclosure obligations); physician obligations of informed consent and patient care issues; potential hospital and physician liability for medical malpractice; and end of life decision-making (withdrawal and refusal of life sustaining treatment by individuals and their surrogates) and physician-assisted suicide.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Environmental Compliance, Auditing and Permitting
catalog.description: This course provides students with an overview of key federal environmental statutes and their inter-relationships, including the Clean Water Act, the Clean Air Act, the Emergency Planning and Community Right to Know Act and the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act. Students will learn about inspections, enforcement and liability, environmental management systems and auditing; and generally, how Congress and the EPA formulate environmental law and regulations and the roles in the processes for the legislature, regulators, regulated communities, citizens, and public interest groups.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Liability and Quality Issues in Healthcare
catalog.description: This is a survey course in Health Law focused on learning the players in our healthcare system. Topics include the laws effecting the relationship among patients, health care providers, and health care payers, licensing, quality control, negligence, confidentiality, the obligation to provide care, and commercial health insurance.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Regulation, Organization, and Finance of Healthcare
catalog.description: This course examines the laws concerning the organization, delivery, and finance of health care in the United States.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Employment Discrimination Law
catalog.description: Substantive and procedural aspects of Equal Employment Opportunity Act and related matters

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Employment Law
catalog.description: Survey of legal doctrines regulating the employment relationship, including the regulation of wages, hours and benefits; privacy in the workplace; workers' compensation; suits for suits for wrongful termination; non-competition agreements; and unemployment compensation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Disabilities and the Law
catalog.description: An interdisciplinary study of the law relating to disabled persons in the areas of employment, education, and access to transportation, health, welfare and social services to provide an understanding of how the law affects individuals with disabilities and public and private entities. Legislation considered include the American with Disabilities Act, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, the individuals with Disabilities Education Act, the Family and Medical leave Act, the Fair Housing Act, the Voting Accessibility for the Elderly and Handicapped Act, and the Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Contracts
catalog.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of contract law in the United States. Specifically, the course addresses components of these topics: contract formation, alternate forms of enforcing promises, the rights and obligations of a contract, including interpretation principles, defenses and justifications, contract performance obligations, excuses for nonperformance, breach of contract, and remedies. Students will be introduced to sections of the Uniform Commercial Code relating to sales of goods and may be introduced to the sections of the Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Contracts
catalog.description: This course reinforces and further explores the complexity of topics introduced in Contracts ( LAW 8501 ), including a deeper study of sections of the Uniform Commercial Code relating to the sale of goods. The course also will introduce concepts of contract law that are normally not covered in LAW 8501 , such as third-party beneficiaries and novation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Torts
catalog.description: Wrongs to the person and to property; legal remedies through which compensation or other relief may be obtained.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Applied Intentional Torts
catalog.description: This course will cover intentional torts, including battery, assault, false imprisonment, intentional infliction of emotional distress, defamation, and privacy rights. Importantly, this course will not only teach the doctrine of torts, it will teach students how to prepare for classes in general by explaining how to study, brief cases, outline, and take exams.
catalog.prerequisites: Students must have completed two semesters of law school, including Torts LAW 8511 . Students also need instructor permission to take the course.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Civil Procedure
catalog.description: This course presents the fundamentals of civil litigation in United States courts. The course addresses these topics: where a case may be filed and heard (including subject-matter jurisdiction, removal, remand, personal jurisdiction, and venue), how a case is initiated and shaped (including pleading standards, service of process, amendments and relation back, joinder of claims and parties, discovery, and the Erie doctrine on choice of law), how disputes are resolved (including dismissal, summary judgment, trial, judgment as a matter of law, and appellate procedure), and the effect of judgments (including claim and issue preclusion). Throughout, the course emphasizes the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and related statutes.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Civil Procedure - Jurisdiction
catalog.description: This course examines where civil disputes may be heard and which law will govern them. Students study the structure and functions of state and federal court systems; doctrines of personal jurisdiction and venue; federal subject-matter jurisdiction (including diversity, federal-question, removal, and remand); and the interaction of these rules with choice-of-law principles. The course also addresses claim and issue preclusion and considers how evolving personal-jurisdiction standards reflect underlying policy choices and allocate discretion to judges.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Discovery Practice in Civil Litigation
catalog.description: This course focuses on the various discovery techniques which are commonly used in federal civil practice, and also compares state procedures. General topics include the uses of discovery, informal discovery, building the discovery plan, ethical issues, privileges and protections, the discovery tools, electronic discovery, experts, motions to compel discovery, and sanctions.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Electronic Discovery
catalog.description: Discovery practice and laws related to electronically stored information in litigation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Civil Procedure: War or Justice
catalog.description: This course considers problems in civil dispute resolution from a philosophical perspective. Students learn to identify relevant criteria for evaluating a civil dispute resolution system and how to assess the extent to which the current system and alternatives satisfy those criteria.
catalog.prerequisites: LAW 8521 Civil Procedure -- Pleadings OR LAW 8522 Civil Procedure -- Jurisdiction

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyering Skills I
catalog.description: Introduction to legal reasoning; case analysis and synthesis; case research; structure and style in legal writing with emphasis on expository writing, including office memoranda.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Common Law, Legal Analysis & Writing
catalog.description: Introduction to legal reasoning; case analysis and synthesis; case research; structure and style in legal writing with emphasis on expository writing, including office memoranda.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyering Skills II
catalog.description: Introduction to advocacy; introduction to interviewing, counseling and negotiation; statutory and computerized research; writing to and on behalf of a client, including a trial or appellate brief; oral advocacy.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Introduction to American Legal Skills
catalog.description: Introduction to oral and written advocacy; interviewing, counseling and negotiation; and alternative dispute resolution.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: American Legal Research
catalog.description: Introduction to research resources in the U.S. and techniques to systematically process and solve basic research problems found in law practice.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Property
catalog.description: The course provides an introduction to the nature of property; basic personal property law; adverse possession; possessory estates; basic future interests; marital and concurrent interests; landlord-tenant relationships.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Property
catalog.description: The course covers the law of licenses, easements, real covenants, equitable servitudes; nuisances; basic water law; brokerage; financing, mortgages, deeds of trust; contract of sale, deeds, closing; title insurance, warranties; recording; eminent domain; zoning.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Adverse Possession
catalog.description: Explores the ancient yet evolving subject of adverse possession as it applies to real property in the United States and around the world. Topics explored include: the ancient doctrine as developed under the common law, the variety of statutory refinements to adverse possession doctrine in the United States and modern attempts to statutorily limit the doctrine, and comparative perspectives on adverse possession including the abrogation of the doctrine in Canada, and the effects of that abrogation on resolution of property disputes there.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Federal Taxation
catalog.description: Theory, history, and principles of federal income taxation; basic concepts of income, classification of income and deductions.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: The study of a contemporary topic of interest. This course is designed to facilitate one of two purposes: an initial offering of a new course (prior to formal approval) or an initial and possible only offering of new topics.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Business Organizations
catalog.description: Partnership, limited liability company and corporation law; choice of business forms, formation of partnerships, limited liability companies and corporations; rights, duties, and powers of partners, members, shareholders, directors, and officers; closely held corporations; proxy regulation; derivative suites; dividends and stock redemptions; introduction to the Securities Act of 1933 and Securities Exchange Act of 1934.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Corporate Governance
catalog.description: This course explores the corporate governance universe by examining key players in corporate governance and the mechanics that make corporations tick. It focuses on public companies, and sheds light on strengths and weaknesses of the current corporate governance model. The course surveys the relationship between corporations and civic society, and investigates solutions to ameliorate current corporate governance shortcomings

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Corporations, Law, and Technology
catalog.description: This course pioneers unexplored spaces at the junction of corporate law, technology (e.g., artificial intelligence, social media, mobile-first investing apps, etc.), and society. It examines the legal framework that governs the relationship between corporate governance and technology, and investigates how technology affects—and will affect—corporate law and policy. Examples of topics discussed in this course include: the role of artificial intelligence in corporate governance, opportunities and risks for corporate governance generated by mobile-first investing apps, finfluencers, and investomers.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: International Criminal Tribunals
catalog.description: This course will examine the types of international criminal tribunals available for the prosecution of individuals accused of war crimes, the crime of aggression, crimes against humanity, and genocide. The course will begin with an introduction to the history of international criminal law and a comparative examination of various international criminal tribunals, including the Nuremberg trials, ad hoc criminal tribunals (ICTY and ICTR), the permanent International Criminal Court in The Hague, and hybrid criminal tribunals (Cambodia, Lebanon, and Sierra Leone). The course will then focus more specifically on the International Criminal Court (ICC), including the ICC’s formation and jurisdiction and examples of individuals and situations investigated and prosecuted thus far by the court. Prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.
catalog.prerequisites: Part of the Ireland Law Program.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Transactional Lawyering Skills Lab
catalog.description: Students are trained in counseling clients and negotiating business formation, dissolution, and liability issues as well as drafting appropriate documents.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Doing Business In Ireland, Part I
catalog.description: A survey of International Trade Law and European and American Competition Law that impact on American multinational companies operating in the Republic of Ireland.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Doing Business in Ireland, Part II
catalog.description: A survey of the Ireland Company Law and comparative United States Corporate Law and a survey of United States corporate taxation of multinational companies operating in Ireland.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: International Field Experience
catalog.description: In connection with relevant coursework, this limited international field experience will permit students to visit a foreign country to see the application of their coursework in a comparative perspective, including tours of legal facilities, visits with experts from the host country, and service learning opportunities. Prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.
catalog.prerequisites: Permission of instructor and designated accompanying coursework.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Taxation Of Business Organization
catalog.description: Survey course of the taxation of business enterprises, particularly partnerships, corporations and subchapter S corporations.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Business and Personal Finance
catalog.description: This course is an introduction to the basic concepts of finance in the legal context (such as financial statements, the use and misuse of statistics, interest rates, debt, and valuations).
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Antitrust And Fair Competition Law
catalog.description: This course examines fair competition law as a body of law designed to protect consumers. Understanding fair competition law requires looking at Supreme Court case law but also lower court decisions, economic analysis, and government enforcement guidelines and policy statements.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Ethical Issues In Family Law Representation
catalog.description: Advanced study of the ethical obligations of public and private attorneys in estate, family, and juvenile law representation. Topics may include identification of the client, ethical and legal obligations of confidentiality and disclosure, competence and client communication, respect for third persons (particularly obligations toward children of clients) and other related subjects. Paper and presentation required. When offered for 2 credit hours, the course fulfills the Schools Professional Responsibility graduation requirement.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Introduction to Trusts
catalog.description: This course explores the law of trusts, including the elements of a valid trust, its creation, administration and termination, the nature of a beneficiary's interest, and the fiduciary duties of trustees.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Estates And Trusts
catalog.description: Intestate succession; testamentary dispositions; execution, modification, and revocation of wills; will contests; advancements, ademption, and exoneration; family allowances; rights of estate creditors; express, implied, resulting, and constructive trusts; basic tax aspects of estates and trusts; rule against perpetuities; will substitutes.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Estate Planning and Drafting Lab
catalog.description: Students are assigned to attorneys at law firms or trust departments and will work on estate planning projects assigned by the supervising attorney. Exams may include drafting will and trust instruments, researching legal issues, and drafting memos.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Estate Planning For Retirement Plan Benefits
catalog.description: The income, gift, estate and generation-skipping transfer tax consequences and rules related to the ownership, distribution and withdrawal of retirement plan benefits, including minimum required distributions, designating beneficiaries, spousal rights and rollover options

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Estate Planning For Charitable Giving
catalog.description: Survey of federal income tax and transfer tax laws governing gifts to charitable organizations, charitable remainder trusts and charitable lead trusts; procedural requirements to assure deductibility; and planning and drafting considerations.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Elder Law For Estate Planners
catalog.description: An examination of the legal tools available for the elderly client for decision-making, both health care and financial, in the event of incapacity, and asset preservation, including Medicare and Medicaid qualification. The course will cover the use of trust; durable powers of attorney, and advance directives for health care and living wills and the relationship to court guardianship.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Evidence
catalog.description: General principles relating to proof of facts in civil and criminal trials; presumptions; order of proof; relevancy; judicial notice; real and demonstrative evidence; authentication; best evidence rule; hearsay; competency; impeachment; rehabilitation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Constitutional Law
catalog.description: Core issues relating to the U.S. Constitution, including the doctrine of judicial review, the powers of Congress and the President, limitations on state power, and judicial protection of individual rights.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Second Amendment – Historical and Constitutional Foundation
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the historical and constitutional foundation for the Second Amendment. The course centers on theories of judicial interpretation and the differences between “collective” and “individual” rights. Students will evaluate historical documents and the constitutional text to argue the intent of the language used in the Second Amendment.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: First Amendment Law
catalog.description: Basic themes and advanced problems relating to the law of the First Amendment to the United States Constitution, including exploration of the values behind the protection, subversive advocacy, regulation of speech in the public forum, access to the media, regulation of the press, symbolic expression, libel, obscenity, commercial speech, picketing, right of association, loyalty oaths, legislative investigations and government demands for information, separation of church and state, free exercise of religion, state aid to the religious schools, regulation of religion-based conduct.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Law and Religion
catalog.description: Explores the interaction of the legal system with religious beliefs and institutions. The course examines issues such as the establishment and free exercise clauses of the United States Constitution, the influence of religion in law making, and religion issues presented in famous trials.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Criminal Law
catalog.description: Introduction to substantive criminal law, its role and purpose in our society; principles of liability, common law and statutory offenses; defenses; punishment.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: International Criminal Law
catalog.description: An introductory course in International Criminal Law focusing on the criminal prosecution of individuals under international law, primarily by international tribunals (or 'hybrid' international/national tribunals) and secondarily by national tribunals applying international law. The course will include a consideration of aspects of criminal law that are common to most criminal legal systems, with a particular focus on those crimes that are 'international;' will revisit the concept of criminal jurisdiction, how it is acquired, and its limitations, such as immunity for heads of state and diplomats; and will examine the elements of war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocide, as well as a few other crimes of international concern; and excuses or justifications under international law, such as self-defense and insanity.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Criminal Procedure I
catalog.description: Introduction to the administration of criminal justice; constitutional rights of the accused; due process; privilege against self-incrimination; right to counsel; arrest, search, and seizure; wire-tapping; police interrogation and confessions; pre-trial identification procedures.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Wrongful Convictions
catalog.description: An examination of the causes of wrongful convictions, a consideration of systemic reforms that might minimize convicting the innocent and a focus on recurring ethical issues that confront prosecutors and criminal defense lawyers. Students also will work with The Midwestern Innocence Project on cases of possible actual innocence.This course provides an insider's look into the operation of the criminal justice system and is designed to help students gain insight into features of the criminal justice system that have a tendency to produce wrongful convictions. It should be of particular interest to any student interested in working in a prosecutor's office, public defender's office or for a firm doing defense work. It is a prerequisite for any student wishing to enroll in the Innocence Project clinic. Limited enrollment (normally, up to 16 students)

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Criminal Procedure II
catalog.description: Continuation of the study of the administration of criminal justice; exclusionary rules; bail; prosecutor's discretion; grand jury; preliminary hearing; jurisdiction, venue; joinder and severance of offenses and defendants; right to speedy trial; pleas of guilty; discovery; trial by jury; publicity; double jeopardy.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Federal Trial Practice
catalog.description: A practical skills course involving consideration and application of the rules of procedure and evidence to civil and criminal cases brought in federal court, including, but not limited to the legal requirements of federal jury instructions, motions in limine, pretrial preparation, pretrial conferences, notice requirements, voir dire, opening statements, direct and cross, evidentiary foundations for exhibits, computerized and computer-related evidence, character and related evidence, witnesses (lay, lay opinion, summary, character, experts), and closing arguments.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Criminal Pretrial Practice
catalog.description: The course provides instruction in basic (non-trial) skills and knowledge of law required of practicing prosecutors and defense attorneys. Students will learn how to effectively prosecute a case and represent a criminal defense client in pretrial proceedings. This course provides legal instruction and skills training in the stages from criminal arraignment through plea and sentencing.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: U.S. Attorney's Office Law Externship
catalog.description: US Attorney’s Office legal externs work in the United States Attorney's Office directly with Assistant US Attorneys (AUSA’s) in one of the Criminal Division units. Activities include legal research and drafting memoranda, motions and briefs; observations and participation in trials, pre-trial hearings, and motions, as appropriate; and general assistance with litigation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Entrepreneurial Lawyering: Solo and Small Firm Practice
catalog.description: Course will focus on law practice management for solo and small firms. Topics include organizational structure, firm management, fee setting and allocation, and effective and ethical marketing. Course includes attendance at the Missouri Bar Solo and Small Firm Conference.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Practice Technology Skills
catalog.description: The course will familiarize students with the basic legal technologies necessary for the twenty-first century lawyer. Course topics include hardware, system architecture, security, practice management, productivity, the cloud, and social media-networking.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: AI and the Law
catalog.description: Students will learn to how AI works generally, its positive uses, and the issues it creates in research and writing, ethics, privacy, copyright, libel, job displacement, “deep fakes,” manipulation of media, elections, and national security. The course will cover the developing bodies of regulatory and case law regarding these issues.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Tech-Competency Training
catalog.description: This course provides students with the opportunity to gain advanced knowledge in the software skills needed by legal practitioners, including: word processing, visual communication, cloud computing, document automation, data analytics, and project management.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Document Assembly
catalog.description: Document automation and assembly can help attorneys more efficiently and accurately deliver legal services to the public and their employer--thus helping attorneys be more competitive in the legal services market place. This two-credit hour course will teach students the skills necessary for document automation and familiarize them with HotDocs, the predominant provider of document assembly applications. Students will produce programmed documents, interviews, and systems for estate planning, businesses planning, or such other projects as are suitable for document assembly. The course may be taught over an eight week period or a summer term. No computer programming experience is required.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Data, Decisions, & Justice
catalog.description: The course will offer an Introduction to data-driven decision making. It will compare artificial and human intelligence, considering issues of accuracy, transparency, fairness, bias, and legal regulation. Students will explore the use of data analytics in a variety of contexts, including the sentencing of criminal defendants, assessing creditworthiness, hiring employees, and forecasting judicial decisions. This course is designed to be fully accessible to those with no prior background in statistics or coding.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Statutes and Regulations
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the centrality of statutes and regulations in U.S. law. Using a variety of examples, the course explores statutory interpretation, the legislative process, and the role of public law and administrative regulation, with emphasis on lawyering skills in reading and applying statutes and regulations. Topics covered include creation of state and federal statutes and regulations (including introduction to the Administrative Procedure Act), judicial review of agency action, the nature and role of administrative agencies and related policy debates, and agency adjudication.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legislation
catalog.description: This course explores a variety of topics under the broad heading of 'Legislation.' Included among them are: electoral and representational structures, legislative drafting, canons of statutory interpretation, identifying and utilizing legislative history, the role of referendums and initiatives as a supplement to representative institutions, public choice theory, and other theories of legislation. The course also includes an opportunity for students to participate in the drafting of legislation for the Kansas for Missouri State legislatures. Paper optional.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Data Privacy & Cybersecurity Litigation
catalog.description: This course explores the evolving legal landscape of data privacy and cybersecurity through the lens of litigation. Students will examine statutory and regulatory frameworks, analyze real-world caselaw, and develop practical litigation skills. Topics include federal and state wiretap laws, biometric privacy, breach notification, website tracking, and class-action strategy. Students will engage in drafting exercises, litigation simulations, and strategic analysis of emerging technologies. The course is designed to prepare students for practice in privacy litigation, regulatory enforcement, and compliance counseling.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Applied Legal Research: Competitive Intelligence and Due Diligence
catalog.description: This course develops the skills necessary to search publicly available information to find vital facts about individuals, businesses, organizations, markets, and industries, and conduct so-called “due diligence” investigations. The first focus is on using public records, commercial services, and company information to gather information about parties. The second focus is on data and statistics, including finding, processing, and interpreting that information.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Applied Legal Research: Foreign, Comparative and International Law
catalog.description: The course is designed to familiarize students with the basic resources of international law by taking an in-depth look at foreign and comparative law resources, teaching students how to utilize and think systematically about those resources and instructing students in the strategies and processes necessary to conduct scholarly research and practice international law. Students taking the course will improve their research competency in authorizing scholarly papers with a comparative or international perspective.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Legal Research-Litigation
catalog.description: Prepares students who wish to focus on advocacy and litigation (including students in litigation with respect to Family Law and Urban, Land Use and Environmental law). The course is also intended to facilitate research for the student's upper-level writing requirement. The course will refresh and refine research skills, help students to think systemically about legal research, and familiarize students with applicable resources. As the final project, students will have the opportunity to develop an in-depth research 'path finder' or guide for an approved topic of their own choosing.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Applied Legal Research: Transactional Law
catalog.description: This course prepares students who wish to focus on transactional law for the research component of the practice. The course is also intended to facilitate research for the student's upper-level writing requirement, although it does not satisfy the writing requirement. The course will refresh and refine research skills, help students to think systemically about legal research, and familiarize students with applicable resources relevant to transactional law including business organizations, tax, pension, labor and employment, competitive business intelligence, real estate, securities, sale of businesses, etc. As the final project, students will have the opportunity to develop an in-depth research 'path finder' or guide for an approved topic of their own choosing.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Developing Legal Research Skills
catalog.description: Course content includes an introduction to mental constructs and thinking about legal research problems, exercises in how to work problems, working with various “problem types,” exercises to understand the terrain of legal research resources based on the characteristics of such resources, building a library for particular legal specialties, building a three-dimensional map of legal research resources based on their fundamental characteristics, aligning problem types with the best resources and techniques, exercises in the legal research process, and concludes with a “Pathfinder” on a subject withing a legal field of the student’s choosing.
catalog.prerequisites: Lawyering Skills I ( LAW 8531 ) and Lawyering Skills II ( LAW 8532 ).

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Access to Justice Self-Help Clinic
catalog.description: An estimated 60% of people in civil cases go to court without a lawyer, usually because they cannot afford or access attorneys. In this clinic, student provide access to legal information and advice for these individuals. Students work in the Self-Help Clinic at UMKC, in collaboration with Legal Aid of Western Missouri, providing brief advice, referral, and limited scope representation. Clinic students will expand the reach of the clinic by building and assisting in conducting pro-se clinics for common legal problems. Clinic students will use technology to build tools for self-represented clients to understand and access their legal rights.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class. Permission of instructor

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Race and the Law Seminar
catalog.description: In-depth examination of the role that race plays in American society as a whole and in judicial decision-making in particular. Course will examine the effect of race on various areas of the law, including torts, contracts, property, criminal law, and criminal procedure. Course will also examine the effect of race on jury decisions and explore the concept of implicit bias. Research paper.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Veterans and the Law
catalog.description: This course will introduce students to the laws governing the administration of federal veterans’ benefits, and the military discharge upgrade process. Students will learn about the military veteran experience and the challenges veterans face after separating from active-duty service with a “bad paper” discharge. Students will be introduced to the laws governing the administration of benefits from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and the military discharge upgrade process. The focus of the course will be on how lawyers can help veterans overcome the obstacles preventing them from obtaining benefits from the VA.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Missouri Public Defender's Office Externship
catalog.description: Public Defender Trial Externs assist in the defense of indigent criminal defendants. Each extern is assigned to a single public defender to allow the extern to observe the life and practice of a public defender, including direct engagement with client (fact development and defense strategy), case file analysis, research, drafting, and exposure to all stages of court proceedings. This is a two-semester externship providing a progression of skill building. Students eligible for Rule 13 student practice authorization may present directly in court.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Missouri Attorney General's Office Externship
catalog.description: Law Externs work side by side with Assistant Attorneys General in the Kansas City regional office representing the State of Missouri in civil or criminal proceedings. Law externs may be placed in one or more of the divisions of the AG’s office: financial services, litigation, labor, consumer protection, public safety, or governmental affairs. Students eligible for Rule 13 student practice authorization may appear in court. Students may appear in Jackson, Clay, Platte, and/or Cass Counties.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Jackson County Prosecutor Externship-Family Law Prosecution
catalog.description: Family Law Prosecution Externs assist Jackson County Prosecutor’s Office, Child Support Division, in prosecuting cases involving paternity establishment and child support. The externship provides formalized instruction, and individual mentoring and supervision from assistant prosecutors.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Federal Public Defender Externship
catalog.description: Federal Defender Externs work in the Federal Public Defender's Office, under attorney supervision to engage with clients; undertake legal research; draft memoranda, motions and briefs; observe and participate in trials, pre-trial hearings and motion hearings; and assist, in general, with litigation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Government Externship
catalog.description: This course provides a substantial lawyering experience for students in government law offices (executive agencies or legislative offices) working on active matters that include advising or direct representation, under the supervision of a licensed attorney. The student’s work will include multiple opportunities for performance of legal skills, feedback, guided reflection, and self-critique. In most instances this course will be paired with a companion seminar. The supervising attorney, student, and faculty advisor sign a three-way agreement defining their respective roles and responsibilities at the beginning of the semester.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Non-Profit /Pro Bono Externship
catalog.description: This course provides a substantial lawyering experience for students in public interest and non-profit organizations working on active legal matters that include advising or direct representation, under the supervision of a licensed attorney. The student’s work will include multiple opportunities for performance of legal skills, feedback, guided reflection, and self-critique. In most instances this course is paired with a mandatory companion seminar. The supervising attorney, student, and faculty advisor sign a three-way agreement defining their respective roles and responsibilities at the beginning of the semester.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Jackson County Prosecutor Externship
catalog.description: Law externs work with attorneys of the Jackson County Prosecuting Attorney's Office in downtown Kansas City and Independence offices. Externs are assigned to specific units: General Crimes, Violent Crimes, Sexual Violence, Warrant Desk, or Independence Office. The externship provides practical experience, courtroom exposure, and an introduction to prosecution hearings and trials. The externship is a two-semester progression of fieldwork allowing students opportunities to build skills and confidence. Students eligible for Rule 13 student practice authorization may present directly in court.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Federal Court Externship
catalog.description: Federal Court Externs serve in a clerkship with a judge or magistrate in a federal court, principally in the Western District of Missouri. With approval of the faculty director of externships, students may also extern with federal judges in different states. Students generally undertake research, draft memoranda and other documents, observe court, and debrief with judges and clerks regarding the legal issues and lawyering styles in the matters before the court.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Family Court Externship
catalog.description: Family Court Externs serve in the chambers of Family Law judges and commissioners and observe mediation, conciliation, adult abuse docket, and cross-court visits. The externship offers students an opportunity to gain practical legal skills, learn about the programs ordered by the judges to assist families in crisis, and develop a working knowledge of the Family Court Division. Family Court judges hear a wide range of matter concerning families, marriage, and children, including marriage (dissolution, annulments, maintenance), child custody, paternity, child support, adult abuse, juvenile delinquency, adoptions, and guardianships.
catalog.prerequisites: LAW 8521 and LAW 8751 (completed or currently enrolled).

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Missouri Court of Appeals Internship
catalog.description: Appellate Court Interns work in the chambers of a Missouri Court of Appeals Judge. Students generally undertake research, draft memoranda, and produce substantial written work under the supervision of the judge or the judge’s clerks. They also observe various proceedings (both in chambers and in the courtroom) and interact with the judges, their clerks, and court staff. Students debrief with judges and clerks regarding the legal issues and lawyering styles of the matters and advocates before the court.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Animal Law
catalog.description: This course will begin with a brief overview of the philosophical and cultural issues underlying human/animal relationships, including basic theories of the legal systems's responses to social change. Legal issues relating to food animals, companion animals, laboratory animals, wild animals, and performing animals will be examined with reference to: (1) federal statues (Animal Welfare Act, Endangered Species Act, Marine Mammal Protection Act, Wild Horses and Burros Act, Animal Damage Control Act, National Wildlife Refuge System Administration Act, Refuge Recreation Act, National Environment Police Act, and Humane Slaughter Act); (2) state statues (anti-cruelty, wills and trusts, hunting, racing and fighting statues); (3) local animal control regulations; and (4) extensive common law (standing, rights, free exercise of religion, property, landlord-tenant disputes, torts, marital dissolution and custody, and bailment).

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Trial Advocacy I
catalog.description: A practical skills course in advocacy which introduces students to the fundamental components of a typical civil and criminal trial and requires students to perform exercises involving each component and try a mock civil or criminal case from provided problem materials.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Drafting Civil Jury Instructions
catalog.description: Covering the essential skills in drafting appropriate civil jury instructions and preserving objections for appeal in civil cases. This is a 'skills course' in which students learn the fundamentals of drafting and arguing civil jury instructions.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Taking and Defending Depositions
catalog.description: introduces the fundamentals of depositions, concluding with a mock deposition. Topical coverage includes: what is a deposition and what is the purpose of depositions; who may be deposed and when; deposition questioning; using exhibits; objections; preparing for the deposition; and producing a witness for deposition. Each student will take and/or defend a mock deposition.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Conflict of Laws
catalog.description: Domicile; jurisdiction and limitations on the exercise of jurisdiction; judgments; full faith and credit; choice of law; conflicts problems in federal and international settings; conflicts problems in selected areas.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Trial Advocacy II
catalog.description: A practical skills course in the art of trial advocacy with an emphasis on technique, style, and methods of persuasion. During class sessions, students perform exercises involving the various stages of a law suit, and are critiqued on their performances. Following performance of the exercises, students are divided into teams and try a mock case in a trial competition, from which the Law School's National Trial Competition Teams are selected. The trials are evaluated by trial lawyers and federal or state judges. Limited enrollment.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyering Skills Competition-Appellate
catalog.description: This course is limited to students who represent the law school in faculty supervised regional, national or international lawyering skills competitions. These competitions require application of lawyering skills in a range of substantive law areas and intensive practice of lawyering skills, judged by faculty and practitioners in the field. Students enrolled in this course will be representing the school in various moot court appellate advocacy competitions. Students will research and draft briefs or equivalent advocacy documents, develop oral arguments, conduct practice oral arguments before a range of student, faculty, and practitioner judges, and represent the law school in regional national or international competitions.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyering Skills Competition-Client Counseling Team
catalog.description: The course is limited to students who represent the law school in faculty supervised regional, national or international lawyering skills competitions. Students enrolled in this course will be representing the school in the client counseling competitions. Students will research a problem from a range of areas of law and develop problem solving and client counseling strategies and documents and conduct mock client interviews.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyering Skills Competition
catalog.description: This course provides an overview of international commercial arbitration and focuses with more specifically on international investment protection law and bilateral investment treaty provisions. The course will provide preparation for the International LL.M. Commercial Arbitration Competition, but it is open to J.D. students.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyer Skills Competition-Negotiation Team
catalog.description: The course is limited to students who represent the law school in faculty supervised regional, national and international lawyering skills competitions, Students enrolled in this course will be representing the school in various negotiation competitions. Students will research a problem from a range of law and develop negotiation strategies and documents and conduct mock negotiations.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyer Skills Competition-Transactional Practice Teams
catalog.description: The course is limited to students who represent the law school in faculty supervised regional, national or international lawyering skills competition. Students enrolled in this course will be representing the school in various negotiation competitions and meets, Students will research a problem involving business transactions or tax and prepare analysis and problem solving strategies.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Trial Advocacy III
catalog.description: Students, under the supervision of trial advocacy faculty, participate in trial competitions. Enrollment by invitation only.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Class Actions and Multidistrict Litigation
catalog.description: An examination of class action lawsuits and their prevalence in American civil litigation; rules, requirements and limitations for class actions; special issues for party joinder and intervention, and the analysis of prerequisites for multi-district litigation (MDL), a common feature of product liability cases and mass torts.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Legal Writing: Practical Skills Development
catalog.description: Preparation of students for writing problems commonly encountered in the first two years of law practice: jury instructions, general correspondence, opinion letters, simple contracts, litigation motions and pleadings including a complaint, answer and some discovery documents. Individual feedback provided.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Legal Writing: Business Contract Drafting
catalog.description: Preparation of transactional documents including, for example, confidentiality agreements, consulting agreements, employment agreements, and technology licensing agreements.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Legal Writing: Civil Litigation Drafting
catalog.description: This course is a survey of the pretrial civil litigation process, with emphasis on practical drafting experience and the mechanics of writing. It is intended primarily for students interested in litigation, but all students can benefit from the coaching in writing skills and the feedback on their writing that the course provides. At course completion, the students should be able to draft basic litigation documents including settlement demands, initial pleadings, discovery, discovery motions, pre-trial motions, and summary judgment motions.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Advanced Legal Writing: Compliance Drafting
catalog.description: Preparation of compliance-related documents to support businesses in highly-regulated industries like health care, higher education, and business and financial institutions. Drafting a portfolio of documents—e.g., policies and procedures; codes of conduct—common to corporate compliance programs.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Applied Legal Research Administrative Regulations/Legislative History
catalog.description: The course is a mini-term designed to provide exposure to federal legislative history and administrative regulation. The course sessions will be equally divided between lecture/demonstration of sources meeting the Learning Objectives; and hands-on student work in assigned groups on a cumulative project throughout the week of the mini-term.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Master Clinical Advocacy Course
catalog.description: This semester-long intensive course will introduce students to the law, advocacy and execution of trial strategy in active litigation. The course will function as a unique clinical course, with a law school professor and local counsel serving as the supervising attorneys. The professor will select an active case in local litigation, preferably in its early stages. The students will be responsible, with supervision, for all areas of the litigation process from drafting pleadings, motions, discovery and taking and attending depositions and trial.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Lawyering Skills Teaching Assistant Methods
catalog.description: Legal analysis, research and writing; instruction and discussion of the research and writing process and related topics in legal method and legal education; supervised production of an expository writing, advocacy writing and scholarly writing; development of research and writing exercises for use in the first-year Legal Writing Program and service as Teaching Assistants in the Program; limited enrollment.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Legal Analysis & Methods
catalog.description: Preparation of students for the bar review and exam process with a focus on improving analytical skills to approach and do well on practice bar exam questions, including essay, multiple-choice, and performance questions. The course will cover specific topics tested on the bar exam with additional emphasis on refining memorization skills and learning how to self-assess understanding of concepts.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Remedies
catalog.description: Remedies for violation of legally protected interests; history and development of equity jurisdiction and modern equity practice; injunctions; declaratory judgments; rescission; reformation; restitution; contempt; damages.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Problems And Issues In The Death Penalty
catalog.description: Issues and problems in the administration of the death penalty; the Missouri capital sentencing scheme; constitutional limitations, statutory schemes, state review systems, procedural matters and collateral review of death sentences.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Death Penalty Clinic
catalog.description: The post-conviction process of collateral review in death penalty cases; training in legal representation of the postconviction petitioner.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Expungement Clinic
catalog.description: Through the Expungement Clinic, students have the opportunity to represent indigent people seeking expungement while learning critical lawyering skills. The Clinic represents people from communities that have been traditionally underserved.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be 2 or 3L, Permission of Instructor.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Introduction to Postconviction Advocacy
catalog.description:
This course is a practical skills course combining elements of Postconviction Remedies (habeas corpus, state postconviction procedural rules and statutes, extraordinary writs, parole, clemency, and other procedural paths for release from prison), Fundamentals of Investigation (document gathering, locating and interviewing witnesses, Internet investigation), and Mental Health Investigation (methods unique to biopsychosocial history investigation), and synthesizing work product into legal claims for relief and arguments for release. Prerequisites:
Completion of two semesters of Law School, including Criminal Law and Lawyering Skills.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Master Class in Postconviction Advocacy
catalog.description: Students will work in conjunction with professors and other pro bono attorneys, paralegals, social workers, and investigators to represent indigent clients in matters relating to securing release from prison through habeas corpus, parole, special statutory procedures, executive clemency, or other appropriate proceeding. The focus of the client representation will be geared towards investigation, development, and presentation of legal claims for relief or mitigating evidence to impact discretionary release decisions.
catalog.prerequisites: LAW 8713L OR any one of: LAW 8903 , LAW 8822 , or LAW 8913

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Wrongful Convictions Clinic
catalog.description: Students, under supervision, provide investigate and legal assistance to prisoners with persuasive actual innocence claims. Students meet weekly with the director of the program for training and evaluation. Assigned tasks depend on the needs of the Innocence Project, and may include interviewing potential clients, gathering records, investigating actual innocence claims, consulting with experts, drafting post-conviction and/or clemency pleadings, and appearing at court hearings. Clinical students work in conjunction with law and journalism students enrolled at the University of Missouri-Columbia. Limited enrollment (normally, 8 students).

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Gender and Justice
catalog.description: Students will examine and discuss legal issues of special importance to women. Topics will include (among others) sexual discrimination, sexual harassment, domestic violence, reproductive autonomy, and pornography. The course seeks to present each topic in its social context by supplementing legal readings with materials drawn from the social sciences, literature, and film. Paper required. Enrollment limited to fifteen students.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Adoption and Assisted Reproduction
catalog.description: This course will examine the law of adoption and how this area of law both shapes and reflects normative understandings of family and parentage. The course also addresses numerous issues with assisted reproductive technology, such as parentage, genetic engineering, and postmortem conception.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, and the Law
catalog.description: This course will examine the evolving status of sexual orientation and gender identity in the law. The course will start with a brief history of the LGBT+ rights movement, before looking at the issues that arise with relation to sexual orientation and gender identity. Subjects covered include criminal justice and the penal system, public accommodations, employment discrimination, domestic relations, treatment and care of LGBT+ youth, and the Constitution.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Cyberlaw
catalog.description: Survey of the areas of the law with existing or potential application to the internet and computers and how changes in the information environment affect law and its application. Areas of law include jurisdiction, contract law, intellectual property law, criminal law, and constitutional law.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Cybercrime
catalog.description:
Cyber threats are a global problem challenging all areas of business, and
 attorneys must be able to advise and defend clients from these threats. Criminal
 lawyers must be fluent in how new technologies work and how they impact
 investigations. In this course, students will learn how these new cyber threats
 and emerging technologies are challenging attorneys across the country. The
 course will prepare students to think as lawyers when confronting these threats.
 Course topics will include computer hacking, spamming, spear phishing, Internet
 fraud and social engineering, cyberstalking, and the rising use of computers and
 social media in violent crimes.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Secured Transactions
catalog.description: Secured Transactions in personal property under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code, function and form of a security agreement, process of perfecting a security interest, priority among unsecured parties; secured sales of goods under Article 2 of the Uniform Commercial Code.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Commercial Transactions
catalog.description: This course offers a study of the Uniform Commercial Code provisions that deal with negotiable instruments (commercial paper)(Article 3), bank collections and deposits (Article 4), funds transfers (Article 4A), and letters of credit (Article 5), as well as the study of alternate payment systems (including electronic fund transfers, credit and debit card payments, and related federal law).

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Introduction to Commercial Arbitration
catalog.description: This course is designed to give students a working familiarity with “the other forum” – the increasingly popular but often misunderstood private alternative to court litigation known as “commercial arbitration.” It will focus on the differences between arbitration and litigation, the types of evidence admitted in arbitration hearings, and how to vacate unfavorable arbitration awards.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Banking Law Seminar
catalog.description: Federal and state law governing banking activities; regulation of bank holding companies; formation of banks; the FDIC and FSLIC; interstate banking; deregulation of banking transactions; banking activities by non-banks; regulation of securities activities of banks. Paper required.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Water Law
catalog.description: Private acquisition of water rights through riparian ownership and prior appropriation; public rights to water existent in bed ownership easements and trusts; ground water management; water distribution organizations; federal allocation and control of water resources; interstate allocation.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Energy Law
catalog.description: The course will deal with the legal, economic and environmental issues of energy production on federal lands and/or under federal jurisdiction. It will focus on a number of energy sources including: oil, coal, natural gas, oil shale, coal bed methane, geothermal, water, wind, and solar. It will also cover the special problems of hydraulic fracturing, air and water pollution, climate change spills, collapses, meltdowns and other disasters as well as liability for cleanup and reclamation.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Law And The American Indian
catalog.description: An anthropological, historical and legal study of the American Indian, including a focus on American Indian traditional law and values, federal policy and current legal issues.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Preservation Law
catalog.description: An exploration of the legal and economic issues impacting preservation of land, wilderness, buildings and archeological and historical sites, including a study of various federal and state preservation legislation, and private land use preservation measures.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Cultural Preservation Law
catalog.description: This course will focus on Federal, State, and Local Law, directed at the preservation of Prehistoric, Historic, and Modern Culture. It will include sections on: The Values and Philosophy of Preservation, Archaeological Protection Law, the Native American Grave Protection and Reparation Law, Sacred Site Protection, Historic Protection in State and Local Government, the Takings Clause, Land trusts and Conservation Easements, Public-Private Partnerships and Modern Ethnic and Socio-economic Communities.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Introduction to American Law & Culture
catalog.description: Introduction to the American legal system, including government structure, sources of law, common law development, and core substantive areas. Available to LL.M. International students only.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Professional Responsibility
catalog.description: This course covers the Model Rules of Professional Conduct; role of the lawyer as a professional; confidentiality; conflict of interest; zeal within the bounds of the law; competency; providing legal services. The course explores the meaning of professional judgment and client-centered lawyering.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Professional Responsibility in Context: Environmental and Resource Law
catalog.description: Covering the law governing lawyers and professional responsibility, setting the perspective and context in the practice of environmental law and resource law. The central focus relates to understanding the role of the lawyer and professional responsibility. The experiential focus is to achieve this goal in a practice context of environment and natural resource law.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Professional Responsibility in Context: Learning from Practice
catalog.description: Covering the law governing lawyers and professional responsibility, the central focus of this course will be using the rules of professional responsibility to explore how a lawyer conceives of his or her role in the profession, in society, and for a client.
catalog.prerequisites: You must be a JD or LLM student to take this class.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Children In The Law
catalog.description: The ways in which the legal system treats children differently from adults and the justifications for such treatment, who should make decisions for the child, decisional authority that should be granted to parents, children and the state in various contexts (e.g., abuse and neglect, health care for the child, foster care, adoption and education).

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Elder Law
catalog.description: This course is an introduction to many of the legal issues that face a person who is older or has a disability. The focus is on the practical aspects of advising the person. Topics covered include ethical considerations (such as appropriately dealing with non-client family members and people who have diminishing intellectual capacity), government benefit programs (including Social Security, SSI, Medicare, and Medicaid), asset management (including conservatorship, durable powers of attorney, and trusts), guardianship and alternatives to guardianship, elder abuse and neglect, healthcare and end of life decisions, housing options, long-term care planning, long-term care insurance, estate planning, designing trusts for people who are older or have a disability, special needs trusts, and planning for people who have too many assets to qualify for means-tested public assistance but not enough to private pay for needed care.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Juvenile Offenders & The Law
catalog.description: An examination of our justice systems's historical treatment of juvenile delinquent and status offenders, and how the goals and objectives of the past have evolved into today's juvenile offender laws; the rights of juvenile offenders in contrast to those of adult criminals; pre-trial and trial procedural issues under the juvenile code; certification of the juvenile offender as an adult; dispositional/treatment alternatives for juvenile offenders; schools and the juvenile offender.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Mediation
catalog.description: The process in which a neutral third party assists others in resolving a dispute or planning a transaction; introduction to the nature of the process, its possibilities and limitations, its current and future uses, and how lawyers can and should be involved in it; public policy and political issues surrounding the mediation movement; professional responsibility and malpractice.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Seminar In Famous Trials
catalog.description: Historical and jurisprudential issues involved in a number of 'political trials.'

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Law Of The European Union (Part I)
catalog.description: An in-depth study of the legal and political framework and institutions of the European Union; the Commission, Council of Ministers, Court of Justice, Court of Auditors, and the European Parliament. Course will examine the interlocking web of European treaties, the expansion of the European Union, the European Union as a trade block and Ireland as a gateway to the European Union for non-bloc nations.

catalog.subject: LAW
catalog.title: Debtor-Creditor Rights
catalog.description: Creditors' remedies and debtors' rights; provisional remedies; secured transactions (Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code); liens and exemptions; overview of bankruptcy law.

catalog.subject: LAW
