Compassion will be considered as central ethical value. Theravada, Mahayana, and Tibetan Buddhism will all be considered.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Feminist Philosophy
catalog.description: This course examines how feminist thinkers have engaged with some of the major fields of philosophy, including ethics, epistemology, metaphysics, philosophy of science, and social and political philosophy. Topics include sex and gender, embodiment, reason and emotion, reproduction, motherhood, free speech, autonomy, scientific bias, and epistemic privilege.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Philosophy of Love
catalog.description: This course addresses philosophical questions about love, relationships, and sex. Topics include different forms of love, so-called “true” love, polyamory, sexual attraction, flirting, cheating, and consent.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Environmental Ethics And Policy
catalog.description: Various philosophical approaches to issues such as the value of nature, human obligations to non-human animals, species, ecosystems and future generations; environmental justice; restoration; resource use; environmental politics; and the relation between environmental issues, policy and ethics will be discussed critically.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Plato
catalog.description: Selected dialogues of Plato are studied with a view to understanding Plato's philosophy and its position in the world of Greece and antiquity. Plato's philosophy is also examined with reference to his place in the Western tradition and in modern philosophy.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Aristotle
catalog.description: Selected portions of Aristotle's works on logic, metaphysics, science, ethics, politics, and poetics are studied with a view to understanding Aristotle's philosophy and its position in the world of Greece and antiquity. Aristotle's philosophy is examined with reference to its place in the Western tradition and in modern philosophy. Recommended preparation: PHILOS 210 or PHILOS 222 .

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Professional Ethics
catalog.description: An analysis and investigation of modern and contemporary ethical theories as they can be applied to professional life. Among the theories considered are ethical relativity, the emotive theory, utilitarianism, Kantianism, and virtue ethics, all within the context of real-life decision-making for professionals such as nurses and doctors, business people, lawyers, engineers, educators and others.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Ethics and Government
catalog.description: This course covers the historical and current role of ethics in the executive, legislative, and judicial branches, including examining the ethical standards of elected officials and appointed public servants.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Bioethics
catalog.description: This course will provide an overview of the history of bioethics from antiquity to the present. The course will provide an overview of foundational ethical theories. The course will explore key events in bioethics and the responses to them in the bioethics literature.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Reproductive Ethics
catalog.description: This course tackles some of the most controversial ethical debates surrounding human reproduction. Topics include contraception, abortion, assisted reproductive technologies, surrogacy, gamete donation, embryonic selection, and genetic enhancement. Students will have the rare opportunity to think critically about the difficult beginning-of-life choices that face parents, healthcare providers, researchers, and society at large.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: The Philosophy of Martin Luther King, Jr.
catalog.description: This is a seminar-style course that will study Martin Luther King, Jr. as a Social-Political Philosopher. As such, students will be critically discussing the philosophical themes in King’s writings with an aim to understand his philosophical outlook, consider the merits or demerits of his philosophical outlook, and apply his philosophical outlook to contemporary social-political issues in America.
catalog.prerequisites: A minimum of 3 credit hours of PHILOS coursework.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Selected Topics
catalog.description: Each time this course is offered a particular philosopher or particular area of philosophy will be the topic of discussion. The course may be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Special Topics And Readings
catalog.description: Intensive reading and/or research in an area selected by the student in consultation with the instructor. May be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Special Topics And Readings
catalog.description: Intensive reading and/or research in an area selected by the student in consultation with the instructor. By permission only. May be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Special Topics and Readings
catalog.description: Intensive reading and/or research in an area selected by the student in consultation with the instructor. By permission only. May be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Managerial And Administrative Decision Making And Ethical Values
catalog.description: Methods of problem definition and decision making in ethics are presented with the goal of providing the student with a matrix for case review. A series of cases is offered that serve to integrate approaches to ethical reflection with management and administrative decision making. Cases are chosen on the basis of topical, curricular and conceptual relevance.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Seminar On Philosophy And Law
catalog.description: An examination from a philosophical perspective of the historical and conceptual relationships present in the evolution, development and analysis of law. Among the systems of analysis examined will be natural law theory, legal positivism and legal realism. Ordinarily the seminar will focus on a specific area of controversy in the law.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Ethics And Government
catalog.description: An examination of ethical issues related to government, with the primary focus on national and local governmental bodies in the United States. Ethics in the executive, legislative and judicial branches are examined. Ethical standards for elected officials and appointed public servants are reviewed. Attempts to "legislate morality" are considered. The course includes a historical review of ethics and government and an analysis of the legal implications of legislation regarding ethics in the executive branch.

catalog.subject: PHILOS
catalog.title: Research In Selected Fields: Graduate Studies
catalog.description: Intensive research in an area selected by the student in consultation with the instructor. By permission only. May be repeated for credit when the topic varies.

catalog.subject: PHY-SCI
catalog.title: Foundations Of Physical Sciences I
catalog.description: Fundamental principles and concepts of the various physical and mathematical sciences, integrated by the history and philosophy of science.

catalog.subject: PHY-SCI
catalog.title: Foundations Of Physical Sciences, Laboratory I
catalog.description: General laboratory and discussion sessions on various topics in the physical and mathematical sciences.

catalog.subject: PHY-SCI
catalog.title: Physics For Future Presidents
catalog.description: A course intended for liberal arts students focusing on the physics they need to be informed citizens in a democracy. Energy, global warming, terrorism, and health are examples of the important topics examined from the perspective of how science should inform policy.

catalog.subject: PHY-SCI
catalog.title: Selected Topics In The History Of Science
catalog.description: Selected Topics In The History Of Science

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Badminton
catalog.description: This course teaches the basic rules, skill techniques, terminology and strategy for badminton.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Weight Training
catalog.description: Weight Training helps students build a solid foundation of current weight training knowledge and practice that can be used throughout their lifetime. Information in the course is consistent with recommendations of the National Strength and Conditioning Association (NSCA) and the American College of Sport Medicine (ACSM). Based on individual goals and assessments, beginning weight training students will create a personal training program and implement a record keeping system to keep track of their progress.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Advanced Weight Training
catalog.description: This course teaches free weight training exercises that are used within a well-balanced training program, and provides experience needed to design weight training programs.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Personal Fitness
catalog.description: This course is designed to expose students to facts about and experiences in dealing with motor, physical, physiological, psychological and nutritional aspects of the human being. Specific areas of study include hypokinetic disease, physical fitness, nutrition and wellness concepts.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Special Topics: Activity
catalog.description: A course designed to deal with a special activity class which is not available in the regular course offerings. Activity class, instructors and prerequisites to be listed in the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Special Topics: Activity
catalog.description: Special topics in physical education.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: First Aid And Safety
catalog.description: Methods of administering first aid in case of accident or sudden illness; bandaging; resuscitation; and caring for wounds and injuries. Safety in schools will be stressed. (Elective).

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Outdoor And Leisure Pursuits
catalog.description: Designed to acquaint students with opportunities for leisure and recreational activity in the outdoors. Emphasizes safety measures and planning skills as well as development of particular movement skills and knowledge about associated wildlife.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Self Defense
catalog.description: Study in the theory of self defense. Content focuses on: technique for eliminating dangers from daily living, methods for recognizing and avoiding dangers, and skills and strategies for employing physical defense when necessary.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Mechanical Analysis of Human Movement
catalog.description: Study of the kinesiologic and biomechanical aspects of human motion with focus on application to sport skill, dance and exercise situations.
catalog.prerequisites: HLSC 120 and HLSC 160 or concurrent enrollment.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Nutrition for Fitness and Sport
catalog.description: This course examines the role nutrition, complemented by exercise, may play in the enhancement of fitness and sport performance. Considerable attention will be devoted to the use of nutritional ergogenic aids with reference to athletic performance.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Physiology of Sport and Exercise
catalog.description: Study of the concepts and principles of exercise physiology with the intent of learning how to apply them to exercise, sport and movement experiences. Includes development of fitness testing skills, program planning and exercise.
catalog.prerequisites: HLSC 120 and HLSC 160 or concurrent enrollment.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Psychology of Sport and Exercise
catalog.description: Exploration of psychological constructs related to the competitive sport process and to physical activity.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Special Topics In Health And Physical Education
catalog.description: This course is designed to offer a topic which is not available in the regular course offerings. Topics, instructors and prerequisites to be listed in the semester bulletin.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription
catalog.description: This course introduces students to health appraisal and fitness assessment of individuals. The course proceeds with prescribing exercise and conditioning programs, to enhance health and develop physical performance.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Teaching Healthy Behaviors in the Schools
catalog.description: Study of school health and physical activity programs with emphasis on methods and materials for health, safety, and classroom physical activity instruction in grades K-8.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Internship
catalog.description: Extensive experience in a practical situation under supervision of university faculty and on-site personnel. Breadth and intensity of involvement will depend on student ability. Available only to upper-division majors.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Organization And Administration Of Athletics
catalog.description: Organization and management of a program of competitive athletics for schools and colleges.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Social-Cultural Aspects of Sport and Physical Activity
catalog.description: The social significance of sport in modern societies. Research on the social structure, social relations and social problems of sport from several subcultural perspectives will be reviewed.

catalog.subject: PHYS-ED
catalog.title: Sport Psychology
catalog.description: Analysis of research and theory focused on the psychological aspects associated with participation in sport and physical activity.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics of Sports
catalog.description: A course intended for liberal arts students focusing on the physics involved in different sports. Physical laws and technological developments that impact sports will be studied.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Backyard Physics
catalog.description: This laboratory course uses readily available ingredients to develop a conceptual understanding of the laws of nature and mathematics. Experiments can be conducted in the residence hall, apartment, park or home using everyday, inexpensive equipment and materials.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: How Things Work
catalog.description: A course intended for liberal arts students focusing on the principles of operations, histories, and relationships of objects from our daily environment. The areas of investigation include mechanical and thermal objects, electromagnetism, light, special materials and nuclear energy.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: How Things Work Laboratory
catalog.description: A course intended for liberal arts students focusing on the principles of operations, histories and relationships of objects from our daily environment. The areas of investigation include mechanical and thermal objects, electromagnetism, light, special materials and nuclear energy.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: General Physics I
catalog.description: Introduction to mechanics, wave motion and sound and heat and thermodynamics. Three hours lecture and two hours laboratory per week.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: General Physics II
catalog.description: Introduction to electricity and magnetism, light and optics and modern physics. Three hours lecture and two hours laboratory per week.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics For Scientists and Engineers I
catalog.description: Introduction to mechanics, wave motion and sound and heat and thermodynamics.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics For Scientists and Engineers II
catalog.description: Introduction to electricity and magnetism, light and optics and modern physics. Four hours lecture and two hours laboratory per week.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Scientific Research Preparation
catalog.description: Through completion of immersive and structured hands-on learning activities, students gain generalized practical and technical skills that are in demand for STEM (Science-Technology-Engineering-Math) internships and that are needed for dynamic careers in scientific, engineering, and Tech research and development sectors. Students learn transferable data analysis, critical thinking, problem-solving, coding, technical communication, and technological literacy skills through the realistic application of concepts, tools, and methods commonly employed in basic research. No previous experience with computer coding nor research methods is required.
catalog.prerequisites: Physics 210 or 240, or consent of instructor

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Mechanics I
catalog.description: Advanced statics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies including gravitation.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 ; and MATH 250 or MATH 268 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Mechanics II
catalog.description: Continuation of Mechanics I, including mechanics of continuous media, Lagranges equations, tensor algebra and theory of small vibrations.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Methods Of Theoretical Physics I
catalog.description: Introduction to mathematical and numerical methods used in the theoretical modeling of physical systems. Treatments of linear systems in scientific and engineering applications will be emphasized.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics of Science Fiction
catalog.description: This course will quantitatively explore the representation of physics in science fiction books, movies and television shows. Many popular science fiction concepts will be explored, spanning centuries of physics from Galileo to string theory.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 ; and MATH 120 or MATH 125 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Modern Physics With Engineering Applications
catalog.description: An introduction to the theories that revolutionized science and technology in the twentieth century. Topics include special and general relativity, introductory quantum mechanics and atomic structure. Inventions and applications based on these are also examined.
catalog.prerequisites: MATH 220 or MATH 268 and PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Practical Astronomy
catalog.description: A practical overview of the basic methods of observational astronomy research, including the principles of telescopes, detectors and measurement theory.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Stellar Astrophysics
catalog.description: A mathematical and conceptual overview of the observed properties of stars and the fundamental astrophysics of radiative transfer, hydrostatic equilibrium, atomic processes and thermonuclear energy production that govern their structure, atmospheres and remnants.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Galaxies
catalog.description: A mathematical and conceptual overview of the observed properties and astrophysics of galaxies highlighting star formation and evolution, the interstellar medium, the Milky Way, galaxy populations and demographics, active galactic nuclei, and galaxy formation and evolution.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics of Electronics
catalog.description: An introduction to the solid state physics of basic electronic components and their operation through both theory and practical labwork.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Computer Interfacing Laboratory
catalog.description: An introduction to data acquisition and automation by computer interfacing transduction and control equipment through the serial and parallel buses. The course is multidisciplinary, balancing the physics of transduction to the computer science of automation programming to the electrical engineering of bus protocols. Both high- and low-level programming are taught within the context of automating an experimental procedure. Digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital conversion is also covered.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Thermal Physics
catalog.description: A study of the laws of thermodynamics and their applications, with an introduction to kinetic theory. Statistical methods are emphasized.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 ; and MATH 250 or MATH 268 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Optics
catalog.description: Geometrical optics, physical optics and introduction to selected topics in modern optics.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 and MATH 210 or MATH 266 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Particle Physics
catalog.description: Essential aspects of modern physics are examined in a historical context, and also in terms of the standard model describing concisely the fundamental interactions among particles. Conservation laws are discussed, and recent developments such as String Theory are considered. Physics 437 is also offered as Physics 5537.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Introduction To Solid State Physics
catalog.description: Crystal structure and binding, elementary lattice dynamics and energy band theory. Free electron models, theory of semiconductors and metals.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Electricity And Magnetism I
catalog.description: Static electric fields in free space and material media; Kirchoff's laws and direct current circuits; static magnetic fields.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 ; and MATH 250 or MATH 268 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Electricity And Magnetism II
catalog.description: Magnetostatics; alternating current circuits; Maxwell's equations and radiation; special relativity; topics in electromagnetism.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Cosmology
catalog.description: This course provides a foundation in both physical and observational cosmology. Students will acquire both a mathematical and conceptual understanding of the formation and dynamics of the Universe.
catalog.prerequisites: PHYSICS 220 or PHYSICS 250 , and MATH 250 or MATH 268 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Introduction To Quantum Mechanics
catalog.description: Introduction to the theory and applications of quantum mechanics with emphasis on the mathematical treatment of modern physics.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Advanced Laboratory
catalog.description: This course offers a selection of important experiments in physics, performed with modern instrumentation. It is designed to give students a deeper understanding of physics and help them develop experimental abilities and improve their communication skills.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Special Problems
catalog.description: The kind of problem and the amount of credit to be given by arrangement with the department.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Undergraduate Research
catalog.description: Independent student research on a physics/astrophysics project under the supervision of a faculty member. Projects will engage students in aspects of the scientific process including data collection and analysis, research methods and strategies, scientific discussion and written/oral communication. Requires a minimum of 3-4 hours of research per week for each credit hour.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Methods Of Mathematical Physics I
catalog.description: Intended to provide the student with the advanced mathematical techniques needed for beginning graduate studies in the physical sciences. Content includes real variables, infinite series, complex analysis, linear algebra and partial differential equations.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Methods Of Mathematical Physics II
catalog.description: A continuation of Physics 500 which includes Sturm-Liouville operators, special functions, Fourier transforms, distributions and Green functions, Laplace transforms, linear groups and tensor analysis.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Survey Of Recent Development In Physics
catalog.description: Specifically designed to help high school and junior college science teachers keep pace with current developments in various subdivisions of physics and their impact on society and technology. (Not applicable for graduate degree in Physics).
catalog.prerequisites: Prerequisite: Baccalaureate degree and one year science teaching experience.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Theoretical Mechanics I
catalog.description: A review of undergraduate mechanics precedes the study of generalized classical mechanics in this course. Topics include variational principles, Lagrangian and Hamilton methods, conservation laws and Hamilton-Jacobi theory.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Theoretical Mechanics II
catalog.description: A continuation of PHYSICS 5510 , this course covers topics such as normal coordinates, small oscillations, continuum mechanics and special/general relativity.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Electromagnetic Theory And Applications I
catalog.description: Electrostatics, magnetostatics and various approaches in solving boundary value problems of electromagnetism, Green's functions, conformal transformations and polynomial expansions, Maxwell's equations and waves.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Electromagnetic Theory And Applications II
catalog.description: Waveguides, fiberoptics, radiation systems and antenna for wireless communications, scattering and diffraction of electromagnetic waves, multipole fields, special relativity and relativistic particle dynamics and radiation.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Quantum Mechanics I
catalog.description: Review of elementary methods, formal preliminaries, axioms, commuting operators, angular momentum, static perturbation theory, Wigner-Eckart theorem.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Quantum Mechanics II
catalog.description: Time dependent perturbation theory, scattering, applications to atoms, molecules and nuclei, reactions, relativistic methods.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Optical Properties Of Matter
catalog.description: Maxwell's equations and the dielectric function, absorption and dispersion, free-electron metals, interband transitions, dispersion relations and sum rules, self-consistent field approximation, current-current correlations and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, plasmons and characteristic energy loss.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Particle Physics
catalog.description: Essential aspects of modern particle physics are examined in a historical context, and also in terms of the standard model describing concisely the fundamental interactions among particles. Conservation laws are discuses, and recent developments such as String Theory are considered.
catalog.prerequisites: (for undergraduates) PHYSICS 240 , PHYSICS 250 , and PHYSICS 350 or PHYSICS 472 .

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Statistical Physics I
catalog.description: Statistical mechanics as a basis for thermodynamics; classical distribution functions; quantum statistical mechanics, kinetic theory, transport phenomena; application to systems of interacting particles.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Statistical Physics II
catalog.description: Special topics in advanced statistical physics including: second quantization, modern many body theory, interacting Fermi and Bose systems, superfluidity and superconductivity, renormalization group and computer simulation techniques.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Atomic And Molecular Structure
catalog.description: Experimental results and theoretical models by quantum mechanics. Special emphasis on the interaction between radiation and matter.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Practical Astronomy
catalog.description: A practical overview of the basic methods of observational astronomy research, including the principles of telescopes, detectors and measurement theory, as well as hands-on experience with data reduction and analysis. This course is open to graduate students from all majors.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Stellar Astrophysics
catalog.description: A mathematical and conceptual overview of the observed properties of stars and the fundamental astrophysics of radiative transfer, hydrostatic equilibrium, atomic processes and thermonuclear energy production that govern their structure, atmospheres and remnants.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Galaxies
catalog.description: A mathematical and conceptual overview of the observed properties and astrophysics of galaxies highlighting star formation and evolution, the interstellar medium, the Milky Way, galaxy populations and demographics, active galactic nuclei, and galaxy formation and evolution.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Nuclear Physics
catalog.description: Fundamental properties of the atomic nucleus discussed in terms of experimental results and theoretical models. Quantum and statistical mechanics are used where appropriate.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Cosmology
catalog.description: This course provides a foundation in both physical and observational cosmology. Students will acquire both a mathematical and conceptual understanding of the formation and dynamics of the Universe.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Quantum Theory Of Solids I
catalog.description: Lattice dynamics and thermal conductivity. Neutron scattering. Symmetry principles in crystals and consequences. Point group, space group and irreducible representations. Energy band theory and methods of band calculation. Elementary Theory of Magnetism. Spin wave theory.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Quantum Theory Of Solids II
catalog.description: Topics will include crystal imperfections, impurities and defects, optical properties of metals and semiconductors, electron-lattice interaction and transport theory, superconductivity and theory of disordered systems.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics Seminar
catalog.description: Contemporary publications and research.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Physics of Electronics
catalog.description: An introduction to the solid state physics of basic electronic components and their operation through both theory and practical lab work.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Topics In Physics
catalog.description: Contemporary publications and research.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Topics In Physics
catalog.description: Contemporary publications and research.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Topics in Physics
catalog.description: Contemporary publications and research.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Computer Interfacing Laboratory
catalog.description: An introduction to computer interfacing through the use of serial and parallel ports and digital-to-analog and analog-to-digital converters. The course also introduces digital filtering techniques, data analysis techniques, and graphical presentation of data. The programming techniques are taught using high level programming languages currently used in research and development labs.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Research And Thesis
catalog.description: Research for thesis in partial fulfillment of the master's degree in physics.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Research Seminar
catalog.description: Seminars on current research topics of research programs in the department and those of external distinguished scientists. (Must be taken by Physics Ph.D. students).

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Special Research Topics
catalog.description: A lecture course presenting advanced research-level topics.
catalog.prerequisites: Ph.D. candidacy. This course is intended to allow faculty and visiting scholars to offer special courses in selected research areas.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Dissertation Research
catalog.description: This course is individually directed research leading to the fulfillment of the Comprehensive Exam requirements of the Department of Physics and Astronomy. These include (i) completion of an NSF-style research proposal and (ii) successful oral defense of it before the student’s research advisory committee.
catalog.prerequisites: Completion of at least 80% of coursework hours, as per the student’s Plan of Study and Permission of the instructor.

catalog.subject: PHYSICS
catalog.title: Research And Dissertation
catalog.description: Research for dissertation in partial fulfillment of the Ph.D. degree requirements in physics.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Preparatory Applied Study
catalog.description: One-hour weekly lesson. Limited to two semesters study. Jury examination is required. There shall be a jury which shall be for comments only unless the student is applying for entrance to the 101 level, at which time a graded jury is required. May not be taken for credit toward the major.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Applied Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: Applied study of a second instrument. One half-hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study. No jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Applied Study for the Non-Music Major
catalog.description: Applied study for the non-music major. One half-hour lesson weekly. No jury required.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be a student in the UMKC Conservatory.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Studio Class
catalog.description: Experiential lab where students gain orientation and experience with pedagogy, literature, and performance.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Special Applied Studies
catalog.description: One-hour lesson weekly. This course is for pedagogical or review purposes. An audition is required, and a jury for comments only may be held at the discretion of the division. May be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Applied Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: One half-hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study. No jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Graduate Applied Jazz Studies
catalog.description: One-hour lesson weekly. Jury examination is required.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Special Applied Jazz Studies
catalog.description: One-hour lesson weekly. This course is for pedagogical or review purposes. A jury for comments only may be held at the discretion of the faculty.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Applied Jazz Study of a Second Instrument
catalog.description: One half-hour lesson weekly. Applied study for those students who wish to pursue applied jazz study in an area other than, and in addition to, their primary performance study.

catalog.subject: PIANO
catalog.title: Graduate Collaborative Piano
catalog.description: Studio lessons for pianists in collaborative piano repertoire at the graduate level. Permission of instructor required.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: American Government
catalog.description: American government and politics, with special reference to the U.S. Constitution. This course meets the state requirement for study of the U.S. and Missouri Constitutions.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Introduction To Comparative Politics
catalog.description: Introduces students to general concepts of political authority and systematically analyzes the causes and consequences of variation in political institutions, processes and policies across countries, illustrating concepts and themes with case studies of major European and Asian countries.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics and Research
catalog.description: This course introduces students to general concepts of political authority, and systematically analyzes the causes and consequences of variation in political institutions, processes and policies across countries. This course also introduces students to research in comparative politics, with students developing an independent research project.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: International Relations
catalog.description: An analysis of relations among nations, with emphasis on structures of international power, causes of war, and approaches to peace.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Law and Politics
catalog.description: What are the political origins of legal systems? Why are there lawyers? Why does the legal system matter for contemporary American society? This class provides an introduction to the relationship between law and politics, and is designed in particular to help pre-law students form a more thorough understanding of the role and identity of lawyers and the functioning of the legal system.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Western Political Philosophy
catalog.description: An examination of the major theories of politics from Plato to today.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Political Behavior
catalog.description: This course will survey research on conventional and unconventional forms of mass political behavior. Topics to be discussed include campaign participation, voting behavior, public opinion, the media, and participation in protests and revolutions. This course will also cover the methodological approaches to the study of political behavior.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Politics of Developing Countries
catalog.description: The course examines the key arguments that have been advanced to account for differences across countries in rates and levels of economic and political development.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Parties and Interest Groups
catalog.description: Introduction to parties and interest groups in the United States and their important role in the political process. Topics include the formation, organization, activities, and impact of political parties and interest groups in American politics.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Public Opinion
catalog.description: Explores public opinion in the United States, surveying theories and empirical research on the measurement, formation, and distribution of public opinion.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Politics In The American States
catalog.description: A study of the structures, functions, and politics of the institutions of American state governments and an assessment of their role in the federal system. This course is particularly interested in the extent to which political economy and political culture, broadly defined, influence public policy within the states.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Politics of Kansas City Metro
catalog.description: This course will provide an understanding of city politics in America through a study of metropolitan Kansas City. It will discuss federalism, relationships between local governments, government organization, forming political alliances, and political issues affecting the metropolitan area. The course will discuss the politics of issues such as fiscal policy, infrastructure, housing, service delivery, and the environment.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Terrorism And Political Violence
catalog.description: This course explores terrorism and armed struggle from theoretical and historical perspectives, and analyzes a number of violent movements with nationalist, ideological, and religious motivations.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Political Psychology
catalog.description: The field of political psychology is an interdisciplinary field that draws on both psychology and political science to address topics in the political world. This course will focus on a variety of topics including inter-group conflict, stereotyping and prejudice, political socialization, attitude formation and change, political communication, decision heuristics and biases, public opinion, and the future of political psychology.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Campaigns And Elections
catalog.description: This course will examine the role of campaigns in determining the outcome of both congressional and presidential elections and the way that electoral rules structure both campaign strategies and electoral outcomes.This course focuses on topics such as the role of the media, campaign advertising, campaign financing, public opinion, registration requirements, and the role of interest groups.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Racial and Ethnic Politics
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the state of the discipline on the political behavior of racial-ethnic minority groups in the United States. This course analyzes the historical and political experiences of the major racial and ethnic minority groups in the United States, and their paths to political incorporation. We will examine the relationships between group consciousness, community, membership, marginalization, incorporation into the polity, civic engagement, political participation, and mobilization.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Foreign Policy
catalog.description: This course is designed to bridge the gap between academic learning and the practical skills required to succeed in international affairs and foreign policy. Using contemporary issues like climate change, current armed conflicts, food insecurity, migration, extreme poverty, geopolitical competition, and U.S. foreign policy development, students will gain hands-on experience through assignments that mirror real-world tasks. By the end of the course, students will be able to operate confidently and professionally in international relations and foreign policy, applying both theoretical knowledge and practical skills to drive real-world impact.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Religion And Politics
catalog.description: Despite predictions that modernization would diminish the influence of religion, it continues to play a significant role in contemporary political life. This course aims to deepen the students’ understanding and appreciation of the impact religion has on politics and vice versa. While the intersection of religion and politics raises profound philosophical questions, the primary focus of this course is on examining how religion influences political processes directly through tools like voter engagement and indirectly through providing civic infrastructure for participants to be better prepared for such engagement and how political dynamics, in turn, affect religious practice.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Women and Politics
catalog.description: This course investigates the role that women play in the political realm and how political institutions, laws, and norms shape women’s experience in politics as citizens, activists, candidates and political leaders, plus the causes and consequences of women’s participation and barriers to same.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Constitutional Law: The Federal System
catalog.description: A study of the president, congress and state governments from the perspective of the Constitution, emphasizing powers and limitations on the exercise of authority.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Constitutional Law: Civil Liberties
catalog.description: A study of civil liberties in American society, emphasizing factors and forces that restrict or enlarge their scope, as understood through constitutional interpretation.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Politics In Eastern And Central Europe
catalog.description: An analysis of the internal politics and foreign policies of the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Poland, and selected other countries in East-Central Europe, emphasizing the transition to post-Communist rule and new and enduring patterns of political culture.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Western European Politics
catalog.description: This course explores democratic representation and political institutions in Western Europe.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Labor, Politics and Society
catalog.description: This course explores many aspects of unions and the labor movement in society and the vital role organized labor plays as a pillar of democratic society. Unions impact the economy, growth, and the distribution of wealth, and the impact racial and gender equality, social security health and job safety, energy and the environment, and even foreign relations. As a social movement, labor has had a major impact on American history. This course covers these topics from a labor perspective. It examines current obstacles for union organizing, recent union campaigns, labor's political role, and the relationship between labor and the media, This course is part of the Certificate Program in Labor Studies and is offered on the University of Missouri Interactive Video Network at UMKC, UMSL, and UMC.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Latin America and International Relations
catalog.description: This course we will survey the relations between Latin American states and between Latin America and the world. Taking the Latin American states as the key actors, we examine the history of US-Latin American relations, including current issues such as drug trafficking, immigration and terrorism. We will also study the region as a player on the international stage, examining Latin America's changing role in the world arena related to trade, development, and the environment. Finally we examine the emergence of new leadership in Latin America.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Immigration Politics and Policy: The United States in Cross-National Perspective
catalog.description: This course introduces issues of immigration in the industrialized world, including historical patterns, current features of immigration in the US and Europe, policies on legal and unauthorized migration, attitudes on assimilation of immigrants and what constitutes an effective immigration policy.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Congress and Parliaments
catalog.description: The objective of this course is to compare the American Congress to parliaments and legislatures in other countries. The course will examine how elections and institutions affect the behavior of legislators and the policy-making process in many countries.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: British Politics
catalog.description: This course focuses on the contemporary politics of the United Kingdom, particularly elections, institutions, and political parties.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: International Political Economy
catalog.description: This course examines major schools of thought and contemporary research in international political economy, as well as the study of the interactions of politics with economics, governments, and markets.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Threats to Human Security
catalog.description: Students will consider how factors such as climate change, poverty, and regime repression impact the security of individuals and how those effects are compounded by race, gender, caste, socio-economic status. Students will also examine how human security impacts state security.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Labor Law
catalog.description: In this course, participants will examine the role of government in the regulation of labor-management relations in the United States. While the focus of the course will be on federal laws regulating private sector labor relations, parallel issues addressed in the Railway Labor Act and state public sector labor relations law will also be covered. Specific topics include the legal framework for the organization of workers, definition of prohibited or unfair labor practices of employers and unions, legal regulation of the collective bargaining process, regulation of the use of economic weapons in labor disputes, enforcement of collective bargaining agreements and the regulation of internal trade union activities.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Women and Conflict
catalog.description: Students will explore the roles of women in armed political conflict; specifically the ways that women influence and participate in conflict and peace processes as well as the ways women are affected by conflict and peace processes.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Political Institutions
catalog.description: Political institutions are all around us, shaping our political, economic, and social lives. What are political institutions? Where do they come from? Why do they matter? This class focuses on these questions.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Pre-Law I: The Role and Identity of a Lawyer
catalog.description: This course addresses the question 'Is law the right career for me?' We will discuss the role of law and courts in organizing American society. We will hear from guests at every step of professional development including law students, early-career, and advanced-career lawyers. Upon completing this course, students should have a stronger sense of the role the law has in organizing American society, and different career paths in the law.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Pre-Law II: Foundations of an Effective Lawyer
catalog.description: This course prepares students to answer the question: “How does my undergraduate education prepare me for success in law school and beyond?”. An enriching undergraduate education is an important foundation for a successful and effective lawyer. This course views the students’ legal training as beginning in their undergraduate education, and preparing them for post-graduate success. The course is structured around characteristics of effective law students and lawyers, and opportunities for pre-law students’ to develop those traits.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Logical Reasoning for Pre-Law Students
catalog.description: This course is designed to help you to prepare to be successful in being admitted to the law school of your choice. The course will focus primarily on introducing you to the skills and habits of preparation necessary to perform your best on the Law School Admission Test (LSAT). The three primary skills we will focus on will be analytical reasoning, logical reasoning, and reading comprehension, with a fourth implicit skill: standardized test taking.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Political Science And Politics
catalog.description: Offered as a special course in the individual faculty member's area of research specialization. The course may be repeated for credit when the topic varies. The topic and instructor will be announced in advance.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Legitimacy, Power, and the Survival of Political Systems
catalog.description: This course examines what allows political systems to survive, exert power, and maintain control over their population. It focuses on the concept of legitimacy – i.e. whether people believe a government has the right to make decisions that are binding on the mass public. The course covers how political systems and institutions develop legitimacy, how that legitimacy helps maintain control of the mass public, and why people sometimes choose to willingly follow commands issued by political authorities and other times choose to resist or rebel.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Conflict Resolution
catalog.description: This course examines theories of peace and conflict resolution in the international system. Students will assess the challenges to conflict resolution, international cooperation, and peace as well as the means through which states and non-state actors overcome those challenges. Students will critically evaluate theories of conflict resolution and peace, while learning to apply those theories to current events.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Judicial Politics
catalog.description: An examination of the judiciary in the American political process, emphasizing the role of judges, lawyers and the Supreme Court.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Seminar in Comparative Politics
catalog.description: A survey of the major research in comparative politics including state building, democracy, economic development, and political violence.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Seminar: Authoritarian Regimes
catalog.description: This course investigates the structure and functioning of authoritarian political systems in comparison to democratic regimes. We examine how repressive leaders gain and maintain power, what factors condition constituents’ choices to support or oppose an authoritarian government, and differences in the ordinary conduct of political and economic life for individuals in comparison to democratic systems.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Civil-Military Relations
catalog.description: A study of the various types of civil-military relationships and the conditions under which they emerge.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Environmental Politics
catalog.description: This course investigates how environmental issues shape and are shaped by politics, including issues of public opinion, party competition, and political and economic institutions. Examining environmental politics from a local, national, cross-national, and international lens, this course will investigate the challenges and potential policy and political solutions to this vital global issue.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Administering American Elections
catalog.description: This is a research-based class which examines the administration of American elections. The federal nature of American elections means that there are a variety of election practices across the US. In this course, students compare the different ways in which state and local election officials conduct elections, and evaluate the performances of different voting systems.
catalog.prerequisites: Pol-Sci 210 or equivalent or permission of instructor

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Concepts in International Relations
catalog.description: This course exposes advanced undergraduate students to major conceptual and theoretical approaches to international relations. Recommended preparation: Prior course in international relations, politics, economics, or history.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Government And Politics
catalog.description: This variable credit course will explore different contemporary issues and problems related to government and politics. Credit may apply to the major but will not satisfy any of the four subfields distribution requirements.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Internship
catalog.description: With the written consent of the department chairman, students may participate in structured internship programs approved by the department for a maximum of six hours.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Study Abroad
catalog.description: With prior approval from the department advisor, students may complete coursework at an approved foreign university and receive up to 6 hours of political science credit.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Political Science Tutorial
catalog.description: Senior political science majors may apply to do independent study under a selected professor. Only one tutorial will count toward the major.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Honors Tutorial
catalog.description: Senior political science majors with a grade point average of 3.4 or above in political science may apply to do independent study under a selected professor. Must have written consent of professor prior to registration. Only one tutorial will count toward the major.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Seminar in Comparative Politics
catalog.description: A survey of the major research in comparative politics including state building, democracy, economic development, and political violence.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Government And Politics Seminar
catalog.description: Offered as a special seminar in the individual faculty member's area of research specialization. The seminar may be repeated for credit when the topic varies. The topic and instructor will be announced in advance.

catalog.subject: POL-SCI
catalog.title: Research And Dissertation
catalog.description: Directed specialized research.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: General Psychology
catalog.description: A survey of the fundamental principles, theories, and methods of psychological science.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Social Psychology
catalog.description: Survey of behavior in the actual, imagined, and implied presence of others, including attitudes, the self, conformity, altruism, aggression, prejudice, and group processes.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Academic and Career Opportunities in Psychology
catalog.description: An introduction to the applied fields of Psychology. Students will explore post-BA career options and engage with professionals who will share their career paths, their academic interests, and challenges of their current positions. Emphasis will be placed on students developing academic plans that will prepare them for professional success.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with C- or better. Must be Psychology BA major and have completed a minimum of 15 credit hours.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Child Psychology
catalog.description: Survey of child development from conception to adolescence, including major theories, developmental milestones and research related to the physical, cognitive, social and emotional growth of children.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Health Psychology
catalog.description: An overview of the scientific study of the attitudes, behaviors, and personality variables related to health and illness. Emphasis is placed on the interaction of biological, psychological, social, and cultural factors that relate to illness and disease, and their influence on treatment and prevention.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Adolescent Psychology
catalog.description: This course discusses development through the adolescent and early adult years. Topics covered include cognitive development, identity formation, sexuality, family and peer relationships, academic achievement, and cultural and media influences. Adolescent development will be discussed as a distinct stage of life, and as an integral component of development across the lifespan.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Research Design in Psychological Science
catalog.description: An overview of research designs and data collection methods used in psychological science. Emphasis is placed on comparing strengths and limitations of various research designs and data collection methods as well as identifying appropriate uses of those research designs and data collection methods.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Psychology of Gender
catalog.description: This course is an introduction to the study of gender. The focus is on the investigation of psychological gender in its diversity rather than biological sex. Using theory, research, and our own experiences, we will examine how gender shapes our sense of self, relationships, culture, history, social structures, opportunities, power, marginalization, and discrimination.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Quantitative Methods In Psychology
catalog.description: Introduction to the use, calculation, reporting, and interpretation of descriptive and elementary inferential statistical techniques in psychological science.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better; and MATH 110 or MATH 116 or STAT 115 or MOTRMATH 110 or higher level math; or MyMathTest College Algebra Score of 70 or higher.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Ethnic and Diversity Perspectives in Psychology
catalog.description: The theory, methods, and content of psychology relevant to the interests and needs of ethnic groups and other diverse identities, as well as their contributions to the field of psychology.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Theory and Methods of Personality
catalog.description: The development, organization, dynamics and determinants of personality. May not be taken for graduate credit.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Motivation and Emotion
catalog.description: A review of the principles of both human and animal motivation from classical drive, behavioral, and cognitive perspectives. May not be taken for graduate credit.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Cognitive Psychology
catalog.description: Historical foundations and current state of knowledge regarding human information processing and the mental processes that underlie human behavior.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Biological Psychology
catalog.description: Introduction to the neural bases of human behavior, including movement, sleep and wakefulness, sensation and perception, and emotion.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Cognitive Neuroscience
catalog.description: Introduction to the study of human cognitive neuroscience. Topics under discussion include methods of investigation in human neuroscience, and their application to recent topics in affective, clinical, and social neuroscience.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Psychological Perspectives on Mental Health
catalog.description: This course is an introduction to psychological problems and disorders. It includes a presentation of the many biopsychosocial influences on psychological health and an overview of current treatment modalities. Students will also learn about factors influencing positive mental health. May not be taken for graduate credit.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: The Psychology Of Aging
catalog.description: Survey of concepts, theory, and methods in the psychology of aging, including biological and social influences on behavior.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a grade of C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
catalog.description: This course covers training and expertise that qualify one to practice clinical psychology. Topics addressed include the scientific foundation of clinical psychology, use of clinical assessments and interventions, and ethical guidelines outlined by the American Psychological Association.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Introduction to School Counseling
catalog.description: This course is as an introduction to the school counseling profession with a focus on topics relevant to school counseling practice, including the school counselor’s role and specific strategies and resources for practical application and implementation.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Offered as the result of student demand, specialized faculty interests, or the availability of a visiting expert in a field related to psychology.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a grade of C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Field Practicum
catalog.description: Provides supervised human services experience in an external community agency or organization that addresses human or social problems.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Directed Individual Research
catalog.description: Students work on an individual research project under the supervision of a departmental faculty member.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a grade of C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Psychology Research Externship
catalog.description: Provides supervised research experience in an external community agency or organization that examines basic or applied research questions.
catalog.prerequisites: PSYCH 210 with a C- or better.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Introduction to Health Service Psychology
catalog.description: This course assists new doctoral students in their orientation to UMKC, the Department of Psychology and Counseling, and the field of Health Service Psychology. It also addresses psychologists’ roles, functions, and other responsibilities, including ethics.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Cognitive Psychology
catalog.description: An advanced study in the intersection of cognition and emotion, focusing on the topics of attention, memory, and executive function, and how these abilities influence and are influenced by emotional processes and by individual difference variables such as health, mental health, age, gender, and ethnicity.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Intellectual And Cognitive Assessment
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide students with a foundation in the use of intellectual and cognitive assessment instruments in assessment practice. The course covers theoretical issues pertinent to intellectual and cognitive assessment, as well as foundational assessment skills including administration, scoring, interpretation, and communication of results for evidence-based intellectual and cognitive assessment measures.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Assessment Methods in Personality
catalog.description: This course is designed to help students develop knowledge and skills related to the selection, administration, and interpretation of some representative objective personality assessment instruments used in counseling/clinical settings. Students will also learn to integrate data obtained from an assessment battery to write comprehensive psychological reports.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Advanced Systems And History Of Psychology
catalog.description: In depth review of the major theoretical systems of psychology in terms of historical assumptions, methodologies and developments with the goal of enabling the student to better evaluate current theories and assumptions in psychology.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Quantitative Analysis I: Regression And Analysis Of Variance
catalog.description: This graduate level statistics course for students in education and the behavioral sciences provides a strong conceptual understanding of two major statistical procedures with the context of the general linear model: multiple regression and numerous analysis of variance (ANOVA) models. Students will learn to select appropriate statistical techniques, test the assumptions of the techniques, analyze data using statistical software, and report the results of their analyses in the format of the American Psychological Association.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Quantitative Analysis II: Advanced Topics In Regression And Multivariate Data Analysis
catalog.description: This graduate level statistics course for students in the behavioral sciences and education provides a strong conceptual understanding of advanced topics in regression (e.g., interaction effects, logistic regression), mediation analysis, and various multivariate techniques (e.g., MANOVA, discriminant analysis). Students will complete a series of data-based activities that allow them to demonstrate their skills in analysis, reporting and interpretation of findings.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Advanced Biopsychology
catalog.description: This course assumes that the student has mastered the basics of biopsychology, and deals with this topic in greater depth and scope than PSYCH 418 . It will begin with a brief review and update of basic materials of neuroanatomy, neuronal conduction, and synaptic transmission but will quickly turn to an emphasis on biological influences on human psychology, in particular those biological factors that are of practical significance in the lives of patient and non-patient populations.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Advanced Social Psychology
catalog.description: The study of the individual in a social context. How social structure and interaction influence the behavior of an individual. Several contemporary systematic positions will be compared.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Advanced Developmental Science Across the Lifespan
catalog.description: This course introduces students to the theories and research of biological, cognitive, social, and personality development across the lifespan, within the multiple layers of social-cultural context of people's lives.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Development And Evaluation Of Assessment Tools
catalog.description: This survey course examines test theories, construction, and measurement theories. Within the context of a variety of conceptual frameworks and examples, students become knowledgeable about the various purposes, approaches, and computer software tools for measurement.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Professional Issues And Ethics In Psychology
catalog.description: This course is designed to introduce graduate students to the ethical standards and contemporary issues affecting professional conduct in the field of psychology. The topics covered all revolve around ethical conduct in practice and research, as well as the decision-making foundations for resolving ethical issues. In addition to ethical standards, legal issues affecting professional practice will be covered in detail.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Supervision and Consultation in Health Service Psychology
catalog.description: This course covers theory and research on community, mental health, organizational, and agency consultation, as well as theory and research on clinical supervision. Entry, process, outcome, and ethical issues surrounding each model of intervention will be explored. Each student will be expected to conduct and report on a consultation project.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Directed Readings In Psychology
catalog.description: Intensive readings in areas of joint interest to the enrolled student and the cooperating faculty.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Structural Equation Modeling
catalog.description: Students will learn core techniques in structural equation modeling, including path analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, structural regression models; and be introduced to advanced topics such as multi-group SEM and latent growth models. There will be multiple lab sessions using appropriate computer applications.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Hierarchical Linear Models
catalog.description: Students will be introduced to hierarchical linear modeling techniques. Foundational topics include the rationale for using hierarchical linear models, issues related to assumptions and data screening, and a dissection of the components of a two-level organizational effects hierarchical linear model. Special topics to be discussed include growth modeling, three-level models, dyadic models, and models with categorical outcome variables (i.e., hierarchical generalized linear models). Multiple class sessions will be devoted toward use of software to build and analyze these models.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Survey of Research in Health Service Psychology
catalog.description: This course is designed to provide a comprehensive overview of both the content and process of research in psychology and expose students to the research literature on a variety of different research methodologies. In addition, students will learn about the process of developing their own research. Students' approach to the course objectives should be consistent with the scientist-practitioner model and responsive to the cultural contexts of the research.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Evidence-Based Practice
catalog.description: This course focuses on learning theories and the fundamental elements of evidence-based practice in health service psychology, including how to evaluate empirically validated treatments for common psychological disorders and how to provide evidence-based treatments in the context of client characteristics, culture and preferences.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Clinical Practicum
catalog.description: Advanced supervised assessment and psychotherapy with individuals and groups in applied settings. Preregistration by application to instructor at least 60 days prior to the beginning of the semester. Approval by Psychology Director of Clinical training required.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Clinical Psychology Internship
catalog.description: Training occurs in an APA-accredited internship site and provides students with intensive, hands-on experience across a range of clinical activities, including assessment, diagnosis, intervention, consultation, and interdisciplinary collaboration. This course supports the integration of academic knowledge with clinical practice and serves as the final applied training before entry into professional practice or postdoctoral residency.

catalog.subject: PSYCH
catalog.title: Pre-Dissertation
catalog.description: Individualized research experiences to prepare students for the conduct of the dissertation.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Creating and Measuring Social Impact
catalog.description: Students learn alternative approaches for conceptualizing and understanding the performance, effectiveness, and impact of nonprofit organizations and the programs they operate, and employ the basic frameworks and processes by which social impact can be measured and evaluated. This includes the use of logic models and theories of change to inform the design, operation, and evaluation of programs, with specific attention to data-based analytic approaches to impact assessment.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Leading and Managing Nonprofit Organizations
catalog.description: Examines the processes by which nonprofit charitable organizations and associations are governed, led, and managed, with particular attention to the work of the board, executives, and managers. Students learn a strategic framework by which to sustain and enhance the performance and impact of these nonprofit organizations. Among topics of special importance are the dimensions of governance, strategy and planning that are unique to nonprofit public service organizations, including stages of organization development, the planning and business model development associated with the financial management, human resource management, board leadership, ethical decision making, and organizational effectiveness and accountability.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Public Service Data Analytics
catalog.description: This course focuses on research methods, data analysis, and statistics in relation to public, nonprofit, and health administration issues and concerns. One of the core functions of an executive is the ability to thoughtfully analyze information and make informed decisions. In this course, students will develop research and data analysis skills and the ability to critically evaluate statistics to make empirically- informed decisions in the workplace. Students will become familiar with research design, data management, descriptive and inferential statistics, and statistical modeling. Through an empirical project, students will learn how to conduct research and use quantitative information in decision making.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Urban Environmental Policy
catalog.description: Our cities are a first line of action in our efforts to sustain our environment. Many have begun to examine and address the connection between city problems and environmental and climate change, and the disproportionate impacts that they often have on the disadvantaged, yet these initiatives address only the surface of the issue. It is essential for scientists, public administrators, environmentalists, and policy thinkers to pay greater attention to the environmental challenges of our cities. Students examine and assess the challenge of understanding, developing and implementing coherent environmental policy to address such challenges in urban communities.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Foundations of Public Service
catalog.description: This course provides students with advanced study of public and nonprofit organizations. The focus throughout the course is on theories and practice of public service, performance metrics and outcomes, and leadership.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Leadership, Change and Social Impact
catalog.description: The two core purposes of this course are for students to learn about effective and ethical leadership, and for students to understand and develop their own capacity for leadership. The course is organized around three general themes: 1) leadership as relations with subordinates, including issues of work motivation; 2) leadership as lateral relations, including organizational politics and conflict management and resolution; and 3) leadership as influence in the organization's environment.
catalog.prerequisites: Sophomore standing; BBA student with declared Nonprofit Management emphasis area.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Special Topics
catalog.description: Special topics in public administration.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Nonprofit Fundraising and Development
catalog.description: Examines the processes and functions by which nonprofit organizations plan, organize, implement and evaluate the work of fundraising and development to secure the financial resources needed to support and sustain their programs and activities. Students gain an understanding of and practical experience in employing the basic approaches and techniques used by nonprofits to raise and deploy philanthropic resources, including annual and multi-year giving programs, major gift solicitation, planned giving initiatives, capital campaigns, and prospect research and proposal writing.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Nonprofit Organizations in Context
catalog.description: Student in this course will investigate nonprofit organizations, an under-examined sector of our society. We will analyze the theoretical reasons for the existence of this sector, its empirical trends, and the significant challenges that nonprofits face.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Internship: Public Administration
catalog.description: An opportunity for students to integrate their academic studies via employment with a business/organization in the community. Internship coursework is evaluated on a credit/no credit basis.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Special Topics In Public Administration
catalog.description: Study and research in areas of special interest under individual faculty direction.

catalog.subject: PUB-ADM
catalog.title: Public Service Data Analytics
catalog.description: This course focuses on research methods, data analysis, and statistics in relation to public, private nonprofit, and health administration issues and concerns. In this course, students will develop research and data analysis skills and the ability to critically evaluate statistics to make empirically-informed decisions in the workplace.
