catalog.title: Seminar - Early Childhood
catalog.description: Supports the culminating student teaching experience and the submission of a final professional teaching portfolio. Student teachers analyze the effectiveness of the teaching strategies they are applying in their student teaching experiences, for their effectiveness in facilitating learning in classrooms, and adapt lessons and assessment for individual learners. Student teachers will work cooperatively with school personnel, the larger professional community, and families to meet students’ needs.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Practicum III - Early Childhood
catalog.description: This field experience is part of Block 3, the third field experience within a four-block sequence. The overarching goal for this field experience is for teacher candidates to apply conceptual and theoretical knowledge to practice in identifying appropriate instructional strategies, planning instruction, and assessing learning. The emphasis is on understanding the relationships among instructional practices, learner characteristics, and learning outcomes.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Seminar - Science
catalog.description: Supports the culminating student teaching experience and the submission of a final professional teaching portfolio. Student teachers analyze the effectiveness of the teaching strategies they are applying in their student teaching experiences, for their effectiveness in facilitating learning in classrooms, and adapt lessons and assessment for individual learners. Student teachers will work cooperatively with school personnel, the larger professional community, and families to meet students’ needs.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Seminar - Social Science
catalog.description: Supports the culminating student teaching experience and the submission of a final professional teaching portfolio. Student teachers analyze the effectiveness of the teaching strategies they are applying in their student teaching experiences, for their effectiveness in facilitating learning in classrooms, and adapt lessons and assessment for individual learners. Student teachers will work cooperatively with school personnel, the larger professional community, and families to meet students’ needs.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Teaching Internship
catalog.description: Teacher candidates will work 3 to 5 days at the school site in which the candidate will complete the year-long teaching internship.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Urban Education Seminar VII
catalog.description: This seminar meets weekly for 2 hours and is led by a clinical professor who serves as a mentor for the students throughout their program. Students will work closely with mentor teachers in the application and integration of social justice and the elementary school curriculum. A critical analysis of current practices, teaching methods, materials and how social justice manifests in curriculum and instruction. Emphasis is on understanding cultural diversity and cultural influences on learning. Concepts of a classroom community, parental relations and democratic classroom processes will be addressed. Students will have opportunities to apply their learning to urban classrooms.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Legal and Ethical Aspects of Teaching
catalog.description: This course provides an introduction to landmark court cases, federal and state laws, and regulations that frame students’ and teachers’ rights and responsibilities and that provide guidance for ethical professional practices.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Cultural Diversity and Teaching English Language Learners
catalog.description: Foundational knowledge on teaching diverse populations and practical instructional approaches for meeting the needs of linguistically and culturally diverse learners. Emphasis on studying and applying instructional strategies that are appropriate for addressing the unique needs of children whose primary language may not be English.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Assessment and Data Literacy
catalog.description: Data collection and assessment strategies—including formative, summative, formal, and informal—to be used in developing student learning profiles, planning learning experiences, and monitoring student progress toward academic goals. Topics include the impact of assessment on equitable education for diverse learners, critical observation and questioning, basic qualitative and quantitative data analysis, working with data teams, collaboration/communication with families and other educational stakeholders, setting and monitoring learning goals, and the ethics of data collection and sharing.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Teaching and Learning with Technology
catalog.description: This course addresses the fundamentals of using technology in education and planning instruction to engage PK-12 students in technology-based problem solving and critical thinking. Topics within the course are informed by International Society for Technology in Education Standards (ISTE), InTASC Model Core Teaching Standards and Learning Progressions for Teachers 1.0, Missouri Teacher Standards and Quality Indicators, and Missouri Learning Standards.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Education of the Exceptional Child and Youth
catalog.description: Students will be introduced to identification and educational intervention strategies for educating exceptional children and adolescents in inclusive classroom situations. This course requires a 10-hour field experience.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Special Methods for Teaching Art
catalog.description: Students preparing to teach K12 Art read, reflect on, and practice the application of current research and instructional practice in art education for the K12 learner.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the Master of Arts in Teaching Program

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Special Methods for Teaching World Languages
catalog.description: This course stresses teaching methods, theory and practical application for K-12 standards-based World Languages instruction.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission to the Master of Arts in Teaching program

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Mathematics in the Elementary School I
catalog.description: Mathematics-specific pedagogy. Methods, techniques, tools and materials for the effective teaching of mathematics. Focus on the principles, methods, and materials of elementary school mathematics instruction and state curriculum in the context of diverse student backgrounds.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Student Teaching in Elementary School
catalog.description: Culminating experience in an elementary school (grades 1-6). Elementary majors must enroll in 9 credit hours and engage in an all-day, full semester placement in an elementary classroom. Hours for other programs using this field experience vary. Teacher candidates should seek advisor approval.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Practicum I - Middle and High School
catalog.description: The purpose of this field experience is to apply theoretical and practical knowledge gained in concurrent courses.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Practicum II - Middle and High School
catalog.description: The purpose of this field experience is to apply theoretical and practical knowledge gained in concurrent courses.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Practicum III - Middle and High School
catalog.description: The purpose of this field experience is to apply theoretical and practical knowledge gained in concurrent courses.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Mathematics in Elementary School II
catalog.description: Mathematics-specific pedagogy. Methods, techniques, tools and materials for the effective teaching of mathematics. Focuses on the principles, methods, and materials of elementary school mathematics instruction and state curriculum in the context of diverse student backgrounds and abilities, with a particular focus on interventions for students with special needs.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Analyzing Learning Environments in Urban Contexts
catalog.description: This course serves as the major vehicle for articulating a programmatic construction of classroom management as establishing productive learning environments, facilitating social interaction, and planning relevant and engaging learning experiences based upon deep knowledge of individual students’ contexts and cultures.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Special Methods of Teaching English in Middle and High Schools
catalog.description: This course stresses the skills, knowledge, and dispositions pertinent to teaching English Language Arts in middle schools and high schools.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Special Methods of Teaching Mathematics in Middle and High Schools
catalog.description: This course stresses the skills, knowledge, and dispositions pertinent to teaching mathematics in middle schools and high schools.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Special Methods of Teaching Science in Middle and High Schools
catalog.description: Provides an opportunity for future science teachers to refine their skills as science educators and at the same time to reflect upon the ways and whys of teaching science.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Special Methods of Teaching Social Science in Middle and High Schools
catalog.description: This course will assist teacher candidates in developing the knowledge, skills, and dispositions needed to design and enact powerful transformative social studies curricular experiences, to foster middle and secondary school students’ abilities to make informed, reasoned decisions and actions for the public good. Students will be introduced to powerful teaching practices, issues, and resources in secondary school social science.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Student Teaching in High School
catalog.description: Culminating experience in a high school (grades 9-12). Enrollment hours vary for teacher candidates in Music, Art, and Foreign Languages. Secondary majors in English, Mathematics, Science, and Social Science enroll for 9 semester credit hours.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Culturally Responsive Strategies for Teaching Diverse Learners
catalog.description: This course is designed to move students from cultural awareness to the application of culturally responsive practice. Specifically, this course will heighten students' understanding of cultural characteristics and their relationships to teaching and learning. Students will learn culturally responsive strategies and their enactment in instruction for diverse learners.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Observation, Assessment & Screening in Early Childhood Classrooms
catalog.description: This course is designed to identify developmentally appropriate ways to measure and evaluate child growth and development.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Student Teaching In Middle School
catalog.description: Culminating field experience in a middle school setting. Student teachers engage in an all-day, full semester placement in a middle school classroom. Middle School Education (English, Mathematics, Science, Social Science) majors must enroll in 9 credit hours. Hours for other programs using this field experience vary. Teacher candidates should seek advisor approval.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Middle School Philosophy and Organization
catalog.description: This course offers teacher candidates an overview of middle school goals, basic principles, and organizations. Topics include interdisciplinary teaming, flexible scheduling, exploratory and advisory programs, and other aspects of the organization within the context of middle school goals and practices.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Literacy Intervention across the Disciplines
catalog.description: Examination of research, policy, and effective practice of literacy intervention in middle and secondary disciplinary classrooms (i.e. English/language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies). Topics will include recognition of reading and writing difficulties, response-to-intervention (RTI), scaffolding instruction for grade level reading comprehension, metacognition, and culturally responsive literacy instruction.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Urban Education VI: Teaching Diverse Students
catalog.description: This interactive course will investigate and examine the principles of teaching diverse students and factors influencing effectiveness of instruction, including empowering African American males, teaching students from diverse populations and working with students with special needs. Some of the class sessions will be taught electronically and work will be submitted electronically.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission into the Institute of Urban Education.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Teaching Internship
catalog.description: Teacher candidates will work 3 to 5 days at the school site in which the candidate will complete the year-long teaching internship.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Urban Education Seminar VII
catalog.description: This seminar meets weekly for 2 hours and is led by a clinical professor who serves as a mentor for the students throughout their program. Students will work closely with mentor teachers in the application and integration of social justice and the elementary school curriculum. A critical analysis of current practices, teaching methods, materials and how social justice manifests in curriculum and instruction. Emphasis is on understanding cultural diversity and cultural influences on learning. Concepts of a classroom community, parental relations and democratic classroom processes will be addressed. Students will have opportunities to apply their learning to urban classrooms.
catalog.prerequisites: Admission into the Institute for Urban Education.

catalog.subject: TCH-ED
catalog.title: Capstone
catalog.description: This seminar is designed to complement the student teaching experience through the discussion and analysis of school-based issues. It is intended to help further develop a reflective, critical and analytical approach to pedagogical decision making through supportive collaboration.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Topical Studies In Theatre Practice
catalog.description: (A, B, C, D) This course provides students with an opportunity to explore special offerings in theatre practice. Different sections of the course may be repeated.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction To Acting for Non-Majors
catalog.description: An introductory course to acquaint the non-major student with the process of acting through relaxation and improvisational exercise.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Acting for the Opera
catalog.description: Students receive basic foundation of acting technique. Students will demonstrate the ability to apply their tools in practice and articulate their process throughout the semester. The course is designed for the coordination of music and acting with particular emphasis on training the singing actor.
catalog.prerequisites: Bachelor of Music: Music Performance-Voice Option major.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction to Theatre Practice: Presence, Stories, and Connection
catalog.description: This course is designed for students who are entering the UMKC Conservatory as Theatre majors, to support the creation of community, explore the art of presence through storytelling, and connect incoming students more deeply with each other and with the vibrant UMKC and Kansas City artistic communities.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Acting I
catalog.description: This course introduces foundational acting techniques to develop students' ability to create authentic and engaging performances. Students will explore acting principles, character development, ensemble collaboration, and improvisation while building physical and vocal expressiveness. Through warm-ups, games, ensemble work, analysis and live performances, the course aims to develop students’ awareness, confidence, spontaneity, and understanding of foundational acting techniques.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be Theatre BA, Theatre Minor, Integrated Arts Minor, or Musical Theatre Certificate student

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction To Technical Production
catalog.description: An introduction to the technical production process with emphasis on production organization, planning and scenic construction techniques. Required laboratory work.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction to Costume Technology
catalog.description: This introductory course explores the technical skills and craftsmanship essential for creating theatrical costumes. Students will learn techniques in sewing and pattern drafting. Through hands-on projects, students will gain practical experience in costume assembly, alteration, and maintenance. The course prepares students for further study in costume design and production within the performing arts.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction to Lighting and Sound Technology
catalog.description: An introduction to the basic principles and techniques of lighting and sound design and technology in the Theatre.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Oral Interpretation Of Literature
catalog.description: Principles of interpretation, analysis and oral reading of prose and poetry. Emphasis upon platform performance: body language, vocal control and performance techniques.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Making Theatre
catalog.description: A semester-long exploration of the creative processes incorporated for the making of live theatrical entertainment. The disciplines of collaboration, conceptualization, and communication as fundamental to potentially successful events are studied, discussed and evaluated throughout this course.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre Practicum
catalog.description: The course requires involvement with productions in the Conservatory. Students will learn the responsibilities and processes of preparing and executing a live theatrical production. Depending on specialty, students will work backstage, in one of the studios, or in some other capacity as defined and agreed upon by the area coordinator.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Script Analysis
catalog.description: The class focuses on reading a script theatrically with a view to mounting a coherent production. Through careful, intensive reading of a variety of plays students study form, structure, genre, character, language, theme, and action as components of a text that provide the theatre artist with the tools for the creation a theatrical production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction To Design For The Theater
catalog.description: An introduction to aesthetics and design for the theater in the areas of scenery, costume, lighting and sound. The emphasis is upon the theory, vocabulary, form, style, historical influences and process in each area. Attendance at theater productions is required. Course is taught by design faculty from each area.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Voice for the Actor
catalog.description: Training in voice and articulation and the techniques of adaptation to the needs of the artist-performer in the theatre: exercises to free the voice, develop effective breathing, tone production, articulation, flexibility of vocal production, and projection.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Movement For Actors
catalog.description: Basic movement training including relaxation and alignment techniques, exercises to increase physical facility and skills to enhance rhythmic coordination and physical characterization.
catalog.prerequisites: THEA 110 -or- THEA 101; this course is for Theatre BA, Theatre Minor, Integrated Arts Minor, and Musical Theatre Certificate students

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre: Production/Performance Role
catalog.description: THEATRE 301 provides students the opportunity to get course credit for their involvement in UMKC Conservatory productions, either in performance or through a major design or technology assignment. This course challenges students to build and maintain professional approaches to their work in production.
catalog.prerequisites: Students must FIRST be cast in a show or assigned a major production role to enroll in this course.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Acting II
catalog.description: Course builds on the Acting I content to introduce students to textual analysis, in-depth characterization, and building a role.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Scene Design
catalog.description: Introduces the mechanics of layout: perspective, basic drafting techniques, front elevation and floorplan execution. Second half of the semester emphasizes scenic design as an art form. Recommended Preparation: THEATRE 113 and THEATRE 311.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Acting III
catalog.description: Course builds on the Acting I and Acting II content to introduce students to deeper studies of period styles of acting, including Ancient Greek, Shakespearean, Restoration, and Neoclassical forms.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History of Costuming I
catalog.description: The study of the history of European costume, with emphasis on the social and economic ramifications of costuming through the ages.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Makeup
catalog.description: Lecture and laboratory work in the fundamentals of makeup for the stage.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre History I
catalog.description: Development of theatre art, including the physical stage, technical production elements, dramatic literature, and audience behavior from primitive origins to the 18th century.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theater History II
catalog.description: Development of theater art, including the physical stage, technical production elements, dramatic literature, and audience behavior from the 18th century to the present.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History of Costuming II
catalog.description: The study of the history of Non-European costume, with emphasis on the social and economic ramifications of costuming through the ages.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Lighting
catalog.description: Stage Lighting is the study of light as a design element. Students will learn the foundation of lighting design theory, technical methods, and general theatrical procedure through lectures, laboratory and crew work. Theatrical genres will vary by semester.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Lighting Technology
catalog.description: This course is a comprehensive study of contemporary technical equipment and its usage to actualize lighting design. Areas of emphasis include photometric, color and color theory, lighting control systems, lighting control operations, cueing techniques, data control of intelligent lighting equipment, lighting fixtures, dimming system, hand drafted light plot standards, CAD light plot drafting, lighting specific software programs, video and image projections, and optical special effects. Theatrical genres will vary by semester.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Projection Design
catalog.description: This course in projection design for the performing arts will give students an overview of the discipline and introduce students to ideas and technologies used in this field. Through the three weekend sessions, students will learn the practical applications of projection design and the techniques of projection controls. Recommended preparation: basic, fundamental knowledge of computers and basic, fundamental knowledge of theatre designs.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Management I
catalog.description: A functional analysis of the duties and responsibilities of the stage manager, with particular reference to the organization and conducting of rehearsals and performances, professional practices and union requirements. Requires student to be an assistant to a stage manager on a University or an KC Rep production. The first of a two-semester requirement in stage management for theater majors.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Speech for the Actor
catalog.description: Continuation of THEATRE 295 - Voice for the Actor, focusing on articulation and adapting to the needs of the artist-performer in the theatre: exercises to free the voice, develop effective breathing, tone production, articulation, flexibility of vocal production, and projection. Course also introduces actors to vocal dialect work.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Special Problems In Theatre
catalog.description: (A-M) Research and/or production projects for advanced upperclass students. No more than three hours with any one instructor. (A) Acting; (B) Children's Theatre; (C) Costumes; (D) Scenic Design; (E) Directing; (F) History; (G) Lighting; (H) Playwriting; (I) Sound; (J) Stage Management; (K) Technical Production (L) Theatre Management; (M) Theory and Criticism.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Special Problems In Theatre: Scenic Design

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Special Problems In Theatre: Stage Management

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Special Problems In Theatre: Theatre Management

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Special Problems In Theatre: Theory And Criticism

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Beginning Directing
catalog.description: Theory and process of play production, including interpretation, composition, picturization, movement, rhythm, and character interpretation.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History of American Musical Theatre
catalog.description: A survey of trends in the American musical theatre from the 18th century to the present. This course includes material on creators and repertory in addition to the discussions of stylistic, analytical, social, aesthetic, and commercial aspects of musical theatre.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Rendering Techniques For The Theatre Designer I
catalog.description: Introduces the mechanics of handling black and white media to develop three-dimensional technique with an emphasis on observational training and object drawing.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Costume Design
catalog.description: The practice of the theatrical costume design, leading to the preparation of designs for production, and the execution of designs in actual costuming for the stage.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Playwriting I
catalog.description: Theory and practice of writing for the theatre with emphasis on the basic techniques.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Playwriting II
catalog.description: Theory and practice of writing for the theatre with emphasis on advanced techniques.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre Sound And Electronics
catalog.description: Study of electronic principles used in audio and control devices. Concentrates on applying knowledge to using the equipment employed in the theatre such as sound-effect systems, inter-communication equipment, and includes a special section on the creation of sound and music for theatre productions.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Management II
catalog.description: Practicum course in stage management. Requires stage management of a University production and/or assistant stage management of an KC Rep production and/or assistant stage management of a main stage University production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre Capstone
catalog.description: Each student plans and executes one significant project in the area of interest which demonstrates significant proficiency in one or more theatrical elements. Supervised by a member of the theatre faculty, the project incorporates research, documentation and a public exhibition.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Branding for Theatre Designers
catalog.description: This course is a single semester journey in the creation of a unique brand identity and marketing toolkit for the live entertainment designer. Through guided practice students will reflect on their visibility, develop their marketing toolkit, reframe presentation abilities, and prioritize brand strategy.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: MFA Costume Design Studio
catalog.description: Costume Design Studio is a semester-long exploration of the processes and techniques used for the development of character design within the context of live production. The disciplines of collaboration, conceptualization, and communication are studied, discussed, and evaluated throughout the course as fundamental components of potentially successful costume design. Theoretical design projects will emphasize problem-solving skills. In Class Studio Sessions, students will develop text and character analysis, research strategies, clear and efficient presentation skills, and graphic skills.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Digital Media for Costume Designers
catalog.description: This is a single semester course in digital illustration for costume designers in the live entertainment industry. Through guided practice and project work, participants will devise their digital workflow in Procreate for IPad, expanding upon their graphic skill set in the creation of highly evocative character design.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Textiles & Fabric Modification
catalog.description: This is a single semester course in textile principles and the basic methods by which fabric is manipulated. Through individual projects and guided practice students will build a foundational knowledge of textiles, handwork, and machine modifications.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Draping
catalog.description: This is a single semester course in the principles of draping garments for the live entertainment industry. Through guided practice, participants will build knowledge on the fundamentals of the drape method, expand upon their understanding of textiles, and incorporate the skills of draping with their pattern making methods.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Flat Patterning
catalog.description: Flat Patterning is a single semester exploration of the skills and techniques of flat pattern drafting as they pertain to the live entertainment industry. Through guided practice and project work, participants will enhance their understanding of garment planning and production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Tailoring & Menswear Production
catalog.description: Tailoring is a single semester exploration of the skill and techniques of classic bespoke tailoring. Though contemporary technologies offer a speedy alternative to the classic method, participants of this course will be instructed in the ways of the old master of Seville Row. Through guided practice, participants will pattern, construct, fit, and finish a men’s vest and trousers.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Mask Making & Craft Mediums
catalog.description: This is a single semester course focusing on the skills and techniques of mask making, casting and molding, and craft mediums as they pertain to the live entertainment industry. Through guided practice, participants will have the opportunity to expand on project and time management skills through the creation of three major mask projects.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Fabric Dyeing & Painting
catalog.description: This is a single semester course in the in the variety of techniques used in dyeing and painting fabric for the live entertainment industry. Through guided practice and project work, participants will explore methods of silk painting, color matching, and yardage dyeing using Union and Acid Dyes.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Wig Making & Styling
catalog.description: This is a single semester course in the principles of wig making and styling within the context of character design for live entertainment. Through guided practice students will learn to prepare and ventilate wigs and facial hair pieces, to style synthetic hair, and to plan and execute period styles.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Millinery
catalog.description: Millinery is a single semester exploration of the skill and techniques used in the creation of hats for the live entertainment industry. Through guided practice and project work, participants will enhance their understanding of hat making and the various materials utilized in its craft.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Stage Management Seminar
catalog.description: Students will work through the process and challenges of stage managing a production in today’s environment. The class is a combination of hands-on rehearsal and performance work, as well as in-person discussions on current topics of the industry and topics as they come up in the rehearsal hall and in the performance space.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be an MFA Design and Technology student in the Conservatory

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Stage Management: LORT
catalog.description: This course examines contacts with the League of Resident Theaters (LORT) alongside the history and the reasons behind many of the rules associated with LORT contracts. In addition, this course will investigate how to interpret these contracts, compare them to contracts with other unions, and apply them in real scenarios.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Stage Management: Dance and Cirque Performance
catalog.description: This course will investigate the technical and creative aspects of stage managing performances centered around dance, movement, and cirque productions.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Performance Studies: Auto-Cours
catalog.description: The course serves as an investigation into how Auto-Cours techniques enable individuals to successfully collaborate within a devising group. We also explore structures for creating dynamic, theatrical events.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Musical Theatre Vocal Training
catalog.description: This course covers components of proper vocal techniques through the study of a variety of repertoires from the Musical Theatre genre. Topics include vocal anatomy & health, onset, space, breathing, resonance, vowels, diction, sight-singing, lyric interpretation, solo & group singing, acting through song, stage presence, audition & rehearsal techniques.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Performance Studies: The Business of the Business
catalog.description: This course equips graduate acting students with the knowledge, tools, and professional practices necessary to build and sustain a career in the performing arts. Topics include marketing and branding, resumes and headshots, agents and casting, union membership, audition etiquette, financial literacy for artists, and how to develop a long-term career strategy.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Performance Studies: Voiceover for the Actor
catalog.description: This course explores the business and craft of professional voiceover work, including various styles of performance and the range and expectations of the industry.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Performance Studies: Acting for the Camera
catalog.description: A practical application of truthful acting techniques adapted to the unique demands of television and film.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Master Class: Graduate Stage Combat
catalog.description: This course introduces graduate acting students to the foundational techniques of stage combat with a focus on unarmed (hand-to-hand) combat and rapier & dagger. Emphasis is placed on safety, storytelling, physical precision, and partnering. Students will explore how physical conflict reveals character, raises dramatic stakes, and serves the text. The course culminates in a choreographed performance piece demonstrating proficiency in both styles.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre Collaboration
catalog.description: A course for M.F.A. students exploring the collaboration/ communication process in preparing a production. Must be elected by all students assigned to design, direct, technical direct or stage manage within the current or the following semester. Maximum of 8 hours applicable towards degree.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Voice Training
catalog.description: (A,B,C,D) Training for the speaking performance voice, development of skills in vocal dynamics, physical control, and relaxation for the actor; accent acquisition; heightened text; vocal extremes. Four semesters required for acting emphasis.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Movement
catalog.description: ( A, B, C, D ) Training in the basic principles underlying stage movement. Work leading to period dance styles, mime, fencing, tumbling, stage combat. Four semesters required for acting emphasis.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Movement
catalog.description: ( A, B, C, D ) Training in the basic principles underlying stage movement. Work leading to period dance styles, mime, fencing, tumbling, stage combat. Four semesters required for acting emphasis.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Movement
catalog.description: ( A, B, C, D ) Training in the basic principles underlying stage movement. Work leading to period dance styles, mime, fencing, tumbling, stage combat. Four semesters required for acting emphasis.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: French Drama And Theatre
catalog.description: Study of significant plays and production methods in France from medieval times to the present. Particular emphasis will be given to the plays of Moliere, Racine, and Corneille, and to internationally renowned contemporary directors.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: 19Th-Century Continental Theatre
catalog.description: Production of significant French, German, Russian, Spanish, and Scandinavian plays and playwriting of the 19th century. Particular emphasis will be given to plays representative of romanticism, realism, naturalism, fin-de-siecle decadence, and intensive study of production history.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: 20Th-Century Continental Theatre
catalog.description: Study of the production of significant plays of Continental Europe from Strindberg to the present. Dramatic literature will be related to artistic currents such as expressionism, surrealism, the absurd, and where applicable, to political currents.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Russian Drama And Theatre
catalog.description: Study of the production of Russian and Soviet plays with reference to the development of theatre art from the Christianization of Russia to contemporary post-Soviet drama.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History Of The American Theatre I
catalog.description: An exploration of the trends in and the development of the American theatre from Colonial times to 1900.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History Of The American Theatre II
catalog.description: An exploration of the trends in and the development of the American theatre for 1900 to the present.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History Of The English Stage I
catalog.description: The English stage and its arts, crafts and literature from the medieval cycles through the Restoration.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History Of The English Stage II
catalog.description: Development of English and Irish theatre art and dramatic literature from the 18th century to the present.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History of Design And Technology II
catalog.description: The study of period style and scenic, costume, lighting, and technical production practices from the 18th century to the present. The course will emphasize the application of research toward the presentation of period plays and contemporary production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Technical Production for The Practitioner
catalog.description: The course is an in-depth review of technologies in scenery, lighting and stage operations, expansion of that knowledge, and application of it to the individual class member's particular theatre. Classroom material is augmented by hands-on experience in a controlled laboratory situation. Students should have a prerequisite of a basic technical theatre course or considerable practical experience. This course can be repeated for credit.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Technical Production for The Practitioner
catalog.description: See course description for THEATRE 5516A .

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Stage Management I
catalog.description: A functional analysis of the responsibilities of the professional stage manager. Requires the student to be an assistant stage manager on a University or KC Rep production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Stage Management II
catalog.description: Practical course in stage management. Requires student to stage-manage or assistant stage-manage a production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Assistant Stage Management
catalog.description: This course develops a skill set for professional assistant stage managers. Class will discuss duties and paperwork and how to supplement the work of the stage manager.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Stage Management: Opera
catalog.description: Class covers duties of the opera stage manager, including how to follow an opera score.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Union Contracts for Actors and Stage Managers
catalog.description: Students study and discuss all the rules in the Equity Rule Book.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Production Management in Theatre
catalog.description: This course is a seminar on the duties, planning, negotiations, and problem solving techniques of the professional theatre production manager.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Individual Performance Studies
catalog.description: (A,B,C) Private instruction for the advanced student.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Sound Design
catalog.description: Professional Sound Design is a series of four courses constructed to develop the designer's skills from research and initial sound collection, into interpretation, collaboration and idea development, concluding with the production of finished designs for the MFA productions. Each section deals with problems of increasing complexity beginning with 'found' design material for early production and leading to indigenous designs created and layered for complex production support. The course may be taken once or twice for non-sound designers with the full cycle being required for the sound design emphasis.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Sound Design
catalog.description: Professional Sound Design is a series of four courses constructed to develop the designer's skills from research and initial sound collection, into interpretation, collaboration and idea development, concluding with the production of finished designs for the MFA productions. Each section deals with problems of increasing complexity beginning with 'found' design material for early production and leading to indigenous designs created and layered for complex production support. The course may be taken once or twice for non-sound designers with the full cycle being required for the sound design emphasis.

catalog.title: Professional Sound Design

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Rendering Techniques for the Theatre Designer I
catalog.description: Introduces the mechanics of handling black and white media to develop two and three-dimensional techniques with an emphasis on observational training and object drawing, as well as white model and/or maquette construction, materials and techniques.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Drafting for The Theatre
catalog.description: Practical laboratory course in drafting for the theatre encompassing floor plans, sections, designer's evaluations, front and rear elevations, working drawings, and problems in communicating design ideas.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Rendering Techniques for the Theatre Designer II
catalog.description: Continuation of Rendering Techniques with the introduction of color, pastels, watercolor and goauche. Skills are applied in developing projects for design in the theatre.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Costume Design
catalog.description: ( A, B, C, D ) The courses in Professional Costume Design are intended to develop the costume designer's skills in research, rendering and drawing. Each section will deal with specific problems of design, such as period, line, silhouette, color and texture. Specific problems in design from realistic to stylized productions will be worked on by the students. The course may be taken once or twice by non-costume designers with the full cycle being required for costume emphasis.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History of Fashion and Culture
catalog.description: This course is a survey of Western fashion from antiquity to the contemporary period, emphasizing the relationship between clothing and artistic, social, and political contexts. The course will be conducted through a variety of study methods including textbook readings, in-class discussion and critique, period research, and sketching.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Technical Studies In Costuming And Makeup
catalog.description: (A,B,C) Concentration in one or more of the arts and crafts necessary to costume design. Areas to be chosen from include: fabric dyeing and painting, millinery, wig design and construction, latex prosthetic, and decorative accessories for the stage. May be repeated up to six hours with content change and permission of instructor.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Scene Design Studio
catalog.description: Professional Scene Design Studio is a series of courses constructed to develop the designer's skills from research and initial sketches to finished renderings, models and working drawings. Each successive section deals with problems of increasing complexity beginning with one-set realistic productions through unit-settings, stylization and multiple setting problems. The course is taken each semester of the program.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: History of Design and Decor
catalog.description: This course provides an overview of the trends in architecture, painting, sculpture, furniture, and decorative motifs, examining multiple periods throughout history. This course is lecture-based with many quizzes and tests.
catalog.prerequisites: Must be MFA Design and Technology student

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Scene Painting
catalog.description: A practicum course in scene painting techniques and execution. Introduction to painting equipment and supplies, priming and preparation of surfaces and materials, standard techniques for painting ornament.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Scene Painting II
catalog.description: A practicum course in scene painting techniques with emphasis on painting interior drops, exterior landscapes and three-dimensional pieces.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Acting Techniques I
catalog.description: Theatre games, exercises, mask work, and some scene study to develop the first year acting/directing class into a training ensemble, instill a clear and uniform vocabulary, heighten awareness, and begin concentrated skill work. The semester will culminate in a class project.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Acting Techniques II
catalog.description: Continuation of THEATER 5545 with emphasis on the application of the first semester's work through scene study of contemporary plays and monologues.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Acting Techniques III
catalog.description: Concentration on non-naturalistic styles. Work on scenes from Shakespeare and other classical playwrights.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Acting Techniques Iv
catalog.description: Work on audition material and further scene work dealing with specific individual acting problems.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Master Class In Acting
catalog.description: (A,B,C,D) Class in advanced studies in acting. May be repeated for credit up to eight hours as content and guest artist change. Permission of instructor or head of area required. Required for third year graduate acting students in the fall semester and may be repeated subsequently as elective.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Rendering Techniques for the Theatre Designer III
catalog.description: Developing techniques for rendering in realistic settings: interiors, landscapes, fabric and furnishings.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Rendering Techniques for the Theatre Designer Iv
catalog.description: Developing techniques for rendering in non-realistic styles with the emphasis on imaginative designs, light and air, created textures, etc.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre History I
catalog.description: Development of theatre art-including dramatic literature, staging, and performance styles-from the beginning through the 17th century. This course also looks at Asian theatre forms. Students read approximately 20 plays.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre History II
catalog.description: Development of western theatre art-including dramatic literature, staging, and performance styles-from the 18th century to the present. Students will read approximately 24 plays.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Actor Practicum
catalog.description: A contemporary scene study class for actors. Actors test their acquired process skills with major emphasis placed on characterization.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Text Analysis I
catalog.description: Linear analysis of selected prose dramas with concentration on character delineation, images and motivation for actors and directors.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Text Analysis II
catalog.description: Continuation of THEATRE 5563 with emphasis on verse plays. Selected playwrights from the Greek and Elizabethan periods will be included along with modern verse dramatists.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Introduction To Professional Directing
catalog.description: The first part of the class is devoted to an intensive study of various and diverse concepts related to the dramatic experience by dramatists, critics, and directors. The class also examines current production methods and practices for today's functioning professional director. Systems related to stage management and actors are investigated.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Directing Practicum
catalog.description: This class will move from concept to production. Work will revolve around the presentation of production concept statements in which the director will select, organize and articulate the theatrical substance in support of his or her chosen concept. Intensive analysis will lead to the development of an image/metaphor for production. Term will include presentation of a full book justifying concept choices for scenic, costume, music and dance, and, finally, full production.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Seminar In Dramaturgy
catalog.description: Critical analysis of dramatic structure and techniques, with special reference to modern and contemporary drama.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Master Class in Directing
catalog.description: (A,B,C,D) Class in advanced studies in directing. May be repeated for credit up to eight hours as new material and guest artist change. Graduate students elect THEATRE 5569 .

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Lighting Design Studio
catalog.description: This graduate-level course is designed exclusively for MFA candidates in Lighting Design to engage with a broad range of topics that reflect the diversity of the field. Students will explore various styles, historical periods, theoretical frameworks, design concepts, venue types, career paths, and foundational practices in lighting design. The course operates on a rotating structure, with new subject matter introduced each semester.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Digital and Immersive Media Studio
catalog.description: This course examines various uses of digital and immersive media throughout the performance industry through a variety of lenses. Focus will be on the manipulation and creation of projected images, the fundamental use and control of automated projectors, and the design techniques required to interpret and materialize digital experiences in live performance, using state-of-the-art projection equipment and control consoles. This course will be repeated each semester throughout the graduate student’s time in the program, engaging with new materials and techniques in each Studio.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Projections Design I
catalog.description: This course examines the techniques of theatrical projection design. Focus will be on the manipulation of projected images, and the fundamental use and control of automated projectors. This hands-on laboratory class will instruct students in the use of state of the art projection equipment and control consoles.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Projections Design II
catalog.description: This class will teach students how to design projections. Students will learn the practical applications of projection design as well as the theoretical and critical thinking necessary to successfully complete a projection design assignment. This class will culminate with the presentation of an assigned projection design or a realized projection design.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Stage Lighting Technology
catalog.description: This is a graduate introductory course to lighting design and technology. The class will be divided into three sections: foundations of lighting design, electricity and equipment, and production lighting skills. Throughout the course students will explore these topics through lectures and hands on experiential learning.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Technical Production
catalog.description: Detailed study and experimentation with recent scenic materials, scenery construction, rigging systems, use of metal and special effects.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Theatre Regulations, Laws and Safety
catalog.description: Survey of fire, city and Equity codes, and insurance, liability, health rules and regulations related to theater operation. Union and legal contracts, philosophy and relations with theatre facilities and operations.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Property Construction
catalog.description: Construction techniques and materials used to make and modify set and hand properties and set dressing.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Advanced Materials
catalog.description: (A,B,C,D) The theatre technician and designer are dependent on a wide range of materials in the creation of their art. Each semester the student will pursue detailed study of a material area (i.e., wood, metal, plastics, textiles), the processes of its usage and its related process-products (i.e., adhesives, paints, dyes, etc.). Field trips and hands-on laboratory work are integral to the course.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Theatre Administration
catalog.description: Theories, problems and techniques preparing the student for effective interaction with professional theater administration, offering a foundation for potential theatre administrators as well as enrichment for students of directing, design, technical and stage management.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Graduate Technical Student Seminar
catalog.description: (A,B,C,D,E,F) Required in every semester for Design/Tech M.F.A. candidates choosing a technology emphasis. This continuing seminar course serves as a forum for all graduate technical students to analyze and discuss problems and solutions on current academic and KCRep productions. The course develops collaborative skills through the sharing of ideas and experiences. In addition, topics of general interest to the technician will be studied through guest lecturers and/or individual projects prepared by the faculty and students and presented to the class.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Seminar on Technical Production Management
catalog.description: Seminar involving shop organization, scheduling, purchasing, lending and borrowing, rentals, personnel, job description, organizing structure, etc. Emphasis upon organization and techniques for repertory theatre operation.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Advanced Technical Drafting
catalog.description: An intensive drafting course required for Design/Tech M.F.A. candidates with emphasis in technology. The course aims to equip the student to prepare clear shop working drawings from designer elevations. Topics include both conceptual planning techniques and developing mechanical drawing skills. One hour lecture, four lab hours, and extensive outside preparation.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Structural Design for the Stage
catalog.description: A course in the structural design of scenic elements. The student learns to work within the visual restrictions imposed by the designer to build structures that will bear given load requirements with a minimum of deflection. Basic engineering and load analysis principles are studied and applied in the design procedure to find the best possible solutions in terms of strength, weight, safety and cost.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Structural Design for the Stage II
catalog.description: This course is designed to give an introduction to the physics behind structural design and to guide the student through the process of designing safe, effective structural scenery for the theatre.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Directed Graduate Studies
catalog.description: Individual projects on the graduate level. No more than three hours with any one instructor. Only one 590 each semester.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Directed Graduate Studies: Theory And Criticism

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Seminar on Stage Management Practice
catalog.description: MFA student stage managers meet one hour a week with the Production Manager of both Kansas City Repertory Theatre and Department of Theatre (and head of stage management training), to discuss current management problems and solutions for productions in progress. The seventeen productions mounted each year by the Department and the Rep will be examined. Students will become aware of problem solving procedures in both the professional and the academic theatre.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Repertory Theatre: Internship
catalog.description: Assignments available in the following areas: directing, design, carpentry, lighting, costume, props, acting, stage management. Technical interns will be assigned by the appropriate heads of those areas. Acting interns may understudy and/or play roles with the Kansas City Repertory Theatre on the Spencer stage or in showcase productions. Also, interns will have some responsibility in technical areas such as change-over, props, costume, running crew, and stage management. Directing interns may assist director or assistant stage manager.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Research And Performance
catalog.description: Primarily for the M.F.A. student. Permission of the graduate faculty.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: MFA Capstone
catalog.description: Course serves as the culmination of the MFA student’s coursework, as it relates to their individual area of study in Theatre: Acting or Design/Technology. Students will synthesize coursework into a final presentation, including but not limited to a performance or portfolio review.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Repertory Theatre: Residency
catalog.description: The residency consists of authorized participation with the Kansas City Repertory Theatre, the Department of Theatre, or an approved outside professional company, and is arranged under departmental advisement, with the chairman of the department, and in consultation with the artistic director of KCRep. The assignment will be determined by matching interest and degree emphasis with available production assignments.

catalog.subject: THEATRE
catalog.title: Professional Theatre Partnership
catalog.description: This course partners 3rd year MFA students with local professional theatres to further their training in production roles, based on their area of study.

catalog.subject: UNIV
catalog.title: Academic Development
catalog.description: This course is designed to help students further develop needed critical thinking and academic skills. Students will have the opportunity to analyze individual learning behavior, and to learn, adopt, and apply critical thinking methods and academic skills that promote success in college.

catalog.subject: UNIV
catalog.title: Self and Major Exploration
catalog.description: The goal of this course is to provide students in their first semester of college assistance in understanding themselves and their academic options as they clarify their educational and career goals. UNIV 101 is required for Exploratory majors.

catalog.subject: UNIV
catalog.title: Career and Major Planning
catalog.description: The goal of this course is to provide assistance career/major exploration in order for students who have not declared their majors to make purposeful decisions about academic plans and career goals while fostering academic success. UNIV 102 is required for new transfer or transitioning UMKC students and for students having completed First Semester Experience in the previous term.

catalog.subject: UNIV
catalog.title: Next Steps in Career & Major Exploration
catalog.description: Designed to actively engage students in their educational and career-planning process by exploring factors that influence personal decision-making. While the course is practical and applied, it also addresses the broader view of work in our lives. The course will include discussion of factors that impact major and career decision-making in order to empower students to make an appropriate decision.

catalog.subject: UNIV
catalog.title: Peer Leadership
catalog.description: Designed for the study and practical application of leadership skills that will benefit Peer Leaders working with courses/laboratory instructors and students. Open to Peer Leaders only. May be repeated for a total of 3 hours. Course to be utilized by multiple academic units to support training efforts.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: GIS For Urban Planning
catalog.description: This introductory level GIS course is designed to expose planning students to Geographical Information Systems (GIS). Students will learn basic concepts and theories of GIS and applications of GIS software with hands-on experience. Students will also learn how to search for demographic, socio-economic, land use, transportation, and geospatial data, and how to use such data for their academic research and professional planning work with GIS. Students will apply GIS to the multiple scales of planning work.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Introduction to Digital Planning Methods
catalog.description: This Urban Planning + Design studio course will introduce methods for analyzing data, visualizing plans, and developing graphic explanations of designs and plans.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Visual Communication for Urban Design
catalog.description: This course introduces visual communication techniques used in professional city planning and urban design.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: History Of Planning And Urban Design
catalog.description: An overview of planning history with an emphasis on the 19th and 20th centuries. The historic framework will include urban history, the rise and development of urban planning, urban design, and social theory and how these areas have affected the shape of our cities.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Land Use Planning
catalog.description: This course explores the basic principles of plan making, land use development and regulation. Students are introduced to contemporary planning and policy issues. Including land use conflicts and alternative models for sustainable planning, design and management. Students will learn how to develop a land use plan using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and other design tools. An introductory GIS course ( UPD 203 ) is highly recommended.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Quantitative Planning Methods And Techniques
catalog.description: Statistical analysis and other analytic techniques of data gathering. Data and problems framed from complex, real world situations. Competence in firsthand research; survey design; case study method; data gathering methods such as observation, open-ended interviewing and questionnaires.
catalog.prerequisites: MATH 110 or higher; or MyMathTest College Algebra Score of 70 or higher, or ACT MATH sub-score of 28 or higher, or SAT MATH sub-score of 660 or higher.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning And Design Studio I
catalog.description: This Urban Planning + Design studio course will introduce methods for analyzing urban spaces at the site and neighborhood level. Students will actively solve problems related to the physical planning of cities and communities while continuing to develop abilities in methods of written, oral and graphic presentation.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning And Design Studio II
catalog.description: Studio instruction in urban planning and design focusing on the synthesis of land use analyses, regulatory reviews, urban design issues, and public participation facilitation. Continued instruction in techniques for visually presenting planning and design ideas.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning Theory And Practice
catalog.description: This course examines contemporary urban planning and design practice. Theories about planning practice and related case studies will be the basis of this course. Topics covered will include the definition of urban planning, the idea of the 'public realm,' planning/design expertise and the rational model, the role of diversity, public participation, communicative planning, advocacy and equity planning, ethics comprehensiveness and the limits of planning. The course will include assignments that will build student's ability to write quick and analytical assessments, often required in planning practice. Students will be required to attend public planning forums in and around the region.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Environmental Sustainability
catalog.description: This course will introduce the concept of sustainability and review how sustainability might work at the individual, neighborhood, state, nation and global scales. Students will participate in some form of community engagement on sustainability as well as reflect upon how their own practices impact the environment. Counts toward A&S Interdisciplinary 'Cluster course.' Key course in sustainability minor.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Neighborhood And Community Development
catalog.description: Course provides a comprehensive introduction to the field of community development and neighborhood planning. The development of theoretical models that explain neighborhood change and history in the U.S. will serve as the basis. Issues explored include: community organizing, social movements, federal and state policies, and the role of planning organizations and community development corporations in neighborhood revitalization.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Advanced GIS For Urban Planning
catalog.description: This advanced level GIS course is designed to expose students to high level GIS techniques and geospatial analyses in urban planning. Students will learn advanced theories and geographic information tools with hands-on experiences. Students will have an opportunity to apply their knowledge and skills in GIS to a real world planning project in class.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: GIS for Urban Planning
catalog.description: The introductory level GIS course is designed to expose graduate students to Geographical Information Systems (GIS). Students will learn basic concepts and theories of GIS and application of GIS software with hands-on experience. Students will also learn how to search for demographic, socio-economic, land use, transportation, and geospatial data.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning and Design Studio III
catalog.description: Instruction in problem analysis and plan development for defined urban or suburban location with multiple constituencies.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Professional Practice I
catalog.description: A seminar preparing students for professional practice in urban planning + design including the preparation of a professional resume and portfolio.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning and Design Studio IV
catalog.description: Capstone course for Urban Planning and Design students to engage in a real-world planning project. Students demonstrate planning knowledge and research capacity, and experience professional practice environments with a client.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Professional Practice II
catalog.description: A continuation of professional practice seminar addressing issues of professional writing in Urban Planning and Design practice.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Transportation Planning
catalog.description: The course provides fundamental theories, methods, and contemporary issues in transportation planning. The topics covered in this course include the transportation planning process, transportation systems, travel demand analysis, and policy issues such as the linkage between land use and transportation, urban transportation finance, social and environmental justice, transportation and environmental impacts, and traffic congestion.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning For Historic Preservation
catalog.description: The course provides a survey of major issues in the field of historic preservation and heritage studies from a planning perspective. Will focus primarily on the built environment of the United States, as well as world heritage sites and international perspectives. The course will include the urban planning techniques used for preserving historic buildings, neighborhood and districts, as well as some of the landmark legal decisions and legislation that have shaped heritage preservation practice in the U.S. Recommended Preparation: UPD 260 .

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Urban Environment Planning And Design
catalog.description: The built environment does not exist in a vacuum. Cities operate within broad ecological processes. Effective environmental planning can protect important natural resources while providing for a higher quality of life for urban residents. As a survey course in a subfield of urban planning, this course introduces students to environment planning approaches and techniques.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Natural Hazards and Disaster Planning
catalog.description: This course provides an introduction to emergency management planning and preparedness.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Planning Law And Practice
catalog.description: Introduction to legal procedures basic to urban planning; including legal, constitutional, legislative, and administrative concepts, controls, and land-use regulations.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Urban Redevelopment
catalog.description: Contemporary issues of urban redevelopment, with an emphasis on American cities, will be examined. Redevelopment processes recently completed or underway in the greater Kansas City region will be the subject of a case study and a theoretical review by each student.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: American Housing
catalog.description: Students will explore housing in cultural, design, and historical terms and examine contemporary American housing policy.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Urban Planning Internship
catalog.description: Urban planning work experience off-campus with an approved professional, Government, or non-profit agency sponsor. A contract specifying the expected product of the internship is required between the student, agency, and faculty coordinator.

catalog.title: Directed Studies In Urban Planning
catalog.description: Intensive reading and/or research in an area selected by the student in consultation with the instructor.

catalog.description: Advanced independent research and analysis in urban planning. Topics and methods used in research, to be established by student and academic supervisor prior to enrollment.

catalog.description: The course provides a survey of the history of urban planning and design with emphasis on the nineteenth and twentieth centuries in the United States. The course also teaches basic historic research methods.

catalog.description: This course introduces graduate students to quantitative methods in urban planning analysis. Topics include relating built form to function, demographic forecasting, economic impact analysis, trip generation, and housing market dynamics.

catalog.description: Exploration of contemporary planning theory and practice, including planning knowledge, skills, values, and ethics.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Historic Preservation Studio

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Natural Hazards and Disaster Planning
catalog.description: Presents the field of emergency management including history, hazard types, uncertainty, mitigation, preparedness, response, recovery and global perspectives..

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Advanced GIS for Urban Planning
catalog.description: This advanced level GIS course is designed to expose graduate students to high level GIS techniques and geospatial analysis in the urban planning context. Students will learn data management skills in GIS and advanced geoprocessing tools with hand-on experiences. Students will also have an opportunity to work on a real world GIS project as part of course requirements.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Transportation Planning
catalog.description: This course provides fundamental theories, methods, and contemporary issues in transportation planning. The topics covered in this course include the transportation planning process, transportation systems, travel demand analysis, and policy issues such as the linkage between land use and transportation and environmental impacts, and traffic congestion.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Introduction to Historic Preservation
catalog.description: The course introduces the history and theory of historic preservation through a survey of major issues in the field from a planning perspective. The course focuses on preservation through cultural, social, historical, legal, policy, and economic lenses, primarily in the United States.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: History of the Built Environment
catalog.description: Survey of the built environment concentrating on nineteenth and twentieth century design in the United States.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Historic Preservation Methods
catalog.description: Exploration of historic preservation methods, including survey, documentation, policy, and management approaches used in practice.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Urban Environmental Planning
catalog.description: Urban environmental planning examines ecological change due to urbanization. It looks at ways to measure and demonstrate ecological change at the site, neighborhood, and regional scales. Students incorporate environmental ideas and policies into plans developed for a client.

catalog.subject: UPD
catalog.title: Urban Redevelopment
catalog.description: This course examines techniques of urban redevelopment within urban planning and real estate. Graduate students learn about the development process, real estate markets, techniques of development finance and local policy approaches to urban redevelopment incentives.

catalog.title: American Housing
catalog.description: Students will explore housing in cultural, design, and historical terms and examine contemporary American housing policy.

catalog.title: Vocal Coaching: Voice Recital Preparation
catalog.description: The purpose of vocal coaching is to aid singers in refining their performance skills in terms of musical style, nuance, language, diction, and character. It is intended to amplify the singer’s understanding of the many aspects of performance including musical shaping, dynamic contrasts, poetic/textual architecture, traditional approaches to literature of various periods and styles, and appropriate performance practices related to voice recitals and/or the operatic stage. In addition, singers will develop additional skills in working with a collaborative pianist and explore appropriate expectations when working with conductors/stage directors.
